**眾教會。**從特殊的意義上說，給以弗所教會的應許也屬於使徒時代由以弗所教會所代表的“眾教會。” 雖然這個應許特別適合於他們，但也適用於各世代的信徒（見 啟 1:11 註釋）。
**凡有耳的。**就是聽從所賜勸勉的人（見啟 1:3 註釋；參賽 6:9, 10 ；太 11:15 註釋）。這句話伴隨著給七教會中每一個教會的應許。
**聽。**原文暗示聽的人會按理解去做（參徒 9:4 註釋）。 聽見上帝的話，卻不照著去生活，就毫無意義的（見太 19:21–27 註釋）。
**得勝。**原文動詞形式暗示“持續的勝利” 。在《啟示錄》中，“得勝”是一個經常出現的話題。《啟示錄》 的諸多應許對於上帝各世代受逼迫的兒女來說特別寶貴。但上文（第 2–6 節）暗示這裡的勝利是特指戰勝那些誘惑信徒追求世俗知識的假使徒和假教師。勝利的獎賞是吃生命樹的果子，這是多麼合適啊！
**樂園。**見路 23:43 註釋。伊甸園曾是地上的“樂園。” 伊甸圓在地上恢復之後（見 《先祖與先知》 第62頁；;《善惡之爭》第646, 648頁），地球將再度成為“樂園。”
關於給以弗所教會的信息適用於歷史上某一特定時期，見本章補充註釋。關於該信息應用於約翰時代的以弗所教會，見啟 1:11 註釋。
**中。**就像在伊甸園中（創 2:9）。樹的位置表明了它在上帝完美世界的計劃中所佔的重要地位。
**生命樹。**見創 2:9 ；啟 22:2 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第589頁；《教育論》第302頁；《早期著作》第21，77頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第91頁；《服務真詮》第449頁；《先祖與先知》第62頁；《證言》卷六第76頁；《證言》卷八第289頁。

28.en: **Morning star.** That is, Christ Himself (see Rev. 22:16; cf. 2 Peter 1:19).
28.zh:
我又要把晨星賜給他。

晨星.就是基督自己（見 啟 22:16 註釋；參 彼後 1:19）。

12.en:
**Angel.** See on ch. 1:20.
**Pergamos.** Or, Pergamum. This city had been the capital of the Roman province of Asia for two centuries after its last king, Attalus III, bequeathed it, together with the kingdom of Pergamum, to Rome in 133 .. (see p. 95). Since the early 3d century .. the city of Pergamum had been a chief center of cultural and intellectual life of the Hellenistic world. Although by John’s time Ephesus was beginning to supersede it as the leading city of Asia, Pergamum continued to retain much of its former importance. The two cities long contended for this honor. For further information concerning the ancient city of Pergamum see p. 93; John’s Literary Productions.
The meaning of the name Pergamos is uncertain, but “citadel,” or “acropolis,” seems to be one of its derived meanings. The characteristic experience of the church during the Pergamos period was one of exaltation. From the status of a proscribed and persecuted sect it rose to a position of unchallenged popularity and power (see on v. 13).
**Sword with two edges.** Like the descriptive titles that introduce the messages to the churches of Ephesus and Smyrna, this is drawn from the description of the glorified Christ in ch. 1:16 (see comment there and on ch. 2:1).
12.zh:
你要寫信給別迦摩教會的使者，說：那有兩刃利劍的，說：

**別迦摩。**別迦摩最後一任國王阿塔羅斯三世於公元前133年把該城連同王國贈送給羅馬（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七第25頁）。此後它就成了羅馬亞細亞行省的首府，達兩個世紀之久。從公元前三世紀初起，別迦摩就是希臘文化活動的一箇中心。雖然到了約翰的時代，以弗所開始超過了它而成了亞細亞的主要城市，但別迦摩仍具有重要的地位。這兩座城市長期以來一直競爭主要城市的榮譽。關於別迦摩古城，詳見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七第93頁；和622頁插圖。
“別迦摩”一詞的含義不明，可能有“堡壘，”“衛城”之意。別迦摩時期教會的特徵是地位提高了。她從一個受禁止、被逼迫的教派，上升為一個普遍信仰，大權在握的宗教（見第 13 節註釋）。
**使者。**見啟 1:20 註釋。
**兩刃利劍。**就像耶穌給以弗所和示每拿教會的書信開頭所作的自我介紹一樣，“兩刃利劍”也來自啟 1：16 對得了榮耀之基督的描述（見該節和啟 2：1 註釋）。

29.zh:
聖靈向眾教會所說的話，凡有耳的，就應當聽！

見 第 7 節的註釋。

25.en: **Till I come.** The “blessed hope” (see Titus 2:13) of the soon coming of Christ has ever been the stay of Christians in affliction. Christ does not necessarily imply that He would return within the lifetime of the members of the literal Thyatira church, nor even within the Thyatira period of church history. However, see on ch. 1:1.
25.zh:
但你們已經有的，總要持守，直等到我來。

基督快來乃是“所盼望的福”（參 多 2:13) 。這個盼望一直在患難中支持著基督徒。基督並沒有暗示祂一定會在一世紀推雅推喇教會信徒話著的時候再來，或在推雅推喇教會所代表的教會歷史時期中再來。見 啟 1:1 註釋。

9.en:
**Thy.** See on v. 2.
**Works.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 10) between retaining and omitting this word. See on v. 2.
**Tribulation.** Or, “distress,” “trouble” “affliction.” Intermittent persecution at the hands of various Roman emperors characterized the experience of the church during this period. Under Trajan (98–117), Hadrian (117–138), and Marcus Aurelius (161–180), persecution was sporadic and localized. The first general, systematic persecution of Christians was conducted by Decius (249–251) and Valerian (253–259). Political oppression reached a bloody climax under Diocletian (284–305) and his immediate successors (305–313). Historically, the period represented by the Smyrna church may well be called the Age of Martyrdom. The centuries since have been fragrant (see on v. 8) with the love and devotion of the thousands of unnamed martyrs of this period who were “faithful unto death.”
**Poverty.** Gr. ptōcheia, “abject poverty” (cf. on Mark 12:42). Doubtless the church at Smyrna was not so large or so prosperous as the neighboring congregation at Ephesus. The Christians at Ephesus had left their “first love,” but no such rebuke is sent to those at Smyrna. Instead, Christ reminds them that spiritually they are “rich” (see on James 2:5).
**Blasphemy.** Gr. blasphēmia, “evil speaking,” whether of God or man. In the present context the translation “slander” may be preferable.
**Jews.** Probably “Jews” in a figurative, not a literal, sense (in the sense that Christians now are sometimes described as Israel see Rom. 2:28, 29; 9:6, 7; Gal. 3:28, 29; 1 Peter 2:9). As here used, the term no doubt refers to those who claimed to serve God, but actually served Satan.
The figure has its basis in history. The book of Acts reveals that many of the troubles of the early church grew out of slanderous accusations hurled at them by Jews (see Acts 13:45; 14:2, 19; 17:5, 13; 18:5, 6, 12; 21:27). Apparently this situation was true at Smyrna. In the 2d century Jews are said to have brought about the martyrdom of Polycarp, a bishop of Smyrna. During this time Tertullian speaks of the synagogues as “fountains of persecution” (Scorpiace 10; ANF, vol. 3, p. 643).
**Are not.** They were hypocrites.
**Synagogue of Satan.** Compare the opprobrious epithet, “generation [brood] of vipers” (Matt. 3:7). As a center of Jewish communal life the synagogue (see Vol. V, pp. 56–58) was doubtless the place where many an evil plot was formed against Christians. The name Satan means “accuser,” or “adversary” (see on Zech. 3:1; Rev. 12:10). These Jewish centers became, literally, “synagogues of the accuser.”
9.zh:
我知道你的患難，你的貧窮（你卻是富足的），也知道那自稱是猶太人所說的毀謗話，其實他們不是猶太人，乃是撒但一會的人。

**你的。**見第 2 節註釋。
**患難。**這個時期的教會在羅馬各任皇帝手下斷斷續續地遭受逼迫。在圖拉真（公元 98 年–117 年）, 哈德良 （公元 117 年–138 年），和馬可.奧勒利烏斯（公元 161 年–180 年）執政期間，對基督教的逼迫是零星而局部的。第一次全國性有組織地逼迫基督教是在德西烏斯（公元 249 年–251 年）和瓦萊裡安（公元 253 年–259 年）執政期間。在戴克裡先 （公元 284 年–305 年）以及他的幾位繼位者統治時期（公元 305 年–313 年），政治上的血腥迫害達到了高潮。示每拿教會所代表的這段歷史時期，完全可以被稱為“殉道時期。” 在這幾個世紀裡，成千上萬沒有留下名字的殉道者“至死忠心。”他們的愛心和獻身精神流芳百世（見 第 8 節註釋）
**貧窮。**參可 12:42 註釋。示每拿教會無疑沒有附近的以弗所教會那麼大，那麼興旺。以弗所的基督徒離開了他們“起初的愛心，” 但對於示每拿的信徒，卻沒有這樣的責備。基督提醒他們說，他們在屬靈上是“富足”的（見雅 2:5 註釋）。
**猶太人。**這裡的猶太人可能不是指肉身意義上的 。就像如今的基督徒有時被稱為以色列人一樣。參 羅 2:28, 29；9:6, 7；加 3:28, 29；彼前 2:9。該詞在這裡無疑指那些自稱事奉上帝，實際上卻事奉撒但的人。
這個稱謂有其歷史的背景。據《使徒行傳》記載，早期教會所遭遇的許多患難，都緣於猶太人對他們的誹謗（見徒 13:45；14:2, 19；17:5, 13；18:5, 6, 12；21:27）。這種情況顯然也存在於示每拿。據說在第 2 世紀，示每拿主教波利卡普的殉道就是猶太人造成的。在這段時期，德爾圖良（Tertullian）稱猶太會堂為“逼迫之源”（《前尼西亞教父文集》卷三 第 643 頁）。
**毀謗話。**說上帝或人的“壞話”。
**不是。**他們是偽善者。
**撒但一會的人。**參另一個類似的稱呼“毒蛇的種類”（太 3:7）。猶太會堂作為猶太人社會生活的中心（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五56-58頁），無疑是聚謀反對基督教的地方。“撒但”意為“控告者，”或“作對者”（見亞 3:1；啟 12:10 註釋）。當時這些猶太活動中心實際上就是“控告者的會堂。”
**懷愛倫註釋**。《佈道論》第603頁；《給傳道人的證言》第16頁；《證言》卷六第475頁。

3.en:
**Hast borne.** The Ephesian church had refused to “bear them which are evil” (see on v. 2), but it did endure patiently the unavoidable affliction caused by the false teachers and the persecution that befell it at the hands of fanatical Jews and Gentiles.
**Patience.** See on v. 2.
**My name’s sake.** See on Acts 3:16. The followers of Christ were known by His name; they were called Christians. It was their allegiance to this name, their loyalty to Him whom it signified as their Lord, that subjected them to persecution by the Roman authorities (see p. 720), and led to suffering at the hands of those who were bent upon subverting their faith.
**Hast laboured.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the omission of these words. The original of v. 3 probably read, “And thou hast had patience and hast borne for my name’s sake, and hast not fainted.”
**Fainted.** Gr. kopiaō, “to become weary,” “to become tired.” Compare the use of kopiaō in Isa. 40:31, LXX; John 4:6.
3.zh:
你也能忍耐，曾為我的名勞苦，並不乏倦。

**能忍耐。**見第2節註釋。以弗所教會不“容忍惡人” （見第 2 節註釋），卻不可避免地忍受了假教師所製造的麻煩，以及猶太人和外邦人中狂熱分子的迫害。
**為我的名。**見徒 3:16 的註釋。跟從基督的人因基督的名而為人所知。他們被稱為基督徒。他們對這名的忠誠，和對所承認之主的忠心，使他們受到了羅馬當局的迫害（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七720頁），並在那些決心破壞他們信仰之人的手中受苦。
**勞苦。**有的文本沒有這個詞。
**乏倦。**參該詞用於七十士譯本賽 40:31 ；約 4:6。

20.en:
**A few things.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the omission of this phrase. However, some ancient manuscripts read “much” or “many things.” The simple reading, “I have [it] against thee” (cf. v. 4), is to be preferred.
**Sufferest.** Gr. aphiēmi, “to permit,” “to allow to operate.” The church was at fault not only because many openly submitted to apostasy but also because no earnest effort was being made to check the course of evil.
**Jezebel.** For the account of the historical Jezebel see 1 Kings 16:31; 18:13; 19:1, 2; 21:5–16, 23–25; 2 Kings 9:30–37. It would appear that, as Jezebel sponsored the worship of Baal in Israel (1 Kings 21:25), so in John’s day some false prophetess was attempting to lead astray the church at Thyatira. The message indicates that here, even more than at Pergamum (Rev. 2:14), apostasy was openly and defiantly rampant. As applied to the Thyatira period of Christian history, the figure of Jezebel represents the power that produced the great apostasy of the medieval centuries (see Additional Note on Dan. 7; see on Rev. 2:18; cf. Rev. 17).
**Commit fornication … eat things sacrificed.** See on Rev. 2:14; cf. 2 Kings 9:22. This doubtless had, first, a local application to the church at Thyatira. Applied to the Thyatira period of church history, this would represent an admixture of paganism with Christianity (see on Eze. 16:15; Rev. 17:1). This process was accelerated greatly under Constantine and his successors. Medieval Christianity absorbed, to a great extent, pagan forms and practices.
20.zh:
然而，有一件事我要責備你，就是你容讓那自稱是先知的婦人耶洗別教導我的僕人，引誘他們行姦淫，吃祭偶像之物。

**容讓。**“允許”。教會的錯誤不僅在於許多人公開背道，還在於沒有努力制止罪惡。
**耶洗別。**關於歷史上的耶洗別，見王上 16:31；18:13；19:1, 2；21:5–16, 23–25；王下 9:30–37。像耶洗別在以色列中倡導巴力崇拜一樣（王上 21:25），在約翰的時代也有一些假先知起來，企圖把推雅推喇教會引入歧途。這個信息表明，推雅推喇的背道甚至比別迦摩（啟 2:14) 更加公開，更加猖獗。耶洗別的比喻用於推雅推喇時期的基督教會，代表了導致中世紀大背道的黑暗勢力（見《但以理書》第 7 章補充註釋；見 啟 2:18 註釋；參 啟 17 註釋）。
**行姦淫，吃祭偶像之物。**見 啟 2:14 的註釋；參 王下 9:22。這無疑首先是指一世紀的推雅推喇教會。若用於推雅推喇教會所代表的教會歷史時期，這就代表異教與基督教的混合（見 結 16:15 ；啟 17:1 註釋）。 君士坦丁及其繼位者們加快了這一過程。中世紀的基督教會大量吸收了異教的禮儀和習俗。

13.en:
**Thy works.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the omission of the words “thy works, and.” Compare on v. 2.
**Satan’s seat.** Pergamum had distinguished itself in 29 .. by becoming the site of the first cult of a living Roman emperor. A temple was built and dedicated to the joint worship of the goddess Roma (a personification of the spirit of the empire) and the emperor Augustus. At the very time John wrote these words Christians were suffering persecution for refusing to worship the emperor Domitian (.. 81–96), who insisted on being worshiped as “lord and god.” Pergamum was also the religious capital of Asia Minor. It was a center of Hellenistic (Greco-Mesopotamian) thought and emperor worship, and had many pagan temples. Its designation as the place “where Satan’s seat is” was thus appropriate indeed (see p. 95).
The Pergamos period of church history may be thought of as beginning about the time of Constantine’s espousal of the Christian cause, in .. 313, or of his supposed conversion—perhaps in 323 or 325—and ending in 538 (see Additional Note at end of chapter). It was during this time that the papacy won religious, and to some extent political, leadership of Western Europe (see Additional Note on Dan. 7), and that Satan established his “seat” within the church. The papacy was a skillful blend of paganism with Christianity. This period may be termed the Age of Popularity.
**Name.** See on v. 3.
**My faith.** That is, faith in Me. Compare the experience of the heroes of faith whose names are enshrined in Heb. 11.
**Antipas.** A familiar Greek name, compounded of the Greek words anti, “in place of,” and pas, an abbreviated form of patēr, “father” (cf. on Luke 3:1; 24:18; see Josephus Antiquities xiv. 1. 3 [10]). It reflected a father’s hope that the son so named would eventually take his place in the world. Some commentators hold that a Christian by this name at Pergamum had recently been martyred for his faith, presumably for refusing to worship the emperor. If so, the experience and example of this faithful martyr may be considered as typical of that of untold thousands who suffered for their faith in later ages. Although it is possible that the name may have a figurative application to the Pergamos period of church history, Inspiration provides no apparent clue with respect to such an application.
**Martyr.** Gr. martus, “witness.” A “martyr” is one whose death testifies to his faith. The Greek here rendered “faithful martyr” is identical with that used of Christ in ch. 1:5 and translated “faithful witness.”
13.zh:
我知道你的居所，就是有撒但座位之處；當我忠心的見證人安提帕在你們中間、撒但所住的地方被殺之時，你還堅守我的名，沒有棄絕我的道。

**撒但座位之處。**有的文本在本節“你的居所”前面還有“你的行為”。參第二節註釋。別迦摩在公元前 29 年第一個敬拜尚健在的羅馬皇帝。該城興建了一座廟宇，來供奉女神“羅馬”（Roma，帝國精神的化身）和皇帝奧古斯都。約翰在寫《啟示錄》的時候，基督徒正為拒絕敬拜圖密善皇帝（公元 81 –96年 ）而遭受迫害。圖密善要人尊他為“主和神。” 別迦摩也是小亞細亞的宗教都市。它是希臘（希臘—美索不達米亞）文化和皇帝崇拜的中心。城裡異教的寺廟林立，稱之為“有撒但座位之處”十分合適（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七95頁）。
別迦摩教會時期可以從公元 313 年君士坦丁支持基督教，或者從他公元323年或 325年在名義上悔改信主算起，直到公元 538 年（見本章補充註釋）。在這段時間裡，羅馬教在西歐取得了宗教上的、甚至一定程度的政治上的領導地位（見《但以理書》第七章補充註釋）。撒但在教會內部安置了他的“座位。” 羅馬教是異教和基督教微妙的混合。這段時期可以被稱為“普及時期。”
**見證人。**殉道者以死來見證自己的信仰。“忠心的見證人”原文與 啟 1:5 對基督的稱呼“那誠實做見證的” 是一樣的。
**安提帕。**這是常見的希臘名字。由希臘詞語anti（“代替”）和pateµr（“父”） 的縮寫形式pas ֺ組成（ 路 3:1；24:18 註釋；見約瑟弗斯《猶太古代史》 1.3.10）。這個名字反映了父親的願望，希望兒子將來能在世界上代替他。一些解經家認為安提帕是別迦摩教會一名剛殉身基督徒的名字。他的殉道可能就是因為拒絕敬拜羅馬皇帝。如果是這樣，這位忠心殉道者的經歷和榜樣就可以視為後世成千上萬無名殉道者的代表。雖然這個名字有可能寓指教會歷史的別迦摩時期中，但這種解釋缺乏明顯的聖經根據。
**我的名。**見第 3 節註釋。
**我的道.。**就是信仰我。參《希伯來書》第 11 章所列信心英雄的經歷。

11.en:
**He that hath an ear.** See on v. 7.
**He that overcometh.** See on v. 7. Here, stress should probably be placed on overcoming in spite of the “tribulation” mentioned in v. 10.
**Second death.** As contrasted with the first death, which ends human life temporarily now, and from which there is a resurrection, both for “the just and unjust” (Acts 24:15). The second death is the final extinction of sin and sinners, and from it there can be no resurrection (see on Rev. 20:14; cf. ch. 21:8).
11.zh:
聖靈向眾教會所說的話，凡有耳的，就應當聽！得勝的，必不受第二次死的害。

**凡有耳的。**見第 7 節註釋。
**得勝的。**見第 7 節註釋。這裡可能強調經歷了第 10 節所提到的“患難而取得勝利。
**第二次死的害。**與第一次的死不同。第一次的死是今生生命的暫時結束；不論“善惡” （徒 24:15）都將復活。第二次死是最後消滅罪惡和罪人，不再有復活（見啟 20:14 註釋；參啟 21:8）。

6.en: **Nicolaitanes.** One of the heretical sects that plagued the churches at Ephesus and at Pergamum (see v. 15), and perhaps elsewhere. Irenaeus identifies the Nicolaitans as a Gnostic sect: “John, the disciple of the Lord, preaches this faith [the deity of Christ], and seeks, by the proclamation of the Gospel, to remove that error which by Cerinthus had been disseminated among men, and a long time previously by those termed Nicolaitans, who are an offset of that ‘knowledge’ might confound them, and persuade them that there is but one God, who made all things by His Word” (op. cit. iii. 11. 1; ANF, vol. 1, p. 426). There is also historical evidence of a Gnostic sect called Nicolaitans a century or so later. Some Church Fathers who report concerning this sect (Irenaeus op. cit. i. 26. 3; Hippolytus Refutation of All Heresies vii. 24) identify its founder as Nicolas of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (see Acts 6:5). Whether the tradition concerning Nicolas the deacon is correct, we do not know, but the sect may be the same as the one mentioned by John. In the 2d century, at least, adherents of this sect appear to have taught that deeds of the flesh do not affect the purity of the soul, and consequently have no bearing on salvation.
6.zh:
然而你還有一件可取的事，就是你恨惡尼哥拉一黨人的行為，這也是我所恨惡的。

**尼哥拉一黨人.。**危害以弗所和別迦摩等地教會的異端派別之一（見第 15 節）。伊裡奈烏斯認為尼哥拉黨人是諾斯替教派的一支：“主的門徒約翰宣講了這一信仰 （基督的神性），並藉著《福音書》設法消除塞林圖斯在信徒中散佈的謬道。在以前很長一段時期裡，這種謬道由那些稱為尼哥拉黨的人所傳播。他們屬於所謂的“知識派”。約翰希望說服他們，使他們認識到只有一位上帝，藉著祂的道創造了萬有”（伊裡奈烏斯《反對異端》 3：11： 1；《前尼西亞教父文集》卷一 426頁）。有歷史證據表明，大約一個世紀之後，確實有過一個叫作尼哥拉黨的諾斯替派分支。一些教父提到過這一教派（見伊裡奈烏斯的《反對異端》 1. 26. 3；希波呂託斯的《駁斥所有的異端》 7：24），認為它的創始人是七執事之一，安提阿人尼哥拉（參 徒 6:5）。 我們不知道有關執事尼哥拉的傳統說法是否屬實。但這個教派很可能就是約翰所提到的。至少在第二世紀，這一教派的信徒主張肉身的行為不影響靈魂的純潔，因而與得救無關。

5.en:
**Remove thy candlestick.** See on ch. 1:12. The church would forfeit its status as an accredited representative of Christ. The church had “fallen,” but divine mercy patiently provided an opportunity to “repent” (cf. 2 Peter 3:9).
**Except thou repent.** In the Prologue of his epistle to the Ephesians, Ignatius reports that the church did heed the call to “remember,” “repent,” and “do the firstworks” (see also Ignatius op. cit. i. l; xi. 2).
5.zh:
所以，應當回想你是從哪裡墜落的，並要悔改，行起初所行的事。你若不悔改，我就臨到你那裡，把你的燈臺從原處挪去。

**若不悔改。**伊納爵在給以弗所人書信的序言中，說這個教會確實聽從了呼召，“回想”、“悔改”，並“行起初所行的事”（又見伊納爵《給以弗所人的信》1：1；11：2）。
**把你的燈臺從原處挪去。**見啟 1:12 註釋。教會將被剝奪她作為基督代表的地位。她已經“墜落”了， 但上帝仍憑著祂的憐憫耐心地為她提供“悔改”的機會（參彼後 3:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第450頁；《證言》卷二第296頁；《證言》卷四第286，403頁；《證言》卷五第191，612頁；《證言》卷六第426頁；《證言》卷八第80，248頁。

26.en:
**He that overcometh.** See on v. 7.
**My works.** That is, works that reflect the character of Christ. These are in striking contrast with the “deeds” of those who ally themselves with Jezebel (see on v. 22).
**Power over the nations.** Compare on ch. 20:4.
26.zh:
那得勝又遵守我命令到底的，我要賜給他權柄制伏列國；

**那得勝。**見第 7 節註釋。
**又遵守我命令到底的。**原文是“持守我行為到底的，” 就是反映基督品德的行為。同那些與耶洗別勾結之人“所行的”（參 第 22 節註釋）完全不同。
**我要賜給他權柄制服列國。**參 啟 20:4 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–28節）**。《服務真詮》第516頁。

14.en:
**Thee.** For the force of the singular see on v. 2.
**Balaam.** See Num. 22–24. The analogy with Balaam suggests that there were some at Pergamum whose purpose was to divide and ruin the church by encouraging practices that were forbidden to Christians (see below on “things sacrificed”; cf. on Acts 15:29). Balaam was concerned about advancing his own interests, not those of God’s people.
**Stumblingblock.** Gr. skandalon, the trigger that springs a trap. Thus to “cast a stumblingblock” before someone is to trip him up. See on Matt. 5:29.
**Things sacrificed.** The two practices here mentioned had been expressly prohibited by the council at Jerusalem (see on Acts 15:29; Rom. 14:1; 1 Cor. 8:1). Balaam influenced Israel to commit “whoredom with the daughters of Moab,” to sacrifice to Moabite gods, and to “eat,” presumably of the meat sacrificed to these gods (Num. 25:1, 2, 31:16).
These two sins led to a mixture of paganism with true religion. Applied to Christian history, this portrayal is peculiarly appropriate to the situation in the church in the period following the legalization of Christianity by Constantine in .. 313 and his nominal conversion some 10 or 12 years later. He pursued a policy of blending paganism and Christianity at as many points as possible, in a studied attempt to unite the diverse elements within the empire and thus strengthen it. The favorable, even dominant, position he accorded the church made it a prey to the temptations that always accompany prosperity and popularity. Under Constantine and his successors, almost all of whom continued his favorable policy, the church rapidly became a politico-ecclesiastical institution and lost much of its former spirituality.
14.zh:
然而，有幾件事我要責備你：因為在你那裡有人服從了巴蘭的教訓；這巴蘭曾教導巴勒將絆腳石放在以色列人面前，叫他們吃祭偶像之物，行姦淫的事。

**你。**關於採用單數形式的意義，見 第 2 節註釋。
**巴蘭。**見 民 22–24章。運用巴蘭的典故，暗示別迦摩有人想藉著倡導基督徒所不該做的事情而分裂和破壞教會（見下面“祭偶像之物”註釋；參 徒 15:29 註釋）。巴蘭所關心的是滿足自己的利益，而不是上帝子民的福利。
**絆腳石。**陷阱的觸發器。“將絆腳石放在”別人面前，就是要誘捕他。見太 5:29 的註釋。
**祭偶像之物。**這裡所提到的兩點是耶路撒冷會議所明令禁止的（見 徒 15:29 ；羅 14:1；林前 8:1 註釋）。巴蘭造成了以色列人“與摩押女子行起淫亂” ，給摩押的神獻祭，並且“吃” 祭拜假神之物 （民 25:1, 2,；31:16）。
這兩樣罪造成了異教與真宗教的混合。從基督教的歷史來看，這段話很適合於別迦摩所代表的教會時期。這段時期是從公元 313 年君士坦丁宣佈基督教合法之後，以及他十多年或二十年後名義上信奉基督教時開始的。君士坦丁的策略就是將異教和基督教儘可能地混合在一起，刻意把帝國境內的各種因素聯合起來，達到鞏固帝國的目的。他對教會的偏愛或支配，使教會落入了伴隨著興旺與名聲的種種誘惑之中。在君士坦丁及其繼位者的優惠政策下，教會迅速發展成為一個政教合一的組織，喪失了她原有的屬靈性質。

16.en:
**Repent.** This sharp warning reflects the grave spiritual peril that confronted the Pergamum church.
**Sword of my mouth.** See on ch. 1:16; cf. ch. 2:12. The sword typifies the punishment that would result from a failure to “repent.”
16.zh:
所以，你當悔改；若不悔改，我就快臨到你那裡，用我口中的劍攻擊他們。

**悔改。**這個嚴肅的警告反映了別迦摩教會面臨嚴重的屬靈危機。
**我口中的劍。**見 啟 1:16 註釋；參 啟 2:12。“劍”象徵對不“悔改”的懲罰。

15.zh:
你那裡也有人照樣服從了尼哥拉一黨人的教訓。

見第 6 節註釋。

22.en:
**Cast her into a bed.** The manner of punishment to be meted out to the false prophetess will be appropriate to her crime. This expression seems to be of Semitic origin, and is used with respect to falling ill (see Ex. 21:18; Judith 8:3, LXX; Matt. 9:2, literally, “a paralytic cast upon a bed”). Compare the English expression “to take to one’s bed.” See on Rev. 17:16, 17; 18.
**Them that commit.** These persons are not identified. Compare on ch. 17:1, 2.
**Except they repent.** The door of mercy had not yet fully shut. God never shuts Himself off from sinners; it is they who shut themselves off from Him.
**Their deeds.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading “her deeds.” From the standpoint of God speaking to His church, the sins of Jezebel and her lovers are essentially her sins, for it is she who as a prophetess, aspires to lead the church.
22.zh:
看哪，我要叫他病臥在床。那些與他行淫的人，若不悔改所行的，我也要叫他們同受大患難。

**叫她臥病在床。**對偽女先知的懲罰與她所犯的罪相當。這一詞語似乎出於閃米特語 （參 出 21:18；《猶滴書》8：3， 七十士譯本； 太. 9:2直譯為 “一個臥病在床的癱子“）。見 啟 17:16,；17;：18註釋。
**與她同行淫的人。**不知道這些人是誰。參 啟 17:1, 2註釋。
**若不悔改。**恩典的門還沒有完全關閉。上帝絕不讓自己與罪人隔絕。是罪人自己與上帝隔絕。
**所行的。**從上帝對祂教會說話的立場上看，耶洗別及其情人們的罪從根本上來說就是她的罪，因為她是領導教會的女先知。

1.en:
**Angel.** See on ch. 1:20.
Ephesus. Some define the name Ephesus as meaning “desirable.” In John’s day Ephesus was the leading city of the Roman province of Asia, and later was its capital (see p. 88; John’s Literary Productions; see on chs. 1:4; 2:12). It was situated at the western terminus of a great highway that crossed Asia Minor from Syria, and this, together with its location as an important seaport on the Aegean, made it a focal point for trade. Christianity appears to have been preached there first about .. 52, by Paul, when he stopped for a short time while homeward bound to Jerusalem and Antioch from his Second Missionary Journey. His friends Aquila and Priscilla settled there at that time, and, together with an Alexandrian Jew named Apollos—whose concept of Christianity seems to have been pre-Pentecostal—fostered the work of evangelization until Paul’s return, probably a year or two later (see Acts 18:19 to 19:7). This time the apostle remained at Ephesus for about three years (see Vol. VI, p. 30), longer than at any other place on his recorded missionary journeys. This would seem to indicate that his work there was especially fruitful. His biographer, Luke, declares that “all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks” (Acts 19:10). It is probable, therefore, that during this time at least some of the other churches in Asia were established (see Col. 4:13, 15, 16). After his first Roman imprisonment Paul appears to have visited Ephesus again, probably about .. 64, leaving Timothy in charge (see 1 Tim. 1:3).
Nothing further is definitely known of the history of the church at Ephesus until its name appears probably about three decades later in the Revelation. However, tradition indicates that John, the beloved disciple of Jesus, became the leader of this church, presumably after the breakup of the Christian headquarters at Jerusalem about .. 68, during the Jewish-Roman War (see p. 716). Thus, at the time the Revelation was written, Ephesus must have been one of the leading centers of Christianity. Consequently it was fitting that Christ’s first message by John should have been addressed to this church. Its central location with respect to the Christian world as a whole makes all the more understandable the fact that its spiritual condition could well be characteristic of the whole church during the apostolic period, the era of Christian history reaching approximately to the end of the 1st century (c. .. 31–100; see Additional Note at end of chapter). It may well be called the Age of Apostolic Purity, an attribute highly desirable in God’s sight.
**Holdeth.** Gr. krateō, “to hold fast,” a more vigorous expression than is used in ch. 1:16.
**Seven stars.** See on ch. 1:16, 20. In a special way the leaders of the church on earth are to be under the protection and control of Christ. In their appointed task they are ever sustained by divine power and grace. It is to be noted that the characteristic way in which Christ introduces Himself to each of the seven churches is drawn from the composite vision John saw in ch. 1:11–18.
**Walketh.** A more vigorous description of Christ’s relationship to His church than in ch. 1:13, where John simply refers to Christ as being “in the midst of the seven candlesticks.” As the individual churches of apostolic times enjoyed the watchcare, attention, and ministry of Christ, so has the Christian church as a whole throughout the successive periods of its history. Thus is fulfilled His promise to the disciples to be with them “alway, even unto the end of the world” (Matt. 28:20).
**Candlesticks.** See on ch. 1:12.
1.zh:
你要寫信給以弗所教會的使者，說：那右手拿著七星、在七個金燈臺中間行走的，說：

**以弗所教會。**有人認為“以弗所”意為“理想的。” 在約翰的時代，以弗所是羅馬亞細亞行省的主要城市，後來還成為她的首府（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七第 88頁；第622頁插圖《約翰的著作》；參啟1：4；2：12註釋）。該城位於從敘利亞穿越小亞細亞的大道西端，是愛琴海的一個重要港口，因此它也是一個重要的貿易中心。基督教在以弗所的傳播似乎始於約公元52年。保羅在第二次傳道行程回耶路撒冷和安提阿時曾在以弗所作短暫的停留。他的朋友亞基拉和百居拉就留在了那裡。還有一位來自亞歷山大的猶太籍基督徒亞波羅。他的基督教信仰似乎還停留在五旬節以前的階段。他們三位一同開展布道工作，直到保羅一、二年以後回到以弗所（見徒 18:19-19:7）。這一次使徒保羅在以弗所留了三年左右（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷六第30頁），在所記錄的傳道行程中時間超在任何其他地方。這似乎表明他在那裡的工作頗有成效。他的傳記作者路加宣稱：“一切住在亞細亞的，無論是猶太人，是希臘人，都聽見主的道”（徒 19:10）。 因此可以斷定，在那段時間裡，至少在亞細亞還建立起其他的一些教會（見西 4:13, 15, 16）。保羅第一次被囚羅馬釋放以後，似乎在公元64年又訪問了以弗所，並把提摩太留下來負責（見提前 1:3）。
此後以弗所教會的歷史留下了空白，直到約三十年後它出現在《啟示錄》中。但教會傳統認為公元68年猶太與羅馬爆發戰爭時，耶路撒冷的基督教總部解散了。之後耶穌所愛的門徒約翰就成為以弗所教會的領袖（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七第716頁）。 在寫《啟示錄》的時候，以弗所一定已成為基督教的中心之一。所以基督讓約翰傳達的第一封信自然就寫給了以弗所。它在整個基督教界的中心地位，使她的屬靈狀況成為整個使徒時期教會（約公元 31年–100年；見本章補充註釋）的代表。這個時代完全可以稱為純潔的使徒時代，在上帝的眼中是非常“理想”的。
**使者。**見啟 1:20註釋。
**拿著。**該詞原文比 啟 1：16 的“拿著”語氣更重。
**七星。**見啟 1:16, 20註釋。從特殊的意義上說，地上教會的領袖都是受基督的保護和掌管的。他們在從事所指定的工作時，始終受到上帝能力和恩典的支持。值得注意的是，基督對每一個教會的自我介紹都出自約翰在 啟1:11-18中所見的種種畫面。
**七個金燈臺中間。**參 啟 1:12 註釋。
**行走。**這裡比 啟1:13 更加生動地描寫了基督與祂教會的關係。在 啟 1:13中，約翰只說基督在“燈臺中間行走。”使徒時期的各個教會曾得到基督的看顧，關注和服務，整個基督教會在以後的各個歷史階段中也是如此。這就應驗了祂“常與你們同在，直到世界的末了”（太 28:20）的應許。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第586頁；《證言》卷五第435頁；《證言》卷六第413，418頁；《證言》卷八第23頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《證言》卷五第435頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《證言》卷六第422頁；《證言》卷八第98頁。

23.en:
**Children.** The fornication of this Jezebel was habitual and of long standing, for she had children. Figuratively, this should probably be understood in the sense that she had won committed adherents. Judgment was to descend not only upon the mother but also upon the offspring, who were contaminated by her evil character. Compare the destruction of the children of Ahab (2 Kings 10:7).
**Death.** John may have in mind the LXX of Eze. 33:27, where the significant passage reads “And those in the caves I will kill with death.” Instead of “death” the Hebrew reads “pestilence,” or “plague.” Possibly this is the meaning of “death” in John’s passage.
**Reins.** That is, the kidneys, which anciently were thought to be the seat of the will and the affections (cf. on Ps. 7:9.)
**Hearts.** That is, minds, meaning the intellect. Christ penetrates both the thoughts and the emotions. Christ’s judgment is just because He sees and takes into consideration the secrets of the heart. See Ps. 7:9; Jer. 11:20; see on 1 Sam. 16:7.
23.zh:
我又要殺死他的黨類（原文是兒女），叫眾教會知道，我是那察看人肺腑心腸的，並要照你們的行為報應你們各人。

**我又要殺死。**約翰可能想到了七十士譯本的結 33:27：“那些在洞裡的，我要殺死他們。” 希伯來原文是“遭瘟疫而死。” 或許這就是約翰在本節的“死”的意思吧。
**她的黨類(原文作兒女)。**耶洗別長期淫亂，甚至生下了兒女。這可能比喻她有了忠實的追隨者。懲罰不僅要落到母親身上，也要落到那些被她的邪惡品格所汙染的兒女身上。參亞哈兒女們的滅亡（王下 10:7）。
**肺腑。**腎臟。古人認為腎臟是人意志及情感的所在（參 詩 7:9 註釋）。
**心腸。**頭腦，指人的智力。基督能看透人的思想和情感。基督的審判是公義的，因為祂瞭解和鑑察人心的秘密。 見 詩 7:9；耶 11:20；見 撒上 16:7 註釋。

18.en:
**Angel.** See on ch. 1:20.
**Thyatira.** The origin and meaning of this name are uncertain. Some have suggested that Thyatira means “sweet savor of labor,” perhaps on the basis of the “works” of the church set forth in v. 19. Although less notable than the other six cities, ancient Thyatira was nevertheless distinguished by the number and variety of trades and crafts that flourished there. Apparently, prominent among these was that of the dyeing of cloth (see Acts 16:14). The Christians of Thyatira doubtless found employment largely in the local crafts. For further information concerning the ancient city of Thyatira see p. 96; John’s Literary Productions.
As applied to Christian history, the message to Thyatira is particularly appropriate to the experience of the true church in the Dark Ages and the later Middle Ages (see Additional Note on ch. 2).
Trends that began in earlier periods became dominant during the Dark Ages. The Scriptures not being available to the ordinary Christian, tradition was exalted in their place. Works came to be considered a means of attaining salvation. An earthly and human priesthood obscured the true and divine priesthood of Jesus Christ. See Additional Note on Dan. 7. It was a time of great difficulty for those who resisted the great apostasy, and the Thyatira period of church history may well be called the Age of Adversity. Because of persecution, the flame of truth flickered and nearly went out. The spiritual message of the Reformation was essentially a restoration of the great truths of the gospel. It proclaimed that men are saved only by faith in Christ, that their only standard of faith and practice is Scripture, and that every man may appear on his own behalf before the great High Priest, Jesus Christ, without a human intercessor.
**Son of God.** See on Luke 1:35; John 1:14. This title, like those that introduce the messages to the other churches, is drawn from the description of the glorified Christ in Rev. 1:13 (see on ch. 2:1). Here the definite article is used, thus specifically identifying the Author of the message as the second person of the Godhead (cf. on ch. 1:13).
**Eyes … feet.** See on ch. 1:14, 15.
18.zh:
你要寫信給推雅推喇教會的使者，說：那眼目如火焰、腳像光明銅的神之子說：

**推雅推喇。**這個名字的來源和含義不明。可能是因為 19 節所提到了該教會的“勤勞”，有人認為“推雅推喇”意為“勞動的芳香。” 古代推雅推喇的名望雖然不及其他六座城市，但它仍以其繁榮的各種行業和工藝而著稱，而其中最出色的要算是布匹的染色了（參 徒 16:14）。推雅推喇的基督徒無疑大都是當地的工匠。關於推雅推喇古城，詳見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七96頁；622頁插圖）。
給推雅推喇的信息特別適合於中世紀黑暗時期和中世紀後期真教會的狀況（見本章補充註釋）。
在黑暗時期，早期的趨勢發展成為主流。普通的基督徒手中沒有聖經，由遺傳取而代之。行為被視為得救的手段。世俗的教階制混淆了耶穌基督神聖真祭司的工作。參 《但以理書》第 7 章補充註釋。對於那些抵制大背道的人來說，那是一段大艱難的日子。推雅推喇教會時期完全可以被稱為“逆境時期” 。逼迫使真理的火炬搖曳不定，幾近熄滅。宗教改革的屬靈信息從根本上來說，是對福音偉大真理的恢復。它宣稱人得救只能憑著信基督。基督徒信仰與行為的唯一標準乃是聖經。每個人都可以自己來到大祭司耶穌基督的面前，不用任何人作為中保。
**使者.。**見 啟 1:20 註釋。
**那眼目如火焰、腳像光明銅。**見 啟 1:14, 15 註釋。
**上帝之子。**見 路 1:35 ；約 1:14 註釋。與給其它教會的信對耶穌的稱呼一樣，這個稱呼也來自 啟 1:13 對獲得榮耀之基督的描述（見 啟 2:1 註釋）。原文在這裡使用了定冠詞，表明信息的來源是三一真神中的第二位（參啟 1:13 註釋）。

24.en:
**The rest.** That is, the loyal believers in Thyatira. Historically, this refers to small groups throughout the Middle Ages that sought to remain loyal to apostolic Christianity. Such movements were found both within and without the formal framework of the Catholic Church. Particularly important were such groups as the Waldenses on the continent of Europe and the followers of Wyclif in England. Neither of these groups had the measure of evangelical truth that was proclaimed later in the Protestant Reformation, but the message “unto the rest in Thyatira” was appropriate to them. Upon them God put no further burden than to be faithful to the light that was theirs.
**This doctrine.** That is, the teachings of Jezebel (see on v. 20).
**Depths.** Literally, “deeps,” meaning “deep things.” Christ takes the very words the apostates proudly apply to their own teachings (“as they speak”), and devastatingly terms them “the deep things of Satan.” The Gnostics claimed to be the only ones who knew “the deep things” (see Vol. VI, pp. 54–58).
**None other burden.** Faithfulness to the light that was theirs would be sufficient.
24.zh:
至於你們推雅推喇其餘的人，就是一切不從那教訓、不曉得他們素常所說撒但深奧之理的人，我告訴你們，我不將別的擔子放在你們身上。

**其餘的人。**即推雅推喇教會中忠實的信徒。在歷史上，這是指中世紀那些努力堅持使徒教會純正信仰的基督教小團體。這樣的團體在羅馬教會內部和外面都有活動。其中最主要的是歐洲大陸的瓦典西人和英國威克里夫的追隨者們。這兩批人所擁有的亮光，雖然都不及後來宗教改革運動所宣揚的福音真理，但給“推雅推喇其餘的人”的信息用在他們身上卻是很合適的。他們只要忠於他們所有的亮光就夠了。上帝不將別的擔子放在他們身上。
**那教訓。**就是耶洗別的教訓（見 第 20 節註釋）。
**深奧之理。**意思是“深奧的事情。” 背道者自稱他們的教訓（即“他們素常所說”）是“深奧之理”。基督則將之貶稱為“撒但深奧之理。” 諾斯替教派聲稱，只有他們明白“深奧之理”（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷六54-58頁）。
**我不將別的擔子放在你們身上。**忠於已經持有的亮光就夠了。

17.en:
**Hath an ear.** See on v. 7.
**Him that overcometh.** See on v. 7.
**Hidden manna.** See Ex. 16:14–36. Some think the allusion here may be to the manna Aaron placed in a pot and preserved in the ark (Ex. 16:33; Heb. 9:4). An ancient Jewish teaching declares that when the Messiah would come, “the treasury of manna shall again descend from on high, and they will eat of it in those years” (2 Baruch 29:8; R. H. Charles, Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, vol. 2, p. 498). In view of John 6:31–34 it seems that John here intends manna to be symbolic of spiritual life in Christ now, and eternal life in the hereafter (see on John 6:32, 33).
**White stone.** Various ancient customs have been suggested as providing a basis for this allusion to the gift of a white stone, but none of these is altogether satisfactory. One of the more common ancient customs was that of the use of a white and a black stone by jurors to determine acquittal or conviction. All that may be said with reasonable certainty is that John doubtless refers to some ceremony involving the bestowal of a special gift or honor.
**New name.** In the Bible a person’s name often stands for his character, and a new name would indicate a new character. The new is not patterned after the old, but replaces it and is different from it. Here the Christian is promised a “new name,” that is, a new and different character, patterned after that of God (cf. Isa. 62:2; 65:15; Rev. 3:12).
**No man knoweth.** The experience of spiritual rebirth, of the transformation of character, can be understood only by personal experience. Attempts to explain this experience to a man who himself has not been born again can never convey a true or complete picture of it (cf. John 3:5–8).
17.zh:
聖靈向眾教會所說的話，凡有耳的，就應當聽！得勝的，我必將那隱藏的嗎哪賜給他，並賜他一塊白石，石上寫著新名；除了那領受的以外，沒有人能認識。

**凡有耳的的，就應當聽。**見 第 7 節註釋。
**得勝的。**見 第 7 節註釋。
**隱藏的嗎哪。**見 出 16:14–36。有人認為這是指亞倫放在約櫃罐子裡的嗎哪（出 16:33；來 9:4）。 一種猶太人的古老說法宣稱，當彌賽亞降臨的時候，“嗎哪將再次從天而降。在那些日子，他們將吃嗎哪”（《巴錄二書》 29：8；2 ；查爾斯 《舊約次經與偽經》 卷 二第 498 頁）。 鑑於 約 6:31–34的教導，這裡的嗎哪似乎象徵基督徒今生在基督裡的屬靈生命，以及來世的永生（見 約 6:32, 33 註釋）。
**白石。**人們曾用各種古代的風俗來解釋這裡賞賜白石的做法，但都不很滿意。一種比較普遍的古代慣例就是陪審員用白石和黑石來代表無罪或有罪。唯一能夠肯定的是，約翰這裡無疑在指某種授予特別禮物或榮譽的儀式。
**新名。**在聖經中，一個人的名字往往代表他的品格，所以新名代表新的品格。新名不是舊名的模仿，而是代替，與舊名完全不同。這裡應許基督徒將有一個“新名，”就是按照上帝的品格塑造的新品格（參 賽 62:2；65:15；啟 3:12）。
**除了那領受的以外，沒有人能認識。**屬靈重生的經驗，品格的改變，只有親歷者才能體會。一個沒有重生的人，是不可能準確完整地解釋這種經驗的（參 約 3:5–8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第646頁；《服務真詮》第516頁；《今日的生活》第156頁；《給青年人的信息》第95頁；《先祖與先知》第297頁。

4.en: **Thy first love.** This “love” probably included wholehearted love for God and for truth, and love for one another as brethren and for their fellow men in general (see on Matt. 5:43, 44; 22:34–40). Perhaps the doctrinal controversies stirred up by the false teachers had given rise to a factious spirit. Also, in spite of diligent efforts on the part of many to stay the tide of false teaching, a number who remained in the church were no doubt affected in greater or less degree by it. To the extent that error had found a lodging place in the church, to that extent was thwarted the activity of the Holy Spirit as a messenger of truth (John 16:13), whose task it is to convert the principles of truth into a living force for the transformation of character (see John 16:8–11; Gal. 5:22, 23; Eph. 4:30; etc.). Furthermore, as the testimony of those who had personally associated with Jesus ended, as one by one they died, and the vision of the imminence of Christ’s return (see on Rev. 1:1) began to fade, the flame of faith and devotion burned ever lower. For comment on other aspects of this departure from the pristine purity of faith and practice see Vol. IV, pp. 834, 835.
4.zh:
然而有一件事我要責備你，就是你把起初的愛心離棄了。

**起初的愛心。**可能包括全心全意地愛上帝，愛真理全，弟兄姊妹的彼此相愛，和對一般同胞的愛（見太 5:43, 44；22:34–40 註釋）。假教師所挑起的教義爭端可能導致了分裂的精神。儘管有許多人竭力阻止假道的蔓延，教會中仍有一部分信徒可能不同程度地受到了假道的影響。謬道在教會里既找到了棲身之所，就妨礙了真理的使者——聖靈的工作（約 16:13)。聖靈的工作就是把真理的原則轉化為改變品格的活潑能力（見約16:8–11；加 5:22, 23；弗 4:30等）。此外，當那些親自與耶穌交往過的人一個地一個地離世後，他們的見證止息了。基督即將再來的前景暗淡了（見啟 1:1註釋)，信心和獻身之火減弱了。關於教會離開起初純正信仰和行為的其他方面，見《SDA聖經註釋》卷四第834，835頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《醫療佈道論》第37頁；《證言》卷二第293頁；《證言》卷八第26頁；《論福利工作》第79頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《使徒行述》第587頁；《歷代願望》第280頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第320頁；《先祖與先知》第165頁；《給傳道人的證言》第168，275，352，461頁；《證言》卷六第368，421頁；《證言》卷八第299頁。

27.en:
**Rule.** Gr. poimainō, literally, “to shepherd,” and thus “to rule” (see on Matt. 2:6). The passage is quoted from Ps. 2:9. For the time, circumstances, and nature of Christ’s breaking the nations with a “rod of iron” see on Rev. 19:15. That the Jews considered Ps. 2:9 a Messianic prediction is evident from the pseudepigraphical Psalms of Solomon 17:26 (Charles, op. cit., p. 649): “He [Messiah, Son of David] shall thrust out sinners from (the) inheritance, He shall destroy the pride of the sinner as a potter’s vessel. With a rod of iron he shall break in pieces all their substance.” Inasmuch as the redeemed will live and reign with Christ they are here represented as sharing Christ’s work (see on Rev. 12:5; 20:4).
**Rod.** The word used here represents the Heb. shebet of Ps. 2:9, which may mean a shepherd’s rod (Ps. 23:4), or a scepter (Ps. 45:6), or a rod of punishment (Ps. 125:3). The context of Rev. 2:27 suggests that the “rod” is here both a symbol of rulership and an instrument of punishment.
**Vessels of a potter.** See Jer. 19:1, 10, 11.
**Broken.** The rule here spoken of results in a destruction of the wicked. For the nature of this rule see on ch. 20:4.
**To shivers.** Or, “to pieces.”
**As I received.** See Matt. 11:27; 28:18; John 3:35; 5:22, 27; Acts 17:31; Vol. V, p. 919.
27.zh:
他必用鐵杖轄管（轄管：原文是牧）他們，將他們如同窰戶的瓦器打得粉碎，像我從我父領受的權柄一樣。

**杖。**源於詩 2:9 的希伯來語 shebet 。可以指牧人的杖（詩 23:4），國王的權杖 （詩 45:6），或懲戒的刑杖 （詩 125:3）。本節的“杖”既指王權的象徵，也指懲罰的工具。
**轄管。**直譯為 “牧養”（見 太 2:6 的註釋）。 這句話引自 詩 2:9。有關基督用“鐵杖”管轄列國的時間，背景和性質，見 啟 19:15註釋。偽經《所羅們詩篇》 17：6 表明猶太人視 詩 2:9 為有關彌賽亞的預言：“祂（大衛的子孫彌賽亞]）將把罪人趕出繼承之地。祂將摧毀罪人的驕傲，象打碎窯匠的瓦器一樣。祂必用鐵杖把他們打得粉碎”（查爾斯的 《舊約次經及偽經》 649頁）。贖民將基督同享永生權柄，一起掌權，所以說他們是與祂同工的（見啟 12:5;；20:4 註釋）。
**窯戶的瓦器.。**見 耶 19:1, 10, 11。
**打得粉碎.。**這裡的權柄使惡人遭到毀滅。關於這一權柄的性質，見啟 20:4註釋。
**像我從我父領受的權柄一樣。**見 太 11:27；28:18；約 3:35；5:22, 27；徒 17:31；《SDA聖經註釋》卷五919頁。

900.zh:
把給七教會的信息應用到教會歷史中七個相繼的時期（見啟 2:1 註釋），自然需要採納一系列的年代，把這些信息與相關的歷史時期聯繫起來。但在確定這些年代的時候需要謹記：一，七教會的預言與嚴格意義上的時間預言不同，因為預言本身並沒有提供年代。它主要涉及教會在相繼的歷史時期中的經歷，與但 7:25 中1260日的預言，但 8：14 中2300日預言，和但 9：25 中的70 個 7 的預言等大不相同。二，主要的歷史時期是無法準確界定的。因此所採用的年代最多隻能作為大概的標誌，而不是精確的界限。兩個時期的過渡是一個逐漸演進的過程。但我們仍需選定一個大概的年代，把七教會的信息同相應的歷史事件聯繫起來。有人提出了與下面不同的年代，用不同的名稱來描述各個時期。但這些年代和名稱的差別不會對七教會信息本身的解讀產生實質性的影響。
1.	以弗所  人們普遍認同它代表使徒時期的教會，從公元 31 年基督昇天的時候算起（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五 257–260頁），直到公元 100 年左右為止。
2.	示每拿  關於將公元 100 年作為這一時期的開始，參上面“以弗所”的解釋。給第二個和第三個教會的信息表明，從示每拿到別迦摩的過渡是教會從受逼迫到受歡迎的過程。第一位所謂信基督教的羅馬皇帝君士坦丁大帝的統治時期（公元 306年–337年）, 代表著這一過渡時期。在他於公元 313 年頒佈著名的米蘭敕令之前，基督教被視為非法宗教，多次遭受當局的猛烈逼迫（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷六 47, 61頁；卷 七18, 19頁）。米蘭敕令宣佈，帝國境內一切宗教都享有同等的權利，並且歸還被沒收的基督教資產。同年，君士坦丁宣佈豁免基督教神職人員參加政府和軍隊服務的義務，免徵他們的財產稅。公元 313 年，或者他名義上信奉基督教的公元 332 或 325 年，均可作為教會從士每拿時期過渡到別迦摩時期的大體時間。
3.	別迦摩  關於教會過渡到別迦摩時期，見前面對“士每拿”的註釋。靈感之筆稱別迦摩時期為妥協，背道和世俗化的時期。在這段時期裡，羅馬教會開始加強其權力和權威。到別迦摩時期結束時，羅馬帝國已經失勢，教皇制已日臻完善，準備執掌西方基督教界的統治大權（見《但以理書》第七章補充註釋）。
以下任何一個重大事件都可以作為這段時期結束的標誌。例如公元 476年最後一位西羅馬皇帝的廢黜。公元 496年法蘭克國王克洛維成為第一位信奉基督教的日爾曼族統治者。他把對其他日耳曼民族的征服同教會的利益緊密聯繫起來。公元 538年，東羅馬皇帝查士丁尼於公元 533年頒佈的法令完全生效。該法令賦予羅馬教皇在東西基督教界的無上權威。
歷史學家們通常把格列高利教皇（公元 590年–604年）的任職作為從古代到中世紀的過渡。他擔任教皇，也可看作另一個此類界限的標誌。格列高利被視為中世紀第一大主教。他在很多方面大膽扮演了西方皇帝的角色。他的統治為後來教皇享有絕對權威的主張奠定了基礎。
公元 756 年標誌著教皇控制領土的開始，以及法國所謂的“教皇長子”地位的確立（參《SDA聖經註釋》卷四 837頁）。那一年，法國的丕平征服了意大利北部威脅教皇統治的倫巴底人，並把他們的領土送給教皇。這一個舉動通常被稱為“丕平捐贈”。它標誌著教皇國的開始,。教皇君臨在這塊領地，實施絕對的統治達一千多年。
然而538年作為一千二百六十年（見但 7:25 註釋）預言的起點，說明它比較適合作為別迦摩時期的終點。見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七18–22頁。
4.	推雅推喇  關於538年作為推雅推喇時期開始的理由，見上面“別迦摩”的註釋。推雅推喇時期的特點是教皇掌握了至高的權力。一千二百六十年的預言在聖經預言中的重要性（見 但 7:25 ；啟 12:6 註釋），說明把1798年作為推雅推喇時期的結束比較合適。但鑑於宗教改革運動對教皇霸權的沉重打擊，也可把1517年作為推雅推喇時期的結束（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷四 837頁； 卷 七 50頁）。有人認為 1870年教皇國的喪失，和教皇自稱為“梵蒂岡之囚” 也可以使這一年成為推雅推喇時期的結束。但1870年與一千二百六十年的預言，以及與《啟示錄》第 2 、第 3 章所描繪剩下的教會歷史都銜接不上。
5.	撒狄  宗教改革時期的教會符合“撒狄”的特徵，因此可以認定它是從1517年或1798年開始的（見以上“推雅推喇”註釋）。那些認為1798年是推雅推喇教會時期的結束和撒狄教會時期開始的人，還認為1833年是撒狄教會的結束。依據下面“非拉鐵非”註釋所提出的理由，有人認為以1755年作為撒狄時期的結束比較妥當。
6.	非拉鐵非 靈感之筆稱非拉鐵非為復臨大覺醒時期的教會。人們提出了它不同的開始時間。有人認為是1833年。那一年自然界出現了我們主所預言的重大徵兆（見太 24:33 註釋），且與威廉米勒耳所發起復臨運動的早期信息密切相關。有人認為1798年是但 11:35 “末了”的開始（見該節註釋），這也有一定的道理。還有人認為是1755年，因為這一年通常被認為是第 6 印中第一個兆頭出現的年代（見 啟 6:12 註釋）。他們認為這個年代與非拉鐵非教會作為復臨大覺醒時期教會的特徵相符。基督復臨安息日會的解經家們普遍認同1844年是非拉鐵非時期的結束，和老底嘉時期的開始（見 但 8:14 註釋）。
7.	老底嘉  關於1844作為這一時期的開始，見上面“非拉鐵非”的註釋。老底嘉時期作為七教會中的最後一個教會，要延續到世界的末日。
900.en:
The application of the various messages to the seven churches to seven consecutive periods of church history (see on ch. 2:1) naturally suggests the utility of a series of transition dates to facilitate the coordination of the several messages with their respective historical periods. In attempting to assign such dates, however, it is well to remember that: (1) The prophecy of the seven churches is not a time prophecy in the usual sense of the term, for no specific chronological data accompany it. It is concerned primarily with successive experiences of the church, and differs considerably from such prophecies as those concerning the 1260 days of Dan. 7:25, the 2300 days of ch. 8:14, and the 70 weeks of ch. 9:25. (2) Major eras of history can hardly be marked off by exact dates. So used, dates are at best convenient landmarks of a rather general sort, not exact boundary markers. Actual transition from one period to another is a gradual process. Nevertheless it is well to select approximate dates as an aid to correlating the messages with the corresponding events of history. Some would suggest different dates from those given below and use different phrases to describe the various periods. However, these variations in dates and names do not materially affect the over-all message found in the letters to the seven churches.
1. Ephesus. There is general agreement that the period thus represented spans the apostolic age, and may, accordingly, be dated approximately from .. 31, the year of our Lord’s ascension (see Vol. V, pp. 257–260), to .. 100.
2. Smyrna. For .. 100 as marking the beginning of this period see the foregoing on “Ephesus.” The messages to the second and third churches identify the transition from Smyrna to Pergamum as one from persecution to popularity. The reign of Constantine the Great, 306–337, the first so-called Christian emperor of Rome, marks such a transition. Prior to his famous Edict of Milan in 313, Christianity was an illegal religion and experienced repeated periods of severe persecution by the state (see Vol. VI, pp. 47, 61; Vol. VII, pp. 18, 19). That edict decreed equal rights for all religions throughout the empire and restored confiscated Christian property. In the same year Constantine exempted the Christian clergy from civil and military service, and their property from taxation. Either this date, 313, or that of his supposed conversion to Christianity, commonly given as 323 or 325, might be taken as an appropriate year to mark the transition from the Smyrna period to that of Pergamum.
3. Pergamos. For the transition to the Pergamos period see the foregoing on “Smyrna.” Inspiration has characterized the Pergamos period as a time of compromise, apostasy, and popularity, the time during which the Church of Rome was consolidating its power and authority. Accordingly, the close of the Pergamos period should find imperial Rome out of the way and the papacy fully formed and ready to embark on its career as ruler of Western Christendom (see Additional Note on Dan. 7).
Any one of various events might serve as an acceptable boundary marker for the close of this period. The deposition of the last Roman emperor in 476 marks it as one such date. The conversion, in 496, of the Frankish king Clovis, the first Germanic ruler to embrace Roman Christianity and to ally himself with the interests of the church in the conquest of other Germanic peoples, is another. In 538 Justinian’s decree of 533, according the pope plenary ecclesiastical power in East and West, began to become effective.
Historians generally take the pontificate of Gregory the Great (590–604) as marking the transition from ancient to medieval times, and his reign as pope might be considered another such boundary marker. Gregory is considered the first of the medieval prelates. He boldly assumed, in many ways, the role of emperor in the West, and his administration laid the foundation for later claims to papal absolutism.
The year 756 marks the beginning of papal territorial rule and the accession of France to the role of so-called “eldest son of the papacy” (see Vol. 4, pp. 837). In that year Pepin of France subdued the Lombards of northern Italy, who had been threatening the pope, and ceded their territory to him. This grant, commonly called the Donation of Pepin, marks the beginning of the Papal States, which the pope governed as an absolute monarch for more than 1,000 years.
However, the importance of 538 as the starting point of the 1,260 years (see on Dan. 7:25) suggests it as a more appropriate terminal date for the Pergamos period than any of the others. See pp. 18–22.
4. Thyatira. For 538 as a beginning date for the Thyatira period see above on “Pergamos.” The Thyatira period is characterized as the era of papal supremacy. The importance of the 1,260-year period in Bible prophecy (see on Dan. 7:25; Rev. 12:6) suggests that 1798 might well be selected as the terminal date for Thyatira. But in view of the importance of the Reformation in breaking papal supremacy, the date 1517 would also be an appropriate terminal date (see Vol. IV, p. 837; Vol. VII, p. 50). Some might hold that the loss of the Papal States in 1870 and the consequent self-imposed status of the pope as “prisoner of the Vatican” would, similarly, make that year eligible for consideration. However, the year 1870 seems to be somewhat too late to comport with either the 1,260 years of prophecy or with the remaining periods of church history as delineated in Rev. 2 and 3.
5. Sardis. Characteristically, this is the church of Reformation times, and as such may be thought of as beginning in 1517, or possibly 1798 (see the foregoing on “Thyatira”). Those who propose 1798 as the terminal date for the Thyatira church period and the opening of the Sardis period suggest 1833 as an appropriate year marking the close of the latter. For reasons set forth below on “Philadelphia,” others suggest 1755 as an appropriate terminal date.
6. Philadelphia. Inspiration has presented this as the church of the great second advent awakening. Various beginning dates have been suggested as appropriate for this period. Some propose 1833, the year of the great climactic sing in nature foretold by our Lord (see on Matt. 24:33). This point of time was closely connected with the early proclamation of the advent message by William Miller. Others suggest 1798, the beginning of the “time of the end” of the Dan. 11:35 (see comment there), which would also be acceptable. Still others favor the date 1755, which is commonly accepted as marking the first of the specific signs of the end under the sixth seal (see on Rev. 6:12), considering that this choice comports well with the character of the Philadelphia church as the church of the advent awakening. There is general agreement among Seventh-day Adventist expositors that the year 1844 should be considered as marking the close of the Philadelphia period and the opening of the Laodicean period (see on Dan. 8:14).
7. Laodicea. For the year 1844 as marking the beginning of this period see the foregoing on “Philadelphia.” Being the last of the seven, the Laodicean period continues till the end of time.

8.en:
**The beast that thou sawest.** That is, the beast of v. 3. John was not shown the beast in either its “was” or its “is not” state, but in its revived state following the “is not” period. However, the angel briefly recounts the past career of this fearful creature by way of identifying the beast as John saw it (see on vs. 8–11).
In the introduction to the vision (vs. 1, 2) and in the vision itself (vs. 3–6) John’s attention was directed almost exclusively to the woman, and the beast is mentioned almost incidentally. In the Greek of vs. 1–6, according to Nestle’s text, 102 words are devoted to the woman and only 12 to the beast. But in the explanation (vs. 7–18) the angel dwells almost altogether on the beast, together with its heads and horns. In the Greek of vs. 7–18 only 36 words are devoted to the woman and 243 to the beast. This noteworthy difference between the vision and its explanation may suggest that although the announced topic of the vision is the divine sentence pronounced upon mystical Babylon, and although she proves to be the leading character in events depicted by the vision, her brief triumph and sudden fall can be understood only by a careful study of the contribution made by the beast, both to her momentary success and also to her eventual defeat.
**Was, and is not.** At some time in the past the beast had been active, but then disappeared. This expression is repeated at the close of v. 8 and again in v. 11. Some identify the “was” period of the beast with that of pagan Rome, the “is not” period with the brief interval between the end of pagan persecution and the beginning of papal persecution and the “yet is” period with that of papal Rome. Others equate the “was” period with that represented by the beast and its seven heads, the “is not” period with the interval between the wounding of the seventh head and the revival of the beast as “the eighth,” and the “yet is” period with the revival of the beast when it becomes “the eighth.” Those who hold the former view thus equate the “was” period of the beast with that of the dragon of ch. 12, whereas those who hold the latter view would include also the leopardlike beast of ch. 13. The present tense, “is not,” stresses time sequence.
**Shall ascend.** Or, “is about to ascend.” The angel still speaks of the career of the beast prior to its rising from the “bottomless pit.” At the time John saw this beast in vision it had already ascended “out of the bottomless pit.”
When the expression “was, and is not” is repeated at the close of v. 8, the words “yet is”—preferably, “is to be”—appear in place of the words “shall ascend out of the bottomless pit,” used earlier in the verse (see below on “yet is”). Accordingly, the beast “yet is” when it ascends “out of the bottomless pit.” The comparable words in this threefold sequence as given in v. 11 are, “even he is the eighth.” Therefore, when the beast ascends “out of the bottomless pit” and “yet is,” it exists as “the eighth,” literally, “an eighth.” In v. 8 the beast goes “into perdition” after ascending out of “the bottomless pit” and existing for an unspecified period of time as “the eighth.”
When the beast exists again as “the eighth,” “they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, when they behold the beast.” A remarkably similar statement is made in ch. 13:3, 8 (cf. v. 4), of the world’s attitude toward the beast of that chapter when its deadly wound is healed: “All the world wondered after the beast. … And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” If ch. 13 here refers to the same event as ch. 17:8, it follows that the statement “his deadly wound was healed” (ch. 13:3) is equivalent to the expression “shall ascend out of the bottomless pit” (ch. 17:8; cf. ch. 20:3, 7). Similarly, the words “did live” (ch. 13:14) would then be equivalent to the expressions “yet is” and “he is the eight” (ch. 17:8, 11); the wounding of the head (ch. 13:3), the going “into captivity,” and “the wound by a sword” (ch. 13:10, 14) would have their counterpart in the implied descent of the “beast” into the “bottomless pit” (ch. 17:8); and “death” (ch. 13:3) would be equivalent to the “bottomless pit” phase of the experience of the beast. The similarities here noted tend to identify the seventh head of the beast as the papal head (see on ch. 17:9, 10). However, this similarity does not necessarily prove identity. For the relationship of the beast of ch. 17 to that of ch. 13 see on ch. 17:3.
**Bottomless pit.** Gr. abussos, literally, “abyss,” implying vast, measureless space (see on Mark 5:10; Rev. 9:1). In the LXX it generally refers either to the depths of the sea or to subterranean waters. In the LXX of Ps. 71:20 and in Rom. 10:7 it is used of the underworld, or place of the dead, commonly called Hades (see on Matt. 11:23; cf. on 2 Sam. 12:23; Prov. 15:11; Isa. 14:9). Descent into the “abyss” would thus be a fitting term to represent the death of a beast that appeared to have been slain.
**Perdition.** Gr. apōleia, “utter destruction,” “annihilation” (see on John 17:12). This indicates the utter end of the beast (cf. Rev. 17:11; see on chs. 19:20; 20:10).
**They that dwell.** That is, those upon whom the “whore … sitteth” (v. 1) and who “have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication” (v. 2). Compare ch. 13:3, 4, 7, 8, 12, 14; see on ch. 17:1, 2.
**Wonder.** Gr. thaumazō, “to be amazed,” “to marvel” (see on v. 6). The people of earth are surprised beyond measure to behold the beast, which they had seen go away into the “bottomless pit” (v. 8), return and take up its former activities. They first “wonder” and then worship (see ch. 13:3, 4, 8, 12, 14), that is, yield their willing support to the beast in the pursuit of its blasphemous schemes. Concerning the relationship of the beast of ch. 17 to that of ch. 13 see on ch. 17:3.
**Not written.** That is, not listed with those whom God accepts as candidates for His kingdom.
**Book of life.** See on Phil. 4:3.
**From the foundation.** The Greek may be understood as implying that the names appearing in the book of life have been written there ever since “the foundation of the world,” or simply that the book itself has been in existence since that time. Here the latter meaning is intended. Compare on ch. 13:8.
**Yet is.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading “is to be” or “is to come.” See above on “was, and is not” and “shall ascend.”
8.zh:
你所看見的獸，先前有，如今沒有，將要從無底坑裡上來，又要歸於沉淪。凡住在地上、名字從創世以來沒有記在生命冊上的，見先前有、如今沒有、以後再有的獸，就必希奇。

**你所看見的獸。**就是第 3 節的獸。約翰所看到的獸，不是處在“先前有”和“如今沒有”的狀態，而是它復元以後的狀態。但天使簡單地解釋了這個怪獸的過去，向約翰說明了她所見之獸的身份（見 第 8–11 註釋）。
在見異象之前（第 1，2 節）和異象之中（第 3–6 節），約翰的注意力幾乎全都集中在那個女人的身上，只是偶而提到那獸。據內斯特希臘文版本，在第 1–6 節中，有 102 個詞是描寫那個女人的，只有 12 個詞是描寫獸的。但在解釋的時候（第 7–18 節），天使幾乎都是在講述獸及其頭和角。在 7–18 節中，只有 36 個詞是涉及那女人，而有 243 個詞用在解釋獸的。異象與異象解釋之間的差異，可以解釋為，雖然所宣佈異象的主題是上帝對奧秘巴比倫的宣判，雖然她是異象的主角，但她短暫的勝利和隨後突然的衰落，只有通過仔細研究獸在她的成功及最終的失敗上所起的作用才能理解。
**先前有，如今沒有.。**該獸在過去某個時期中曾十分活躍，但隨後就消失了。這句話在第 8 節的結尾和 第 11 節中重新出現。有人認為獸的“先前有”是指異教羅馬的階段，“如今沒有”是指異教逼迫結束到羅馬教開始逼迫的這個階段。“以後再有”是指羅馬教時期。也有人認為“先前有”是指獸及其七個頭；“如今沒有” 是指從第七頭受傷到獸以“第八位“的形式復活的這段時期；“以後再有”是指該獸復活為“第八位” 的階段。持第一種觀點的人認為，獸的“先前有”時期等於 啟 12 章中龍的時期。持第二種觀點的人則認為“先前有”時期還應當包括 啟 13 章中象豹的獸。“如今沒有” 強調了時間的順序。
**將要。**. . . 上來。 天使仍然在講述獸從“無底坑”上來之前的狀況。當約翰在異象中看見該獸的時候，它已經“從無底坑裡上來”了。第 8 節最後在重複“先前有，如今沒有”的時候，用“以後再有”來代替前面“將要從無底坑裡上來” （見下面“以後再有”的註釋）。因此該獸“從無底坑裡上來”之後就進入“以後再有” 的階段。 “以後再有”在第 11 節中的對應詞語是“第八位。” 所以當該獸“從無底坑裡上來” 並“以後再有” 時，它就是以“第八位” 的身份存在了。第 8 節的獸“從無底坑裡上來”以後，要以“第八位”的身份存留一段時間，然後“要歸於沉淪。”
當該獸再以“第八位”的身份出現時，“凡住在地上名字從創世以來沒有記在生命冊上的，見先前有，如今沒有，以後再有的獸，就必希奇。”這句話與 啟 13:3，8 （參 第 4 節）驚人地相似。啟 13:3，8 描寫了世人對第 13 章的獸死傷醫好的反應：“全地的人，都希奇跟從那獸。…凡住在地上，名字從創世以來，沒有記在被殺之羔羊生命冊上的人，都要拜它。” 如果 啟 13 章指的是與 啟 17:8 相同的事件，那麼可以說“死傷 . . . 醫好” （啟 13:3） 就相當於“從無底坑裡上來” （啟 17:8；參 啟 20:3，7）；“還活著”（啟 13:14） 相當於“以後再有” 和“第八位” （啟 17:8，11）； “被擄掠，”和“受刀傷” （啟 13:10，14）相當於文中所暗示的“獸”下到“無底坑”（啟 17:8）；頭受了死傷 （啟 13:3）相當於獸被拘禁在“無底坑”裡。根據上述的相似性，獸的第七個頭似乎是指羅馬教（見 啟 17:9，10 註釋）。但相似並不一定就是相同。關於 啟 17 章中獸與 啟 13 章中獸的關係，見 啟 17:3 註釋。
**無底坑。**abussos，直譯為“深淵，”暗示遼闊無垠的空間（見可 5:10；啟 9:1 註釋）。在七十士譯本里，該詞一般指海洋或地下水。在七十士譯本的 詩 71:20 以及在 羅 10:7 中，該詞指陰間，即死人的所在，通常稱為地獄（見 太 11:23 註釋；參 撒下 12:23；箴 15:11；賽 14:9 註釋）。所以下到“無底坑” 代表受了死傷之獸的死。
**沉淪。**apoµleia，“毀滅，”“滅絕”（見 約 17:12註釋），表示獸的徹底滅亡（參 啟 17:11；見 啟 19:20；20:10 註釋）。
**凡住在地上的。**指那些讓“大淫婦” 騎在身上 （第 1 節），和“喝醉了她淫亂的酒”的人（第 2 節）。 參 啟 13:3，4，7，8，12，14；見 啟 17:1，2 註釋。
**從創世以來。**原文既可理解為生命冊上的名字從“創世以來”就記在上面，也可理解為生命冊從“創世以來”就已存在。本節傾向於後一種意思。參 啟 13:8 註釋。
**沒有記在。**就是沒有列在上帝準備接納為天國公民的名單之內。
**生命冊。**見 腓 4:3 註釋。
**以後再有。**參 以上“先前有，如今沒有”及“將要 . . . 上來”的註釋。
**希奇。**“驚訝，”“吃驚”（見 第 6 節註釋）。地上的人看見獸時非常驚訝。因為他們曾看見它落到“無底坑”中（第 8 節），現在又看到它上來恢復以前的活動。他們先是“希奇，” 然後是敬拜它（參 啟 13:3，4，8，12，14），心甘情願支持獸實施褻瀆上帝的計劃。關於 啟 17 章的獸與 啟 13 章的獸之間的關係 ，見 啟 17:3 註釋。

1.en:
**One of the seven angels.** See on ch. 1:11; cf. ch. 21:9. The identification of this angel as one of the seven plague-bearing angels of chs. 15 and 16 implies that the information about to be imparted to John is related to the seven last plagues. This relationship is confirmed by the fact that the announced topic of this chapter—“the judgment of the great whore”—takes place under the seventh plague (see ch. 16:19).
**Vials.** See on chs. 15:7; 16:1.
**Talked with me.** The Greek word translated “with” (meta) may be understood as implying an intimate relationship between John and the angel. Possibly the angel addressed John before taking him off in vision. See on ch. 1:2, 10.
**Come hither.** Or, “Here” The expression has the force of an imperative. See on v. 3.
**I will shew unto thee.** See on chs. 1:2; 4:1.
**Judgment.** Gr. krima, “sentence,” “decision,” “verdict,” “decree,” here of the heavenly assize with respect to “the great whore,” in view of her criminal course of action (see on vs. 4–6; cf. on ch. 18:10). Note that the angel does not show John the execution of the sentence, or he would have used the word krisis, which word is translated “judgment” in ch. 18:10. He simply tells him of it. Krisis may indicate either the act of investigating a case or the act of carrying out the sentence. See on chs. 16:19; 18:5; 19:2; cf. Isa. 23:11.
Chapter 17 consists of two distinct parts: (1) the symbolic vision of vs. 3–6, which John saw, and (2) what he was told (v. 7) in explanation of it as recorded in vs. 8–18. Part one sets forth the crimes of Babylon, and thus constitutes Heaven’s bill of indictment, a declaration of why the divine sentence is to be pronounced upon her (see on v. 6). Part two sets forth the sentence itself and the means by which it is to be executed. Babylon’s criminal career reaches a climax under the sixth plague (see on ch. 16:12–16), whereas the sentence decreed is executed under the seventh (see on chs. 16:17–19; 17:13–17; 18:4, 8; 19:2). Accordingly, part one is concerned most particularly with events under the sixth plague, and part two with those under the seventh. Thus ch. 17 is a delineation of the final crisis, when Satan puts forth his supreme effort to annihilate God’s people (cf. ch. 12:17) and when all the powers of earth are arrayed against them (cf. GC 634). God permits Satan and the human agencies allied with him to carry forward to the verge of success their plot to annihilate the saints. But at the moment the blow is to be struck God intervenes to deliver His people. The hosts of evil, arrested in the very act of attempting to slay the saints, stand without excuse before the bar of divine justice (see Dan. 12:1; cf. EW 282–285; GC 635, 636; LS 117). Little wonder that John was filled with amazement as he beheld the climax of the great drama of the mystery of iniquity (see on ch. 17:6).
**Whore.** Gr. pornē, “prostitute,” “harlot.” Pornē probably goes back to a word meaning “to sell” or “to export for sale” such things as slaves. In Greece prostitutes were usually purchased slaves. The OT prophets often compare apostate Israel, which repeatedly went “a whoring” after heathen gods (Eze. 23:30; cf. Isa. 23:17; see on Eze. 16:15), with an adulterous woman. Concerning mystical Babylon as a harlot see on Rev. 17:5 (cf. vs. 2, 4; ch. 19:2). For OT passages whose thought or wording is similar to that of Rev. 17 see on Isa. 47:1; Jer. 25:12; 50:1; Eze. 26:13.
**Sitteth upon many waters.** That is, exercises despotic power over many “peoples” and “nations” (see v. 15). The form of the verb in Greek presents the “great whore” as in power at the time and as continuing to exercise power. As the ancient city of Babylon was situated upon the literal waters of the Euphrates (see on Jer. 50:12, 38) and dwelt figuratively “upon many waters,” or peoples (Jer. 51:12, 13; cf. Isa. 8:7, 8; 14:6; Jer. 50:23), so modern Babylon is represented as sitting upon, or oppressing, the peoples of earth (cf. on Rev. 16:12).
1.zh:
拿著七碗的七位天使中，有一位前來對我說：你到這裡來，我將坐在眾水上的大淫婦所要受的刑罰指給你看。

**碗。**見 啟 15:7；16:1 註釋。
**七位天使中，有一位。**見 啟 1:11 註釋；參 啟 21:9。這是 啟 15，16 章中傾倒七災的七位天使之一，暗示即將傳給約翰的信息與最後的七災有關。本章所宣告的主題：在第七災時“大淫婦所要受的刑罰” （參 啟 16:19），進一步證實了這種關係。
**對我說。**“對”的原文 （meta） 暗示了天使與約翰的親密關係。很可能，天使可能在帶約翰進入異象之前，先對他說話。見 啟 1:2，10 註釋。
**到這裡來。**這是祈使語氣的句子。見 第 3 節註釋。
**我將 . . . 指給你看。**見 啟 1:2；4:1 註釋。
**坐在眾水上。**就是對“多人多國”實施專制（參 第 15 節）。希臘動詞的形式表明“大淫婦”當時正得勢，而且將繼續得勢。正如古代的巴比倫坐落在幼法拉底河畔 （見 耶 50:12，38 註釋），並象徵性地坐在“眾水” 即多民之上（耶 51:12，13；參 賽 8:7，8；14:6；耶 50:23），照樣，現代的巴比倫也被描寫成騎在地上萬民之上，即壓迫地上的萬民（參 啟 16:12 註釋）。
**淫婦。**porneµ，“妓女”。該詞可能追溯到一個表示“出售”或“出口銷售”的詞，如出售奴隸等。在希臘，妓女通常是買來的奴隸。《舊約》的先知們常常把背道的以色列比作淫婦，因為她不斷地“行邪淫，”隨從異教的假神（結 23:30；參 賽 23:17；見 結 16:15 註釋）。關於奧秘之巴比倫是淫婦，見 啟 17:5 註釋（參啟 17: 2，4 ；啟 19:2）。關於《舊約》中與 啟 17 章用語或觀念相似的經文，見  賽 47:1；耶 25:12；50:1；結 26:13 註釋。
**刑罰。**krima，“判決，”“決定，” “裁斷，”“法令”。這是上天對“大淫婦”罪行的判決（見 第 4–6 註釋；參 啟 18:10 註釋）。請注意，天使並沒有向約翰展示判決的執行，否則他就會用krisis一詞了（見 啟 18:10）。他只是告訴約翰這件事。Krisis 既可表示案件的調查，也可表示判決的執行。見 啟 16:19；18:5；19:2 註釋；參 賽 23:11。
第 17 章分成兩個部分：一， 第 3–6 節的象徵性異像是約翰所看見的。二，在第 8–18 節中天使向約翰解釋了 （第 7 節）所見的異象。第一部分揭露了巴比倫的罪行。因此它是上天的訴狀，說明宣判她的理由（見 第 6 節註釋）。第二部分宣佈了判決，以及執行判決的方法。巴比倫的罪孽在第六災時已經是登峰造極的了（參 啟 16:12–16 的註釋）。判決的執行乃是在第七災之下（見 啟 16:17–19；17:13–17；18:4，8；19:2 註釋）。因此第一部分主要涉及第六災下的事件，而第二部分則涉及第七災下的事件。啟 17 章就這樣描述了最後的危機。那時撒但將千方百計要消滅上帝的子民（見 啟 12:17）。地上的各種勢力將起來攻擊他們（參 《善惡之爭》 第634頁）。上帝允許撒但及其人間的黨羽將消滅聖徒的陰謀實施到幾乎成功。但就在那危急的關頭，上帝進行了干預，拯救了祂的子民。邪惡的軍隊正要殺害聖徒的時候受到了制止。他們在上帝公義的審判臺前是無法推諉的（參見但 12:1；參 《早期著作》第 282–285 頁；《善惡之爭》 第635，636頁；《懷氏傳略》第 117 頁）。難怪當約翰看到不法的隱意充分表現之時，會感到驚訝（見 啟 17:6 註釋）。

5.en:
**Forehead.** The character reflected by the name “Babylon” is the woman’s considered choice. This may be implied by the fact that the name appears on her forehead. Compare on ch. 13:16.
**Was a name written.** Rather, “a name stands written,” that is, it had been written there in the past and remains there. The name reflects character.
**Mystery.** This word is descriptive of the title, not part of it; hence the appropriateness of the term “mystical Babylon” (see on ch. 1:20).
**Babylon the great.** Although, in one sense, mystical Babylon may be considered as representative of apostate religious systems throughout history, “Babylon the great” in the book of Revelation designates, in a special sense, the united apostate religions at the close of time (see on chs. 14:8; 16:13, 14; 18:24). In ch. 17:18 mystical Babylon is called “that great city” (cf. chs. 16:19; 18:18). Here, doubtless, Babylon is referred to as “great” in view of the fact that this chapter deals most particularly with Satan’s great final effort to secure the allegiance of the human race through religion. “Babylon the great” is the name by which Inspiration refers to the great threefold religious union of the papacy, apostate Protestantism, and spiritism (see on ch. 16:13, 18, 19; cf. on chs. 14:8; 18:2; cf. GC 588; Dan. 4:30; Zech. 10:2, 3; 11:3–9). The term “Babylon” refers to the organizations themselves and to their leaders, not so much to the members as such. The latter are referred to as “many waters” (Rev. 17:1, 15) and as the “inhabitants of the earth” (v. 2; cf. v. 8).
**Mother of harlots.** As already noted, “Babylon the great” includes apostate Protestantism at the time here envisioned. The daughters of this “mother” thus represent the various religious bodies that constitute apostate Protestantism.
**Abominations.** See on v. 4.
5.zh:
在他額上有名寫著說：奧秘哉！大巴比倫，作世上的淫婦和一切可憎之物的母。

**額上。**“巴比倫”這個名字所反映的品格是這個女人深思熟慮的選擇。這或許就是名字寫在她額上的原因。參 啟 13:16 註釋。
**有名寫著說。**即過去寫在上面，現在依然存在。名字是品格的反映。
**奧秘。**這是名號的全部，而不是名號的一部分。所以稱她為“奧秘之巴比倫”十分合適（見 啟 1:20 註釋）。
**大巴比倫。**雖然從某種意義上說，奧秘的巴比倫可以被看成代表歷代以來所有背道的宗教體系，但從特殊意義上說，《啟示錄》的“大巴比倫”主要代表在末時聯合起來的背道宗教（見 啟 14:8；16:13，14；18:24 註釋）。在 啟 17:18 中，奧秘的巴比倫被稱為“大城”（參 啟 16:19；18:18）。稱巴比倫為“大”，無疑是因為本章所敘述的，主要是撒但藉助宗教來確保人類效忠的最後掙扎。“大巴比倫” 就是靈感之筆所說的羅馬教，背道的基督教和招魂術三合一宗教聯盟（見 啟 16:13，18，19 註釋；參 啟 14:8；18:2 註釋；參 《善惡之爭》 第588頁；但 4:30；亞 10:2，3；11:3–9）。“巴比倫”一詞指的是這些組織本身及其領袖，而不是這些組織的成員。這些成員則被稱為“眾水”（啟 17:1，15） 和“住在地上的人”（第 2 節；參 第 8 節）。
**淫婦。**. . . 母。 如上所述，“大巴比倫”包括這裡所預言的背道的基督教。因此，這位“母”親的女兒們自然代表組成背道改正教的各宗教團體。
**可憎之物。**見 第 4 節註釋。

15.en:
**He saith unto me.** See on ch. 17:1.
**Waters.** See on v. 1. For other instances of waters as a symbol for human beings see on Isa. 8:7; Dan. 7:2.
**Sitteth.** Or, “is sitting.” Here the angel again refers to what John saw in vs. 3–6, within the time period specified by vs. 11–13 (see comment there).
15.zh:
天使又對我說，你所看見那淫婦坐的眾水，就是多民、多人、多國、多方。

**天使又對我說。**見 啟 17:1 註釋。
**坐。**或“正在坐”。天使再次提到約翰在 第 3–6 節所看到的情景。該情景發生在在 第 11–13 所指的時期（見該處註釋）。
**眾水。**見 第 1 節註釋。關於眾水象徵人群，見 賽 8:7；但 7:2 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第440頁。

2.en:
**Kings of the earth.** That is, the political powers of earth (see on v. 12), which place their authority and resources at the disposal of the “great whore” (v. 1; see on v. 13) and through which she designs to realize her ambition to slay all of God’s people (see on vs. 6, 14) and to rule over the “inhabitants of the earth” (cf. v. 8). The “kings of the earth” are her accomplices in crime.
**Committed fornication.** Gr. porneuō, the related verb form of pornē (see on v. 1). This expression is equivalent to “gone a whoring” in the OT (cf. Eze. 23:30; Hosea 4:12). Used figuratively, as here, it refers to an illicit alliance of professed Christians with some master other than Christ, in this instance to a religio-political compact between an apostate church (see on Rev. 17:5) and the nations of earth. Compare Isa. 23:15, 17.
**Inhabitants.** As a result of the course followed by their leaders, the inhabitants of the earth are deceived (cf. on v. 8) into cooperating with the policy of the “great whore” (cf. ch. 13:8).
**Made drunk.** That is, completely intoxicated. The normal powers of reason and judgment have been stupefied and the spiritual perception benumbed. Compare Jer. 51:7; 2 Thess. 2:9, 10; Rev. 13:3, 4, 7, 18; 14:8; 18:3; 19:20. It may be noted that here the intoxication of the inhabitants of earth is mentioned following reference to the illicit alliance between Babylon and the kings of the earth. Apparently Babylon acts through the kings of the earth to gain control of those inhabitants of earth who have not already voluntarily submitted to her. Rulers and subjects are alike deceived (GC 624).
**With the wine.** That is, by drinking the wine. This “wine” is Satan’s deceptive policy of uniting all the world under his control, together with the falsehoods and “miracles” by which he advances his policy (cf. chs. 13:13, 14; 18:23; 19:20).
**Of her fornication.** Or, “[which is] her prostitution.” The alliance between apostate Christianity and the political powers of earth is the means by which Satan proposes to unite the world under his leadership.
2.zh:
地上的君王與他行淫，住在地上的人喝醉了他淫亂的酒。

**地上的君王。**就是地上的政治勢力（見 第 12 節註釋），將自己的權力和資源都交給“大淫婦”支配（第 1 節；參 第 13 節註釋）。她要藉著他們實施根除上帝子民的野心（見 第 6，14 節註釋），並統治“住在地上” 的人（參 第 8 節）。“地上的君王”是她犯罪的幫兇。
**行淫。**porneuoµ，是 porneµ （見 第 1 節註釋）的動詞形式。 其含義與《舊約》中的“行淫”是一樣的（參 結 23:30；何 4:12）。但在本節裡是寓指自稱基督徒的人與他人進行不正當的勾結，也就是背道的教會（見 啟 17:5 註釋）與地上各國的同盟。參 賽 23:15，17。
**住在地上的人。**由於領袖們所採取的行徑，地上的居民受迷惑（見 第 8 節註釋）配合“大淫婦” 的策略（參 啟 13:8）。
**喝醉了。**正常的思維和判斷能力，屬靈的識別力都麻木了。參 耶 51:7；帖後 2:9，10；啟 13:3，4，7，18；14:8；18:3；19:20。可以看出，本節提到地上居民的醉酒是在巴比倫與地上的君王非法結盟之後。巴比倫顯然是通過地上的君王，來控制本來不願服從她的地上居民。統治者和被統治者都受了迷惑（《善惡之爭》 第624頁）。
**她淫亂的。**背道的基督教與地上的政權結盟，成了撒但用來控制全世界的工具。
**酒。**這“酒”就是撒但把全世界聯合起來受他控制之下的騙局，包括推行他策略的各種邪術和“奇事”（參 啟 13:13，14；18:23；19:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第536頁。

4.en:
**The woman.** See on v. 3.
**Purple and scarlet.** Compare Eze. 27:7; Rev. 18:7, 12, 16, 17, 19. These were the colors of royalty (see on Matt. 27:28), to which this “woman” laid clam (cf. Rev. 18:7). Scarlet may also considered the color of sin and of a prostitute (see on ch. 17:3). This prostitute, this apostate religious organization, depicted in all her seductiveness, s gaudily dressed and vulgarly bedecked. She stands forth in striking contrast with “bride” of the Lamb, whom John saw arrayed in fine line, clean and white (see ch. 19:7, 8; cf. 1T 136; Ed 248). See on Luke 16:19.
**Abominations and filthiness of her fornication.** Or, “unclean acts, even the filthiness which is her fornication.” The gold of the cup deceives men with respect to the nature of the contents. See on v. 2.
4.zh:
那女人穿著紫色和朱紅色的衣服，用金子、寶石、珍珠為妝飾；手拿金盃，杯中盛滿了可憎之物，就是他淫亂的汙穢。

**那女人。**見 第 3 節註釋。
**紫色和硃紅色。**參 結 27:7；啟 18:7，12，16，17，19。紫色和硃紅色是皇家的顏色 （見 太 27:28 註釋），這“女人”聲稱自己出自皇家（參 啟 18:7）。硃紅色也可以視為罪和妓女的顏色（參 啟 17:3 註釋）。這個勾引人的妓女，也就是背道的宗教組織，穿著妖嬈，打扮俗麗，與約翰所見身著潔白光明之細麻衣的羔羊“新娘”形成了鮮明的對比（見 啟 19:7，8；參 《證言》 卷一第 136 頁；《教育論》第248頁）。 見 路 16:19 註釋。
**可憎之物，就是她淫亂的汙穢。**或 “不潔的行為，就是她淫亂的汙穢。”金盃以其所盛之物迷惑人。見 第 2 節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–6節）**。《善惡之爭》第382頁。

3.zh:
我被聖靈感動，天使帶我到曠野去，我就看見一個女人騎在朱紅色的獸上；那獸有七頭十角，遍體有褻瀆的名號。

**被聖靈感動。**直譯為“在靈裡”（見 啟 1:10 註釋；參 啟 4:2；21:10）。 原文的“靈”不用定冠詞是強調這個經驗的性質。
**帶我。**. . . 去。這一感動無疑是為了幫助讓約翰的心從目前的時間和地點，轉移到了異象之中（參 結 3:12–14；8:3；40:2，3；啟 21:10）。
**曠野。**“荒涼之地” （見 啟 12:6 註釋）。啟 17:16 中的相關動詞意為“使荒涼，”“使成為廢墟，”“剝光，”“遺棄。”“曠野”是杳無人煙之域。那裡的生存條件非常艱苦和危險。食物，住處，可能還有飲水，都很難得到，再加上野獸和盜匪出沒。因此有人認為 “曠野” 在這裡是寓指上帝的子民所處的艱難和危險（見 第 6，14 節）。在希臘文中，“曠野”前面沒有定冠詞，說明它是泛指一種狀態，而不是具體的地點。
鑑於啟 17 章主要涉及最後七災的時期（參 第 1 節），有人認為這裡的“曠野”是指上帝的子民在那時的經歷。本節的描寫與 啟 12:6，13–16 的“曠野”相似，但不相同。
**女人。**《舊約》的先知經常把上帝背道的子民比作淫婦（參 結 16:15–58；23:2–21；何 2:5；3:1等）。這個“女人”是“大淫婦”（啟 17:1），即奧秘的“大巴比倫”（第 5 節），沾滿“地上一切被殺之人的血”（啟 18:24），顯然存在於整個人類的歷史。奧秘之巴比倫可能包括自古以來所有與上帝作對的宗教組織，但在本節主要指末世的時候，（見 啟 17:5 註釋）。
**騎在。**該動詞的形式表示持續的動作。 第 1 節說“大淫婦”直接在宗教上控制每一個人。這裡又說她在指導政府的政策（見 第 18 節註釋）。背道基督教的特徵就是政教聯合，為了鞏固宗教對國家政策的控制（參 卷 4，第 837 頁）。參考我們主所宣佈祂的“國” 不屬 “這世界”（約 18:36）。
**硃紅色。**豔麗奪目的色彩。在 賽 1:18中，硃紅色代表罪。參 啟 12:3 的“大紅龍。”
**七頭。**見 第 9–11 節註釋。關於古代神話中的七頭獸，見 賽 27:1 註釋。
**十角。**見 第 12–14，17 註釋。
**獸。**在聖經的預言中，獸通常代表政治勢力（但 7:3–7，17；8:3，5，20，21；參 啟 12:3；13:1）。該獸的顏色表明它是邪惡的化身。它身上遍佈褻瀆的名號，說明它是與上帝為敵的。因此這個獸代表撒但。歷代以來，他利用這些受他控制的政治機構來作工。
這個獸在某些方面像啟 12:3 的大紅龍，在其他方面則像啟 13:1，2 那個類似豹的獸（見兩處註釋）。根據上下文，該獸與後者更像一些。啟 13 章 的獸和 啟 17 章的獸之間最大的差異，在於前者代表羅馬教，是政教不分的；但在 啟 17 章中，這兩者是分明的。獸代表的是政治勢力，女人則代表宗教勢力。
**遍體。**它背叛和反對上帝，已經惡貫滿盈了。
**褻瀆的名號。**見 可 2:7；7:2註釋。在 啟 13:1 中（見該節註釋），褻瀆的名號是在七頭上；而在本節，褻瀆的名號遍佈獸的全身。這些名號代表獸的本性，就是妄想篡奪上帝的權威。“遍體有褻瀆的名號”表明它一心致力於這個目標。參 賽 14:13，14；耶 50:29，31；但 7:8，11，20，25；11:36，37。
3.en:
**Carried me away.** The sensation of motion was doubtless designed to aid John in making the mental transition from his own time and place to those of the vision (cf. Eze. 3:12–14; 8:3; 40:2, 3; Rev. 21:10).
**In the spirit.** Literally, “in spirit” (see on ch. 1:10; cf. chs. 4:2; 21:10). The absence of the definite article in Greek stresses the quality, or nature, of the experience.
**The wilderness.** Gr. erēmos, “a desolate place” (see on ch. 12:6). The related verb used in ch. 17:16 means “to desolate,” “to lay waste,” “to strip bare,” “to abandon.” A “wilderness” was an uninhabited region where life could be sustained only amid difficulty and danger. Food, shelter, and possibly even water would be difficult to obtain, and there would be danger from wild animals and perhaps from brigands. Accordingly, some consider that when used figuratively, as here, a “wilderness” would be a situation fraught with difficulty and danger, apparently for God’s people (see vs. 6, 14). Absence of the definite article before the word “wilderness,” in the Greek, clearly makes the term qualitative and descriptive. In other words, it specifies a condition rather than a particular location.
In view of the fact that ch. 17 appears to deal most particularly with the time of the seven last plagues (see on v. 1), some hold that the “wilderness” situation here referred to is descriptive of the experience of God’s people at that time. The situation here depicted is similar to, but not to be identified with, that of the “wilderness” of ch. 12:6, 13–16.
**Woman.** The OT prophets repeatedly represent an apostate people as a licentious woman (cf. Eze. 16:15–58; 23:2–21; Hosea 2:5; 3:1; etc.). This “woman”—the “great whore” (Rev. 17:1), or mystical “Babylon the great” (v. 5)—is guilty of “the blood … of all that were slain upon the earth” (ch. 18:24), apparently throughout history. Mystical Babylon constitutes the organized religious opposition to God’s people, probably from the beginning of time, but here, particularly, at its very close (see on ch. 17:5).
**Sit.** The form of the verb denotes continuing action. In v. 1 the “great whore” is represented as being in direct control of men as individuals, religiously, and here as directing the policies of civil government (see on v. 18). It has ever been characteristic of apostate Christianity to attempt a union of church and state, in order to consolidate religious control over public policy (cf. Vol. IV, p. 837). Compare the declaration of our Lord that His “kingdom” is not “of this world” (John 18:36).
**Scarlet.** Or, “crimson,” a brilliant color certain to attract attention. In Isa. 1:18 scarlet is the color of sin. Compare the “great red dragon” of Rev. 12:3.
**Beast.** In Bible prophecy beasts commonly represent political powers (Dan. 7:3–7, 17; 8:3, 5, 20, 21; cf. Rev. 12:3; 13:1). The color of this beast may intimate that it is the epitome of evil, as the names of blasphemy with which it is covered indicate that it stands in opposition to God. Accordingly, the beast itself may be identified as Satan working through those political agencies, in all ages, that have submitted to his control.
In certain respects this beast resembles the great red dragon of ch. 12:3, and in others the leopardlike beast of ch. 13:1, 2 (see respective comments.) The context makes the latter relationship appear to be closer. The chief difference between the beast of ch. 13 and that of ch. 17 is that in the former, which is identified with the papacy, no distinction is made between the religious and the political aspects of papal power, whereas in the latter the two are distinct—the beast representing political power and the woman, religious power.
**Full.** Apostasy and opposition to God are complete.
**Names of blasphemy.** Or, “blasphemous names” (see on Mark 2:7; 7:2). In Rev. 13:1 (see comment there) the names are on the seven heads; here, they are scattered over the entire beast. These names indicate the character of the beast—it presumes to usurp the prerogative of Deity. That it is “full” of blasphemous names indicates that it is wholly devoted to this objective. Compare Isa. 14:13, 14; Jer. 50:29, 31; Dan. 7:8, 11, 20, 25; 11:36, 37.
**Seven heads.** See on vs. 9–11. For seven-headed beasts in ancient mythology see on Isa. 27:1.
**Ten horns.** See on vs. 12–14, 17.

6.zh:
我又看見那女人喝醉了聖徒的血和為耶穌作見證之人的血。我看見他，就大大的希奇。

**喝醉了。**見 第 2 節註釋。從廣義上說，巴比倫“喝醉”了歷代殉道者的血 （參 啟 18:24），但從更直接的意義上來說，這是指世界歷史最後幾幕中殉道，或將要殉道的聖徒。上帝認為巴比倫要對那些她下令要殺害，但因上帝的干預而未遭殺害之聖徒的血負責（見 《善惡之爭》 第628頁）。巴比倫完全陶醉在她過去逼迫聖徒所取得的成功中（見 但 7:25 ；太. 24:21；參 啟 6:9–11；18:24），陶醉在她即將完成其血腥屠殺的前景中（見 啟 16:6；17:14 註釋；參 《善惡之爭》 第628頁）。
**聖徒。**直譯為“聖潔的人”（見 徒 9:13；羅 1:7 註釋）。
**血。**見 啟 16:6 註釋。
**為耶穌。**或“作關於耶穌的見證，”先是用他們的話語，再是藉著他們的殉身。他們被殺是因為他們堅持為耶穌及其真理作見證，效忠祂的名，不惜犧牲自己的性命。
**作見證之人。**martures，也可譯為“殉道者。”（見 啟 2:13 註釋）。參 賽 47:6；耶 51:49；見 啟 18:24 註釋。
**我看見她。**不知道約翰這裡是指他在第 3–6 節中所看見的一切，還是單指她在第 6 節犯罪高潮時的行為。天使對約翰驚訝表現的回答（第 7 節），暗示可能是指前者。
**就大大第希奇。**原文反映了一個典型的希伯來用語。天使曾叫約翰來觀看對宗教淫婦巴比倫的宣判（第 1 節）。使徒可能原以為會看到一幅完全毀滅和敗落的景象，不料他卻看到了一位喝得酩酊大醉，衣著昂貴豔麗，騎在可怕怪獸身上的女人。天使曾對約翰說起過這個邪惡的“女人”（見 啟 14:8；16:18，19）。但現在展現在約翰眼前的，是她更全面，更驚人的犯罪畫面，使約翰大為希奇，遠超過了他在《啟示錄》其他地方所表現的驚訝。
天使所指控奧秘之巴比倫的罪行如下（參 啟 18:4 註釋）：
一.	引誘：她勾引地上眾王與她非法結合，以進一步滿足她罪惡的慾望（見 第 2 節；啟 18:3註釋）。
二.	壓迫：她坐在“眾水”之上，壓迫地上的百姓（見 啟 17:1 註釋）。
三.	加重人類的罪孽。她讓聖徒之外的地上百姓喝醉了她策略之酒，使他們成為她邪惡陰謀的幫兇（參 第 2 節）。她藉著 “淫亂，”“敗壞”了“世界”（啟 19:2）。
四.	醉酒。 她“喝醉了聖徒血。”他們得罪她是因為拒絕喝她邪惡之杯，拒絕屈從她統治地球的野心。
五.	謀殺和企圖謀殺。她圖謀殺害基督的新婦，就是啟 12 章中的婦人（見 啟 17:6，14；18:24 註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第59頁。
6.en:
**Drunken.** See on v. 2. Literally, “continuing in a state of intoxication.” In a general sense Babylon may be said to be “drunken” with the blood of the martyrs of all ages (cf. ch. 18:24), but in a more immediate sense with that of martyrs and prospective martyrs in the closing scenes of earth’s history. God holds Babylon accountable for the blood of those whose death she has decreed but whom she is prevented from slaying (see GC 628). Babylon is utterly intoxicated with her past success at persecuting the saints (see on Dan. 7:25; Matt. 24:21; cf. Rev. 6:9–11; 18:24), and with the prospect that soon she will have the satisfaction of completing the gory task (see on chs. 16:6; 17:14; cf. GC 628).
**Blood.** See on ch. 16:6.
**Saints.** Literally, “holy ones” (see on Acts 9:13; Rom. 1:7).
**And with the blood.** Or, “that is, with the blood.”
**Martyrs.** Gr. martures, literally, “witnesses” (see on ch. 2:13). Compare Isa. 47:6; Jer. 51:49; see on Rev. 18:24.
**Of Jesus.** Meaning, probably, “who bore witness concerning Jesus,” first by their words and then by their martyrdom. They had been slain because they persisted in witnessing for Jesus and His truth, and had been loyal to His name at the cost of their lives.
**When I saw her.** It is not clear whether this refers to all that John had seen in vs. 3–6, or only to her conduct in v. 6, the climax of her criminal career. The angel’s reply to John’s amazement (v. 7) may imply the former.
**I wondered with great admiration.** Literally, “I was amazed with great amazement,” the Greek being a reflection of a typically Hebrew idiomatic expression. The angel had called John to witness the sentence to be pronounced on Babylon, the religious prostitute (v. 1), and the apostle probably expected to see a picture of complete ruin and degradation. But, instead, he sees a woman garbed in costly and gorgeous attire, in a state of intoxication, and sitting upon a fearsome beast. An angel had already told John something about this evil “woman” (see chs. 14:8; 16:18, 19), but now he is given a more complete and startling account of her crimes. What John sees fills him with utter astonishment, far beyond anything he express elsewhere in the Revelation.
The crimes of mystical Babylon, as set forth in the angel’s indictment, may be enumerated as follows (cf. on ch. 18:4): 1. Seduction. By seducing the kings of the earth into illicit union with her, in order to further her own sinister designs (see on v. 2; ch. 18:3). 2. Oppressive despotism. By sitting upon “many waters”—oppressing the peoples of earth (see on ch. 17:1). 3. Contributing to human delinquency. By making the people of earth—except for the saints—drunk with the wine of her political policy, thus causing them to become her accomplices in her evil plot (see on v. 2). By her “fornication” she “did corrupt the earth” (ch. 19:2). 4. Drunkenness. By being “drunken with the blood of the saints,” who had offended her by refusing to drink of her evil potion of error or to submit to her ambition to rule the earth. 5. Murder and attempted murder. By plotting the murder of Christ’s bride, the “woman” of ch. 12 (see on chs. 17:6, 14; 18:24).

7.zh:
天使對我說：你為什麼希奇呢？我要將這女人和馱著他的那七頭十角獸的奧秘告訴你。

本節的“我”是強調的。本章其餘的部分是天使對“奧秘”或第 3–6 節異象意義的解釋。第 8–17 節解釋獸；第 18 節解釋“女人”。
7.en: **I will tell thee.** In the Greek the pronoun is emphatic: “I myself will tell thee.” The remainder of the chapter is the angel’s interpretation of the “mystery,” or the symbolism of the vision of vs. 3–6. The “beast” is explained in vs. 8–17, the “woman” in v. 18.

9.zh:
智慧的心在此可以思想。那七頭就是女人所坐的七座山，

**智慧的心。**參 啟 13:18。天使就這樣開始介紹 啟 17:8 中“先前有，如今沒有，以後再有的獸” 。約翰所見的是一個“奧秘”（參 第 7 節；見 第 5 節註釋），因為真相隱藏在象徵性語言中，需要有“智慧”來理解其含義。雖然天使的話可能主要是針對第 8 節奧秘，特別是第 9 節，10節的解釋，但也適合於整個異象，包括10–18 節的解釋。
**七頭。**似乎代表撒但藉以毀滅上帝在地上之子民和工作的七個主要政治勢力（見 第 2，3，6，10 節註釋）。不清楚聖靈是否以這七個頭代表歷史上的七個國家，因為在《啟示錄》中，“七”的數字往往是象徵性的，而不是真實性的（見 啟 1:11 註釋）。因此有人認為這七個頭代表歷史上所有反對上帝在地上之子民和聖工的政治勢力，不一定代表七個國家。
