**All that were slain.** Mystical Babylon represents apostate religion since the beginning of time (see on chs. 14:8; 17:5, 13). However, chs. 13 to 18 are concerned most particularly with the culmination of apostasy at the end of time. Thus, in a general sense, “all that were slain” may properly include the martyrs of all time, but emphasis here is doubtless on those who lay down their lives in the closing struggle of the great controversy between good and evil, and probably also those whom Babylon purposes to slay but is prevented from slaying, by divine intervention (see on ch. 17:6; cf. Isa. 47:6; Jer. 51:47–49).

900.zh:
奧秘之巴比倫在 啟 14 章到 19 章中扮演了主要角色，特別是在 啟 17 章和 18 章。鑑於《啟示錄》的描述主要依據《舊約》中的歷史記錄（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七 第 725 頁），特別是古代幼法拉底河畔的巴比倫是奧秘之巴比倫的預表（見 啟 14:8；17:5 的註釋），參閱《舊約》的相關經文，至少有助於部分理解奧秘之巴比倫含義。
《啟示錄》對奧秘之巴比倫的描述大都源於 賽 13；14；47；耶 25；50；51；結 26–28。關於這些經文對理解本章主題所起的作用， 見 賽 47:1；耶 25:12；50:1；結 26:13 註釋。在下面的對照表中，左欄是《啟示錄》有關奧秘之巴比倫的一系列話題，右欄是《舊約》對古巴比倫的重要描述。請注意第 五 項是例外。

Mystical Babylon plays a major role in Rev. 14 to 19, particularly chs. 17; 18. In view of the fact that the imagery of the Revelation appears to be based largely on historical parallels in the OT (see p. 725), and especially since mystical Babylon is the figurative counterpart of the ancient literal city situated on the Euphrates (see on chs. 14:8; 17:5), a comparison of relevant OT passages may be expected to clarify, at least in part, the role attributed by Inspiration to mystical Babylon.
In large measure the imagery of the Revelation concerned with mystical Babylon is drawn from Isa. 13; 14; 47; Jer. 25; 50; 51; Eze. 26–28. For an analysis of the contribution of these OT passages to the subject under consideration see on Isa. 47:1; Jer. 25:12; 50:1; Eze. 26:13. In the following comparative table, the left-hand column consists of a composite, topical series of statements in the Revelation concerning mystical Babylon. The right-hand column lists the more significant OT passages dealing with ancient Babylon. Note the one exception—No. 5.

8.en:
**But.** A strong contrast is now presented.
**Fearful.** Gr. deiloi, “cowardly,” “fearful.” The word is always used in the evil sense of cowardice, or unwarranted timidity. Compare its use in Matt. 8:26; Mark 4:40; the related verb in John 14:27; and the related abstract noun in 2 Tim. 1:7. In each instance cowardice is the basic meaning. Owing to cowardice, moral faintheartedness, many fail to overcome in the Christian warfare; they give up in the time of trial. Compare Matt. 24:13.
**Unbelieving.** That is, those who lack faith, in the sense of not remaining faithful. They do not trust God to the end; they prove to be untrustworthy.
**Abominable.** Gr. bdelussō, “to make foul,” “to turn away in disgust from,” “to detest,” related to the verb bdeō, “to stink.” The noun bdelugma occurs in Luke 16:15; Rev. 17:4, 5; 21:27.
**Murderers.** These include the persecutors and murderers of God’s faithful children throughout history.
**Whoremongers.** Gr. pornoi, “fornicators” (see 1 Cor. 5:9, 10; etc.). The feminine form is translated “harlots” in Matt. 21:31, 32; Luke 15:30. Compare on Eph. 5:3, 5.
**Sorcerers.** Gr. pharmakoi, “practicers of magical arts.” Basically, the root refers to magic, enchantment, sorcery, and to the use of drugs to produce a stupefied condition. A modern counterpart of the ancient practice of sorcery is spiritism.
**Idolaters.** A reference to heathen peoples, as well as to Christians who practice heathenish rites. Compare on 1 Cor. 5:10; 6:9; 10:7.
**Liars.** Including those who preach false doctrines. See on Ex. 20:16; see PP 309.
**Second death.** See on ch. 20:6.
8.zh:
惟有膽怯的、不信的、可憎的、殺人的、淫亂的、行邪術的、拜偶像的，和一切說謊話的，他們的分就在燒著硫磺的火湖裡；這是第二次的死。

唯有。 這裡表現出強烈的對比。
**膽怯的。**“怯懦的，” “膽小的。” 形容怯懦或毫無根據的膽怯。參該詞用於  太 8:26；可 4:40 ；其相關的動詞用於 約 14:27 ；其相關的抽象名詞用於 提後 1:7 。在上述經文中，膽怯均為基本的含義。由於膽怯和道德上的懦弱，許多人未能在基督徒的戰爭中得勝，在試煉的時候放棄了信仰。參 太 24:13。
**不信的。**就是缺乏信心，不保持忠心的人。他們沒有信靠上帝到底，所以證明為不值得信任的。
**可憎的。**bdelussoµ，““弄髒，”“厭惡，” 相關動詞為 bdeoµ（“發出臭味”）。其名詞形式為 bdelugma ，出現在 路 16:15；啟 17:4，5；21:27中。
**殺人的。**包括歷代逼迫和殺害上帝忠心兒女的人。
**淫亂的。**“私通者” ，見 林前 5:9，10等。 該詞的陰性形式在太 21:31，32；路 15:30 中譯為“妓女。” 參 弗 5:3，5 註釋。
**行邪術的。**其詞根的基本含義是魔術，邪術和巫術，以及使用藥物產生迷幻的狀態。古代邪術的現代形式是招魂術。
**拜偶像的。**指外邦人和參加異教活動的基督徒。參 林前 5:10；6:9；10:7註釋。
**說謊話的。**包括傳假道的人。見 出 20:16 註釋；見 《先祖與先知》第 309頁。
**第二次的死。**見 啟 20:6 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷二第630頁；《證言》卷四第336頁。

2.en:
**Holy city.** Ancient Jerusalem contained the Temple, where God could manifest His presence to His people (1 Kings 8:10, 11; 2 Chron. 5:13, 14; 7:2, 3), even as He had done at the door of the tabernacle in the desert (Ex. 29:43–46; 40:34–38). The city was described as “holy” (Dan. 9:24; Matt. 27:53), but in the course of time the spiritual degradation of God’s people became so great that Jesus pronounced the Temple a “den of thieves” (Matt. 21:13), and predicted the fall of the city (Matt. 22:7; Luke 21:20). Now God promises a new kind of Jerusalem, which John describes as the “new Jerusalem.”
**New.** Gr. kainos, new in kind and quality (see on v. 1). Compare Gal. 4:26; Heb. 11:10; 12:22; 13:14.
**Coming down.** In vision John beheld the city as it descended (cf. PP 62).
**From God.** God is the author, the originator, the source.
**Out of heaven.** Its place of origin (cf. chs. 3:12; 21:10).
**Prepared.** The form of the word thus translated suggests that the preparation had been initiated in the past and brought to perfection, so that the city now stands fully prepared (cf. GC 645, 648).
**Bride.** The city is here represented as the bride (see on ch. 19:7).
**Adorned.** Gr. kosmeō, “to arrange,” “to furnish,” “to adorn.” The English word “cosmetics” is derived from kosmeō. The form of the Greek verb suggests that the adorning had begun in the past and had by now been brought to completion.
**Husband.** That is, the Lamb, Christ (ch. 19:7).
2.zh:
我又看見聖城新耶路撒冷由神那裡從天而降，預備好了，就如新婦妝飾整齊，等候丈夫。

**聖城。**古代的耶路撒冷包括聖殿在內。上帝在那裡向祂的子民顯現（王上 8:10，11；代下 5:13，14；7:2，3），就像祂在曠野的會幕門口所行的那樣 （出 29:43–46；40:34–38）。該城原被稱為“聖” 的（但 9:24；太 27:53），但隨著時間的流逝，因上帝的子民在屬靈上退化墮落，後來耶穌竟宣佈它為“賊窩” （太 21:13），並預言了它的毀滅（太 22:7；路 21:20）。 現在上帝應許將有一座新的耶路撒冷城。約翰稱之為“新耶路撒冷。”
**新。**指品質上的“新”（見 第 1 節註釋）。參 加 4:26；來 11:10；12:22；13:14。
**由上帝那裡。**上帝是創創者，是根源。
**從天。**聖城是從天而降的（參 啟 3:12；21:10）。
**而降。**在異象中，約翰看見聖城正從天而降（參 《先祖與先知》 第 62頁）。
**預備好了.。**譯文暗示準備工作是從過去開始，現已完成。這座城市完全預備好了（參《善惡之爭》第645，648頁）。
**新婦。**本節把聖城比作新娘（見 啟 19:7 註釋）。
裝飾。  kosmeoµ，“整理，”“佈置，”“打扮。”英語中的“化妝，”（“cosmetics”）， 源於該詞。 原文的動詞形式表明裝飾是從過去開始的，現已完成。
**丈夫。**就是羔羊基督（啟 19:7）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第591頁；《早期著作》第18，31，291頁；《善惡之爭》第427，663頁。

3.en:
**Great voice.** The speaker is not identified. It is presumably not God, for He is spoken of in the third person.
**Tabernacle.** Gr. skēnē, “tent,” “booth,” “tabernacle.” The verb skēnoō, “to tent,” “to dwell,” appears in John 1:14: “The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us” (see comment there). This visible presence of God was made plain by the Shekinah in the days of the theocracy, and later by the personal appearance of Jesus Christ as a member of the human family, dwelling among men. The great voice from heaven now stresses the wonderful fact of a new creation and of God dwelling personally with His people.
**With men.** Later in the verse the phrase “with them” appears twice. Three times in this verse the apostle uses the preposition “with,” thereby stressing the amazing fact of God keeping company with men throughout eternity, making His home with them.
**Dwell.** Gr. skēnoō (see above on “tabernacle”). With this verse compare Eze. 37:27. Ezekiel describes conditions as they might have been; John, conditions as they will be fulfilled.
3.zh:
我聽見有大聲音從寶座出來說：看哪，神的帳幕在人間。他要與人同住，他們要作他的子民。神要親自與他們同在，作他們的神。

**大聲音。**未能確認發聲者。大概不是上帝，因為這裡用第三人稱來稱呼上帝。
**帳幕。**skeµneµ，“帳篷，” “棚子，” “小房間。” 其動詞形式 skeµnooµ，（“支搭帳篷，” “居住” ）出現在 約 1:14中：“道成了肉身住在我們中間”（見該節註釋）。上帝的臨格在神權時期曾藉著施恩座上的榮光顯示出來，後來又藉著耶穌降世為人，住在世人中間表現出來。現在從天上來的大聲音強調了新造和上帝親自與祂子民人同居的奇妙事實。
**與人。**本節兩次出現“他們” ，兩次出現“與” ，強調上帝永遠與人同在，住在他們中間的奇妙事實。
**同在。**skeµnooµ （見 上面 “帳幕”註釋）。請將本節與結 37:27進行對照。以西結所描述的是可能性，而約翰所描述的則是必然性。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《善惡之爭》第676頁；《救贖的故事》第431頁。

6.en:
**It is done.** Rather, “It has come to pass.” Textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 10) for the reading “They have come to pass,” or “They have occurred.” Important textual evidence may also be cited for the reading “I have become the Alpha and the Omega …” What God had promised through His holy prophets and to which His righteous people have looked forward with eager anticipation, will finally become an accomplished fact. The preview given to John is a guarantee of the final accomplishment yet to be carried out.
**Alpha and Omega.** See on ch. 1:8.
**Athirst.** The true believer is not eager to amass the things of this world, to be rich in worldly goods. Rather, he is eager to drink deeply of the spiritual riches from God.
**Fountain.** Or, “spring.” Compare John 4:14; Rev. 7:17; 22:17.
**Of life.** The passage may be translated, “out of the spring of that water which is life itself.” This is the promise of immortality (1 Cor. 15:53).
**Freely.** That is, “gratuitously.” The gift of immortality may be purchased “without money and without price” (Isa. 55:1).
6.zh:
他又對我說：都成了！我是阿拉法，我是俄梅戛；我是初，我是終。我要將生命泉的水白白賜給那口渴的人喝。

**都成了。**有古卷為，“我已成了阿拉法和俄梅戛。”上帝藉著祂的聖先知所應許的，祂公義的子民曾企望的，都將成為事實。約翰的預先看見使他得到了應許最後實現的保證。
**我是阿拉法，我是俄梅戛。**見 啟 1:8 註釋。
**生命。**指永生的應許（林前 15:53）。
**泉。**參 約 4:14；啟 7:17；22:17。
**白白。**即“免費的。” 永生的恩賜是“不用銀錢，不用價值” （賽 55:1）。
**口渴的人。**真信徒不想聚斂屬世的財富或物質。他渴望深飲於上帝屬靈的富泉。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第83頁；《早期著作》第279頁；《基督教育原理》第363頁；《證言》卷一第484頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《善惡之爭》第540頁。

20.en:
**Sardonyx.** Perhaps an onyx with red and brown layers against a white background.
**Sardius.** Believed to be a reddish-colored gem. The RSV reads “carnelian,” a reddish variety of chalcedony.
**Chrysolyte.** Literally, “golden stone.” A yellow-colored stone of uncertain identification.
**Beryl.** Believed to be a gem of sea-green color.
**Topaz.** Believed to be a more or less transparent yellow-colored stone used by the ancients for making both seals and gems. Some think the gold-colored chrysolite is meant.
**Chrysoprasus.** The modern chrysoprase is an apple-green, transparent gem. There is some uncertainty as to whether this is the stone here referred to.
**Jacinth.** Probably a purple-colored gem. Some identify the jacinth with the modern sapphire.
**Amethyst.** Thought to be a purple-colored gem.
20.zh:
第五是紅瑪瑙；第六是紅寶石；第七是黃璧璽；第八是水蒼玉；第九是紅璧璽；第十是翡翠；第十一是紫瑪瑙；第十二是紫晶。

**紅瑪瑙。**可能是縞瑪瑙。白底，帶紅色和褐色條紋。
**紅寶石。**據認為是一種紅色的寶石。英文RSV版譯為“紅玉髓，”。
**黃碧璽。**直譯為“金色的石頭。”一種未能確定類屬的黃色石頭。
**水蒼玉。**據認為是一種深綠色的寶石。
**紅碧璽。**據認為是稍帶透明的黃色石頭。古人用作印章和寶石。有人認為這是指金色的貴橄欖石。
**翡翠。**現代的翡翠是蘋果綠色的透明寶石。不知道這裡的翡翠是否就是現代的翡翠。
**紫瑪瑙。**可能是一種紫色的寶石。有人認為這裡的紫瑪瑙就是現代的藍寶石。
**紫晶。**據認為是一種紫色的寶石。

24.en:
**Nations.** A description of the redeemed from “all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues” (Rev. 7:9; cf. Isa. 60:3, 5).
**Kings.** The picture is drawn from the OT (see Isa. 60:11).
24.zh:
列國要在城的光裡行走；地上的君王必將自己的榮耀歸與那城。

**列國。**指來自“各國，各族，各民，各方”的贖民（啟 7:9；參 賽 60:3，5）。
**君王。**這幅畫面來自《舊約》（見 賽 60:11）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第676頁。

21.en: **One pearl.** The size of the gems listed is beyond human comprehension.
21.zh:
十二個門是十二顆珍珠，每門是一顆珍珠。城內的街道是精金，好像明透的玻璃。

**一顆珍珠。**這麼大的珍珠是人所無法想象的。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–22節）**。《使徒行述》第592頁。

11.en:
**Glory of God.** This probably refers to the abiding presence of God with His people throughout eternity. The glory that denotes His presence will never leave the New Jerusalem. Compare Ex. 40:34; 1 Kings 8:11.
**Light.** Gr. phōstēr, “a luminary,” “a light-giving body.” The word occurs in Phil. 2:15 in the clause, “among whom ye shine as lights [luminaries] in the world.” The “light” of the city is the “glory” of God, mentioned in the preceding comment (see Rev. 21:23).
**Jasper.** Gr. iaspis ch. (see on 4:3). The passage reads literally, “having the glory of God, her luminary, like a stone most precious, as jasper, flashing forth.”
**Clear as crystal.** Gr. krustallizō, “to flash forth light,” “to scintillate.” The English term “crystal” is derived from krustallizō.
11.zh:
城中有神的榮耀；城的光輝如同極貴的寶石，好像碧玉，明如水晶。

**上帝的榮耀.。**可能指上帝永遠與祂的子民同在。榮光象徵祂的臨格，將永不離開新耶路撒冷。參 出 40:34；王上 8:11。
**光輝。**“發光體。” 該詞出現在 腓 2:15 中：“你們顯在這世代中，好像明光照耀。” 城裡的“光輝”就是前面註釋所提到的上帝“榮耀”（見 啟 21:23）。
**碧玉。**見 啟 4:3 註釋。本節可直譯為：“有上帝的榮耀，她的光輝如同極貴的寶石，好像碧玉，閃閃發光。”
**明如水晶。**意為“閃光，”“發光。”
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第676頁；《救贖的故事》第431頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《使徒行述》第591頁。

18.en:
**Building.** Gr. endomēsis, “a building in,” from dōmaō, “to build.” The word occurs only here in the NT. Josephus (Antiquities xv. 9. 6) uses it of a mole, a sea wall built out into the sea as an inset in the water. Here endomēsis may refer to an inset in the wall as though the wall were inlaid, or studded, with jasper.
**Jasper.** See on ch. 4:3.
**Pure gold.** The structure of the city appears to have the transparency of glass. Its flashing beauty doubtless changes with every ray of light that falls upon it.
18.zh:
牆是碧玉造的；城是精金的，如同明淨的玻璃。

**碧玉。**見 啟 4:3 註釋。
**精金。**城的建築看上去像玻璃那樣透明。它美麗的光芒無疑會隨著照射在上面的光線而變化。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《今日的生活》第357頁。

1.en:
**New.** Gr. kainos, “new” in quality as opposed to that which is worn or marred. Both occurrences of “new” in this verse are translations of kainos. Neos, also translated “new” in the NT (Matt. 9:17; 1 Cor. 5:7; Col. 3:10; etc.), refers to newness in point of time. By using the word kainos, John is probably emphasizing the fact that the new heavens and earth will be created from the purified elements of the old, and thus be new in quality, different. The new heavens and the new earth are, then, a re-creation, a forming anew of existing elements, and not a creation ex nihilo. Compare 2 Peter 3:13.
**Were passed away.** That is, in so far as their former, marred state is concerned. That which was perfect as it came from the hand of the Creator, which He pronounced as “very good” (Gen. 1:31), had become terribly marred by sin and could not be allowed to continue throughout eternity.
**No more sea.** The clause reads literally, “and the sea is not any longer,” that is, the seas as we know them now will not exist in the new creation. Some have insisted that this “sea” is symbolic of peoples, nations, tongues (cf. ch. 17:15); but if so, the heavens and the earth would necessarily be symbolic also. Here John simply affirms that the heavens, the earth, and the seas will no longer exist as we know them now (cf. PP 44).
1.zh:
我又看見一個新天新地；因為先前的天地已經過去了，海也不再有了。

**新。**希臘文為 kainos，指品質的“新”，與陳舊相對應。本節的兩個“新”均譯自 kainos 。在《新約》中，Neos 也譯為“新”（太 9:17；林前 5:7；西 3:10；），指的是時間上的“新”。 約翰可能用 kainos來強調，新天新地是用經過潔淨的舊物質來再造的，因此在質量上是新的，與以前的不一樣。所以新天新地是對已有物質的重新建造，而不是從無到有的創造。參 彼後3:13。
**已經過去了。**即相對於原先汙損的狀態。當世界從創造主的手中出來時，祂曾宣佈說“甚好”（創 1:31）。但它因受罪惡的毀損，不能存留到永恆。
**海也不再有了。**也就是我們現在的海將不再存在於新造的世界中。有人認為這裡的“海”象徵多民，多國和多方 （參 啟 17:15）。但如果是這樣，天和地也是象徵性的了。其實約翰在這裡只是強調天，地和海都將不再是我們現在所熟悉的那個樣子了（參 《先祖與先知》第44頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第539頁；《善惡之爭》第674頁；《先祖與先知》第62頁；《救贖的故事》第430頁；【 SDA7.988】。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《教育論》第301頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–27節）**。《證言》卷一第67-71頁。

12.en:
**Wall great and high.** Such walls were built around ancient cities for protection against enemies. John’s imagery is borrowed in part from the description of the city Ezekiel saw (see on Eze. 48:35). The picture is that of an ancient city with walls and gates. These were terms with which the apostle was familiar, and Inspiration chose to reveal the glories of the eternal city to him in terms that he understood. Human language and human portrayals cannot adequately represent the grandeur of that celestial city. In pictorial prophecy the degree of identity between the picture and the actual calls for careful interpretation (see on Eze. 1:10; 40:1).
**Twelve gates.** Compare the city described by Ezekiel (ch. 48:31–34).
**Twelve angels.** The New Jerusalem is pictured as having angelic gatekeepers.
**Twelve tribes.** See Eze. 48:31–34. For the picture of spiritual Israel reckoned by tribes see on Rev. 7:4.
12.zh:
有高大的牆，有十二個門，門上有十二位天使；門上又寫著以色列十二個支派的名字。

**高大的牆。**古時建造高大的城牆，是為了防禦敵人。約翰的描寫有一部分源於以西結對所見之城的描述（見 結 48:35 註釋）。這是一座有城牆和城門的古城，是使徒所熟悉的。聖靈選擇了約翰所熟悉的事物將永恆之城的榮耀啟示給他。人的語言和描寫手法不可能充分表達天城的榮美。要注意理解預言異象中畫面與真實狀況之間的差異（見 結 1:10；40:1 註釋）。
**十二個門。**參 以西結所描寫的城（結 48:31–34）。
**十二位天使。**新耶路撒冷有天使守衛。
**十二個支派。**見 結 48:31–34。關於按支派來清點屬靈的以色列人， 見 啟 7:4 註釋。

7.en:
**Overcometh.** That is, according to the Greek, continually conquers, or habitually conquers. The Christian lives the victorious life by the power of the Holy Spirit. He may make mistakes (see on 1 John 2:1), but his normal life presents a picture of spiritual growth (cf. Rev. 2:7, 11, 17, 26; 3:5, 12, 21).
**All things.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the reading “these things,” that is, the promises given in the Revelation, particularly the things mentioned in this chapter.
**His God … my son.** Compare Gen. 17:7; 2 Sam. 7:14. The promise of intimate family connection is here set forth. The sinner saved by grace will be received into the family of God and be brought into a relation as close as if he had never sinned. The inhabitants of unfallen worlds cannot be closer to God and Christ than will be the redeemed sinner. See DA 25, 26.
7.zh:
得勝的，必承受這些為業：我要作他的神，他要作我的兒子。

**得勝的。**原文意為“不斷得勝者”。基督徒靠著聖靈的能力過得勝的生活（見 約壹 2:1 註釋）。他的日常生活反映了他的屬靈狀況（參 啟 2:7，11，17，26；3:5，12，21）。
**這些。**就是《啟示錄》中的應許，特別是本章所提到的應許。
**他的上帝 … 我的兒子。**參 創 17:7；撒下 7:14。這裡反映了親密的家庭關係。蒙恩得救的罪人將被接到上帝的家中，與上帝建立起親密的關係，就像他從來沒有犯過罪一樣。未曾墮落之諸世界的生靈與上帝和基督的關係，不可能有贖民那麼親密。見 《歷代願望》第25，26頁。

13.en: **On the east three gates.** Ezekiel’s enumeration is in the order, north, east, south, west (Eze. 48:31–34). John’s order is east, north, south, west. The difference is doubtless without significance.
13.zh:
東邊有三門、北邊有三門、南邊有三門、西邊有三門。

**東邊有三門。**以西結所列的順序是北，東，南，西 （結 48:31–34）。 約翰所列的順序是東，北，西。這種差異無疑沒有什麼意義。

23.en: **No need.** Light-giving bodies will not be imperative for the illumination of the city. The glorious effulgence of the presence of God will give more than sufficient light (cf. Isa. 60:19, 20). Material things are not indispensable in God’s plan; in His presence they are put to shame (cf. Isa. 24:23). Created light cannot outshine the uncreated glory of the divine presence.
23.zh:
那城內又不用日月光照；因有神的榮耀光照，又有羔羊為城的燈。

那城不需要發光體。上帝臨格的榮光已足夠明亮的了（參 賽 60:19，20）。在上帝的計劃中，屬於物質的東西不是不可缺少的。在祂面前，這一切都抱愧蒙羞（參 賽 24:23）。受造的光在上帝臨格的非受造榮光面前黯然失色。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第301頁；《早期著作》第170，179，286頁；《今日的生活》第357頁；見弗5：25懷愛倫註釋。

16.en:
**Foursquare.** There is beauty inherent in right proportion, perfect balance, and congruity. For various foursquare items see Ex. 27:1; 28:16; 30:2; 39:9; 2 Chron. 3:8; Eze. 41:21; 43:16; 45:2; 48:20.
**Twelve thousand furlongs.** A furlong (stadion) is about 606 ft. 6 in., or 185 m. (see Vol. V. p. 50). Thus, 12,000 furlongs would be about 1,378.4 mi. (2,218 km.). The text does not state whether this is a measure of the circumference or of one side. If the former, the city would measure about 344.6 mi. (551.4 km.) to a side. For the custom of measuring a city by its circumference see The Letter of Aristeas 105. It should be noted that the English furlong is not identical with the stadion.
**Equal.** Various attempts have been made to explain the dimensions of the city. It is difficult to envision a city reaching upward of 12,000 (or 3,000) furlongs (see above on “twelve thousand furlongs”). Some, though not denying the reality of the city, believe that the measurements here, like those of the wall, are “the measure … of the angel” (see on v. 17). They hold that it is therefore scarcely possible that human dimensions can here be intended. Others point to a similarity between the size of the city here described and that envisioned by the Jews. This question is discussed thus in the Midrash: “Whence the length and breadth and height [of Jerusalem]? And it enlarged itself and increased ever upward, Eze. 41:7. It has been taught, R. Eli‘ezer b. Ja‘aqob has said: Jerusalem will ultimately rise up and mount up to the throne of glory, and will say to God: ‘Too restricted is my space, recede from me that I may dwell!’ Isa. 49:20” (Pesiqtha 143a, cited in Strack and Billerbeck, Kommentar zum Neuen Testament, vol. 3, p. 849).
Still others assign to the word here translated “equal” (isos) the meaning “proportion,” and believe that although the length and breadth may well be equal, the height will be proportionate to the other dimensions. This is possible, although it is difficult to demonstrate such a definition from either Biblical or classical sources. Another interpretation permits isos to retain its normal meaning but observes that the word here translated height (hupsos) may mean not only “height” but also “the high part,” “the top,” “the summit,” “the crown.” If hupsos is understood in this sense, John means that the distance around the top of the wall is the same as that around the bottom.
Whatever uncertainty there may be as to the exact proportion or size of the city, it is certain that the glories of that celestial city will far exceed the fondest imagination. None need be concerned, for there will be room enough for all who desire residence. In the Father’s house there are “many mansions” (John 14:2).
16.zh:
城是四方的，長寬一樣。天使用葦子量那城，共有四千裡，長、寬、高都是一樣；

**四方的。**這裡蘊含著均衡之美。關於各種四方的事物， 見 出 27:1；28:16；30:2；39:9；代下 3:8；結 41:21；43:16；45:2；48:20。
**四千裡。**約2，218 公里（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五50頁）。沒有說這是指城的周長還是邊長。關於丈量城池周長的習俗， 見 《阿里斯提塔俄斯書信》  105 節。
**一樣。**對於該城的尺寸，有多種解釋。很難想像一座城會高達四千裡。有人雖然不否認該城的真實性，但認為這裡的尺寸和城牆的尺寸一樣，是“天使的尺寸”（見 第 17 節註釋），不可能是人間的度量。也有人指出該城的尺寸與猶太人著作的描述相似。《米德拉什》談到這個問題時說：“（耶路撒冷）的長、寬、高有何出處呢？它越高越寬。結 41:7。有教導說，雅各以利以亞曾說：耶路撒冷終將高升，上達榮耀的寶座，並將對上帝說：‘這地方我居住太窄，求你給我地方居住！’賽 49:20”（Pesiqtha 143a，引自斯特拉克和 比勒貝克《新約註釋》卷 三 第 849 頁）。
還有人認為本節的“一樣” （isos）是“均衡”的意思。他們相信長和寬可能是一樣的，但高度將會與長和寬成均衡的比例。雖然很難從聖經或古典文獻中找到該種解釋的根據，但也不無可能。另一種解釋保留 isos 的普通含義，但認為hupsos（高）不僅指“高度”，也有“高部，”“頂部”的意思。如果這樣理解，約翰的意思就是城牆頂部的長度同城牆底部是一樣的。
儘管我們無法確定這座城的精確比例或尺寸，但可以肯定天城的榮耀將遠遠超過人最美妙的想象。任何人都不必擔心，因為有足夠的地方為所有願意住在其中的人預備。因為在父的家裡，有“許多住處”（約 14:2）。

10.en:
**In the spirit.** That is, in a trance, in vision (see on ch. 1:10). The carrying away was “in a vision” (cf. on Eze. 8:3; Dan. 8:2).
**To a great.** In vision John seemed to be deposited upon a “great,” that is, a high mountain. From this vantage point he beheld the details of the city (cf. on Eze. 40:2).
**Descending.** Compare v. 2.
10.zh:
我被聖靈感動，天使就帶我到一座高大的山，將那由神那裡、從天而降的聖城耶路撒冷指示我。

**被聖靈感動。**就是被帶到異象之中 （見 啟 1:10 註釋；參 結 8:3；但 8:2 註釋）。
**到一座高大的。**約翰在異象中被帶到一座大山上，居高臨下，觀看城中的詳情（參 結 40:2 註釋）。
**從天而降。**參 第 2 節。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–14節）**。《早期著作》第18，291頁。

9.en:
**One of the seven angels.** One of the plague-bearing angels had already shown John the judgment of the great harlot (see ch. 17:1). Now, one of them (possibly the same angel, as some suggest) directs John’s attention to the New Jerusalem, the center and seat of the eternal kingdom. It is of interest to note that in the first instance it was a plague-bearing angel that presented mystical Babylon to the prophet, whereas now it is one of them who shows him the New Jerusalem. Historically, ancient Babylon and Jerusalem were traditional enemies, and figuratively they represent the two sides of the great controversy between evil and good. The one is represented as a fallen woman (ch. 17:5), the other as an honorable woman (chs. 19:7; 21:2).
**The Lamb’s wife.** See on ch. 19:7; cf. ch. 21:2.
9.zh:
拿著七個金碗、盛滿末後七災的七位天使中，有一位來對我說：你到這裡來，我要將新婦，就是羔羊的妻，指給你看。

**七位天使中，有一位。**執掌七災的天使中有一位已向約翰展示了大淫婦所受的懲罰（見 啟 17:1）。現在他們中的一位（有人認為是同一位天使）把約翰的注意力引到新耶路撒冷，就是永恆國度的中心和所在地。值得注意的是，先由掌管七災的天使之一位將奧秘之巴比倫向先知展示，現在又由他們中的一位將新耶路撒冷向他展現。在歷史上，古巴比倫是耶路撒冷的宿敵。它們象徵善惡鬥爭中的兩方。一方由墮落的女子來代表（啟 17:5），另一方由貞潔的女子來代表（啟 19:7；21:2）。
**羔羊的妻。**見 啟 19:7 註釋；參 啟 21:2。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–10節）**。《早期著作》第251頁；《善惡之爭》第426頁。

4.en:
**All tears.** Literally, “every tear.” See on Rev. 7:17; cf. Isa. 25:8; 65:19.
**Death.** The clause reads literally, “the death shall be no longer.” The definite article is of significance. John speaks of “the death”—the principle of death that came in as a result of sin. The definite article has, here, the force of a demonstrative. John says in effect, “this death, the one we know so well and fear so much, shall be destroyed.” Compare the language of Paul: “Death is swallowed up in victory,” literally, “The death was swallowed down in victory” (1 Cor. 15:54); “The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death [literally, “the death”]” (v. 26).
**Sorrow.** Grief, such as accompanies bereavement. The causes for sorrow will be completely removed. Compare Isa. 35:10.
**Crying.** Gr. kraugē, “outcry,” “clamor,” “crying.” No cause for crying will exist in that beautiful land of tomorrow.
**Pain.** Much of life’s misery and anguish is the result of harassing pain. Pain will be completely banished in that beautiful world of tomorrow.
**Former things.** That is, conditions as we know today will pass away. There will be nothing that bears the mark of the curse (ch. 22:3).
4.zh:
神要擦去他們一切的眼淚；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭號、疼痛，因為以前的事都過去了。

**一切眼淚。**直譯為“每一滴眼淚。” 見 啟 7:17；參 賽 25:8；65:19。
**死亡。**約翰所說的“死亡”是犯罪的結果。約翰實際上是在說，“我們所瞭解和恐懼的死亡，將要消滅。” 參保羅所說：“死被得勝吞滅”（林前 15:54）；“盡末了所毀滅的仇敵就是死”（第 26 節）。
**悲哀。**如喪失親人之悲痛。悲哀的根源將被完全剷除。參 賽 35:10。
**哭號。**kraugeµ，“喊叫，”“叫嚷，”“哭喊。”在將來的美地，再也沒有理由哭號。
**疼痛。**人生許多的不幸和痛苦都源於精神的痛苦。在那美麗的新世界，痛苦將完全消除。
**以前的事。**即現在的狀況都將過去。新天地裡將沒有任何咒詛的痕跡（啟 22:3）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第602頁；《復臨信徒家庭》第543，544頁；《兒童教育指南》第568頁；《教育論》第302頁；《早期著作》第289頁；《福山寶訓》第17頁；《服務真詮》第506，508頁；《今日的生活》第153，348，349，355頁；《救贖的故事》第413頁；《證言》卷八第42，45頁；《證言》卷九第287頁。

19.en:
**Garnished.** Gr. kosmeō, “to adorn” (cf. on v. 2).
**Precious stones.** Twelve kinds of precious stones are listed as being in the foundation. Not all of these can be identified by the modern jeweler, nor is much to be gained by making a comparison with the jewels of the high priest’s breastplate (Ex. 28:17–20). Neither ancient sources nor modern scholars agree as to the identification of all the stones. Some of their suggestions are listed below under the respective stones.
**Jasper.** See on ch. 4:3.
**Sapphire.** Perhaps lapis lazuli, a transparent or translucent sky-blue stone of great hardness.
**Chalcedony.** The identification of this stone is uncertain. The RSV reads “agate.” Some suggest a gem of greenish color.
**Emerald.** Believed to be a gem of bright-green color.
19.zh:
城牆的根基是用各樣寶石修飾的：第一根基是碧玉；第二是藍寶石；第三是綠瑪瑙；第四是綠寶石；

**寶石。**城牆的根基用十二種寶石裝飾的。其中不是每一種都能確認為現代的寶石，也無法通過與同大祭司胸牌上的寶石（出 28:17–20）進行比較而得出結論。古代的資料和現代的學者都無法完全對這些寶石進行確認。現把他們的一些看法羅列如下。
**修飾。**參 第 2 節註釋。
**碧玉。**見 啟 4:3 註釋。
**藍寶石。**可能是青金石，一種透明或半透明的高硬度天藍色寶石。
**綠瑪瑙。**類屬不明。英文RSV版為“瑪瑙。”有人認為是一種綠色的寶石。
**綠寶石。**據認為是一種淺綠色的寶石。

5.zh:
坐寶座的說：看哪，我將一切都更新了！又說：你要寫上；因這些話是可信的，是真實的。

**坐寶座的。**沒有說明身份（參 啟 20:11 註釋）。  啟 4:2 （見該節註釋）描寫聖父坐在寶座上。本節可能也指聖父。有人以 太 25:31 為據，認為“坐寶座的”是耶穌基督。
**看哪。**說話者提醒人注意即將揭示的重大事件。
**一切。**不再有任何詛咒（參 啟 22:3）。
**更新。**見 第 1 節註釋。
**寫上。**見 啟 1:11 註釋。約翰在異象中多次奉命把所看見的寫下來（啟 1:19；2:1；14:13等）。
**可信的，是真實的。**上帝的話語和應許都是值得信任的，因此也是可靠的（見 啟 22:6）。
5.en:
**He that sat.** Or, “the one sitting.” He is not identified (cf. on ch. 20:11). In ch. 4:2 (see comment there) the Father is represented as seated on the throne, and the same may here be implied. Some point to Matt. 25:31 as evidence that the reference may be to Jesus Christ.
**Behold.** The speaker calls attention to something important about to be disclosed.
**All things.** Nothing of the curse is to remain (cf. ch. 22:3).
**New.** Gr. kainoi (see on v. 1).
**Write.** See on ch. 1:11. At different points in John’s experience in vision the command to write is repeated (chs. 1:19; 2:1; 14:13; etc.).
**True and faithful.** That is, genuine and trustworthy. The words and promises of God are altogether trustworthy and may therefore be depended upon. (See ch. 22:6.)

14.zh:
城牆有十二根基，根基上有羔羊十二使徒的名字。

**十二根基。**“十二”的數字在第 12-14節中出現了五次。關於“十二”的意義， 見 啟 7:4 註釋。
**十二使徒。**新約教會是建立在使徒和先知的根基上的（弗 2:20）。
14.en:
**Twelve foundations.** The number “twelve” is given five times in vs. 12–14. For twelve as a significant number see on ch. 7:4.
**Twelve apostles.** The NT church is built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets (Eph. 2:20).

15.zh:
對我說話的，拿著金葦子當尺，要量那城和城門城牆。

**葦子。**參 結 40:3；啟 11:1。這裡測量的舉動及其結果無疑都是為了證明天家的寬敞（參 約 14:2 註釋）。
15.en: **Reed.** Compare Eze. 40:3; Rev. 11:1. Here the act of measuring and the stating of measurements are doubtless to give assurance of the adequacy and sufficiency of the heavenly home (cf. on John 14:2).

17.zh:
又量了城牆，按著人的尺寸，就是天使的尺寸，共有一百四十四肘。

**量了城牆。**在《新約》時期，一肘約等於44.5 釐米（見《SDA聖經註釋》 卷 五，第 50 頁），144 肘約為64 米。約翰沒有說這個尺寸代表城牆的高度。有人猜測是指城牆的厚度。
**天使的。**含義不明確。有人據此認為不能武斷地將人的度量標準用於新耶路撒冷。無論尺寸如何，我們都可確信這座城是十分完美的。當聖徒們看見聖城時，就會明白約翰所說尺寸的意義了。
17.en:
**Measured the wall.** On the basis of the NT cubit, which was about 17 1/2 in. (44.5 cm.) (see Vol. V, p. 50), 144 cu. would be about 210 ft. (64 m.). John does not say that this measurement represents the height of the wall. Some have conjectured that it may be that of its thickness.
**Of the angel.** In the Greek there is no definite article with “angel.” The passage reads, “of a man, even of an angel.” The meaning is somewhat obscure. Because of this, some urge we should refrain from dogmatically applying purely human standards of measurement to the New Jerusalem. Whatever the dimensions, we may rest assured that all is perfection. The saints will understand the significance of John’s figures when they see the city.

22.zh:
我未見城內有殿，因主神─全能者和羔羊為城的殿。

**殿。**希臘文為 naos，表示聖殿時，指的是聖所與至聖所，不包括外院和其它建築物。希臘文hieron 則包括整個聖殿，見 路 2:46；啟 3:12 註釋。
地上的聖所是上帝居所的象徵。亞當夏娃因犯罪而被趕出了伊甸園，離開了上帝的聖面。當罪惡剷除以後，教會將重新在上帝的面前居住。這時就不再需要任何建築物來象徵上帝的居所了。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第676頁；《今日的生活》第365頁；《救贖的故事》第432頁。
22.en:
**Temple.** Gr. naos, the word for the sanctuary is confined to the holy and most holy places, not including the outer courts and other buildings. For hieron, the word for the entire sacred enclosure, see on Luke 2:46; Rev. 3:12.
The earthly sanctuary was symbolic of the dwelling place of God. Because of their sin Adam and Eve were driven from Eden and the presence of God. When sin has been removed, the church will again be able to dwell in His presence, and no structure will be required to symbolize the dwelling of God.

25.zh:
城門白晝總不關閉，在那裡原沒有黑夜。

無疑是因為第23節所提到的原因（參 亞 14:7）。
25.en: **No night.** Doubtless because of the circumstances mentioned in v. 23 (cf. on Zech. 14:7).

26.zh:
人必將列國的榮耀、尊貴歸與那城。

**列國。**參 第 24 節。

27.zh:
凡不潔淨的，並那行可憎與虛謊之事的，總不得進那城；只有名字寫在羔羊生命冊上的才得進去。

**凡不潔淨的.。**無疑引自 賽 52:1。 約翰對聖城的描寫，有許多都引自《舊約》先知對耶路撒冷可能達到之榮耀境界的描寫。約翰正在描述該城將來的狀況（見 結 48:35 註釋）。
**行可憎。**見 第 8 節註釋。
**虛謊。**見 第 8 節註釋。
**生命冊。**見 腓 4:3 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第76頁；《健康勉言》第103，285頁；《善惡之爭》第474，481頁；《福山寶訓》第24頁；《今日的生活》第321頁；《醫療佈道論》第144，268頁；《先知與君王》第84頁；《先祖與先知》第326頁；《成聖的人生》第31頁；《論節制》第69頁；《給傳道人的證言》第149頁；《證言》卷五第278，331，384，475頁；見啟20：12-15懷愛倫註釋。
27.en:
**Any thing that defileth.** Doubtless an allusion to Isa. 52:1. Much of the imagery in John’s description of the Holy City is borrowed from the writings of ancient prophets who described the glories of the Jerusalem that might have been. John is describing the city that will be (see on Eze. 48:35).
**Worketh abomination.** See on v. 8.
**Maketh a lie.** See on v. 8.
**Book of life.** See on Phil. 4:3.

9.en:
**Those beasts.** See on v. 6. The praise uttered here is antiphonal. It is initiated by heavenly creatures, those nearest to God.
**Thanks.** Heavenly beings as well as men owe God thanks, for He has given them life. They exist by His pleasure. In the ultimate sense God owes His creatures nothing; they owe everything to Him.
**Him that sat.** See on v. 2.
**Who liveth for ever.** Compare the OT expression “the living God” (Joshua 3:10; Ps. 42:2; 84:2). God is the source of all life, and the fact that He “liveth for ever” is the basis of His unceasing sustenance of nature (see on John 1:4; Rev. 4:8).
9.zh:
每逢四活物將榮耀、尊貴、感謝歸給那坐在寶座上、活到永永遠遠者的時候，

**活物。**參第 6 節註釋。這裡的讚美是輪唱形式的。從離上帝最近的天上生靈開始。
**感謝。**天上的生靈和人類都要感謝上帝。因為祂賜給他們生命。他們因祂的美意而存在。從最終的意思上來講，上帝並不欠祂所造之物，而是受造之物在凡事上都欠祂的。
**那坐在寶座上的。**見 第 2 節註釋。
**活到永永遠遠者.。**參《舊約》的用語 “永生上帝”（書 3:10；詩 42:2; 84:2）。上帝是一切生命的源頭。祂“活到永永遠遠”，不停地維持著大自然的運作（見 約 1:4 註釋；啟 4:8 註釋）。

11.en:
**Worthy.** God is “worthy” to receive praise from His creatures, because He has given them life and all else they possess. He has made them what they are.
**O Lord.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the reading “our Lord and God.” Those who hold the view that the 24 elders are human beings point out that the use of the title kurios, “Lord,” by the elders and not by the four beasts may be significant, for kurios is the Greek counterpart of the Heb. Yahweh, the divine name by which God revealed Himself to His people (see Ex. 6:2, 3). Such a title, they assert, is particularly fitting for the praises of men. See Vol. I, pp. 171, 172.
**For thy pleasure.** Or, “by thy will.” It pleased God to bring the universe into existence and to give life to its creatures. He saw that it was good to do so. There was nothing desirable from His point of view in being alone in an empty universe. It pleased Him that the universe should be peopled with intelligent beings, capable of appreciating and reflecting His infinite love and perfect character. This was His purpose in creating them.
**Are and were created.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading, “they were, and they were created.” By the expression “they were” John doubtless refers to the existence of the universe after God had brought it into being. God created and now sustains all things (see on Col. 1:17).
11.zh:
我們的主，我們的神，你是配得榮耀、尊貴、權柄的；因為你創造了萬物，並且萬物是因你的旨意被創造而有的。

**我們的主，我們的上帝。**那些認為二十四位長老是人類的人指出，這裡稱上帝為“主（ kurios）的是長老，而不是四活物，說明kurios 是希伯來文 Yahweh （“耶和華”）的希臘對應詞。這是上帝所啟示給祂子民的自己的名字（參 出 6:2, 3），特別適合人對上帝的讚美。見《SDA聖經註釋》卷一 171, 172頁。
**配得。**上帝“配得” 祂所造之物的讚美，因為祂賜給他們生命，以及他們的一切。他們的存在全在於祂。
**你創造了萬物。**上帝創造了萬物，又維持著萬物的生存（參 西 1:17 註釋）。
**因你的旨意。**上帝樂意創造宇宙，賜生命給受造的生靈。祂認為那樣做很好。祂不願意宇宙空蕩蕩的。祂喜歡宇宙中居住著有智慧的生靈，能欣賞和反映祂無限的大愛和完美的品格，所以祂創造了他們。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第437頁；《先知與君王》第70頁。

3.en:
**He that sat.** Here again only the participle is (see on v. 2).
**Jasper.** Gr. iaspis, not precisely the modern jasper, but a stone described by the ancient naturalist, Pliny, as translucent (Natural History xxxvii). John has recourse repeatedly to precious stones for describing brilliant colors, for sunlight shining on such stones produced some of the most brilliant colors known to man in his day. In the present instance, the iaspis probably describes a bright, flashing light, more notable for its brilliance than its color.
**Sardine stone.** The carnelian or some other stone of a reddish color. Pliny (ibid.) notes that this stone was to be found at Sardis, and accordingly took the name of that city. Here it describes a brilliant red light.
**Rainbow.** Compare Ezekiel’s vision of the throne of God (Eze. 1:26–28).
**Like unto an emerald.** That is, of a green color. The brilliance of the light flashing forth from the presence on the throne is tempered by the soft green light of an encircling rainbow. This rainbow represents the combination of justice and mercy that characterizes God (see Ed 115; cf. COL 148).
3.zh:
看那坐著的，好像碧玉和紅寶石；又有虹圍著寶座，好像綠寶石。

**那坐著的。**再次採用分詞形式（見 第 2 節註釋）。
**碧玉。**不一定是現代的碧玉。古代的博物學家普林尼說它是半透明的（《自然史》 第 37 章）。 陽光照耀下的寶石，在當時看來是最璀璨不過的，所以約翰經常用寶石來形容光耀奪目的色彩。在本節中，碧玉可能主要是指它耀眼的光芒，而不是它的色彩。
**紅寶石。**撒狄石。指瑪瑙或其他紅色的寶石。普林尼說這種寶石產自撒狄，故命名為撒狄石。在本節它代表耀眼的紅光。
**虹。**參以西結所見的上帝寶座的異象（結 1:26–28）。
**好像綠寶石。**就是綠寶石的綠色光芒。坐寶座者的耀眼光芒因周圍彩虹的綠色柔光而減緩。這虹代表上帝品德中公義和慈愛的結合（見 《教育論》第115頁；參 《天路》第148頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第493頁；《教育論》第115頁；《先知與君王》第370頁；《給傳道人的證言》第157頁；《證言》卷六第340頁；《證言》卷八第23頁；見羅3：24-26懷愛倫註釋。

8.en:
**Six wings.** The cherubim of Ezekiel’s vision each had four wings (Eze. 1:6; 10:21), whereas the seraphim of Isaiah had six (Isa. 6:2). Wings may be understood as indicating the speed with which God’s heavenly creatures execute their errands (cf. Heb. 1:14).
**Full of eyes.** See on v. 6.
**Rest not.** Men customarily work by day and rest by night, but “he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep” (Ps. 121:4). The divine power upholding the universe never relaxes.
**Day and night.** Night brings an intermission to most human activities, but it has no effect on the ceaseless stream of praise to God that issues forth from the beings of heaven.
**Holy, holy, holy.** This is also the cry of the seraphim in Isaiah’s vision (see on Isa. 6:3). There is no valid reason for taking this triple ascription of praise as implying the Trinity, for it is directed to the presence on the throne, the Father. The second and third persons of the Godhead are here represented by other symbols (see Rev. 4:5; 5:6).
**Lord God Almighty.** See on ch. 1:8.
**Was, and is, and is to come.** See on ch. 1:4.
8.zh:
四活物各有六個翅膀，遍體內外都滿了眼睛。他們晝夜不住的說：聖哉！聖哉！聖哉！主神是昔在、今在、以後永在的全能者。

**六個翅膀。**在以西結的異像中，每一個基路伯有四個翅膀（結 1:6; 10:21），而以賽亞的撒拉弗則有六個翅膀（賽 6:2）。翅膀可能代表天上的生靈在執行任務時的速度（參來 1:14）。
**滿了眼睛。**參 第 6 節註釋。
**晝夜。**夜晚能中止人類的大部分活動，卻無法打斷天上生靈對上帝的讚美。
**不住。**人們通常日出而作，日落而息。但那“保護以色列的，也不打盹，也不睡覺”（詩 121:4）。上帝的能力托住宇宙，永不放鬆。
**聖哉，聖哉，聖哉。**這也是以賽亞異象中撒拉弗的讚美聲 （見 賽 6:3 註釋）。有人認為這三重的讚美是指三一真神，但這種說法證據不足，因為這是獻給那坐在寶座的。三一真神的另外兩位在這裡用其他的形象來表示（見 啟 4:5; 5:6）。
**全能者。**見 啟 1:8 註釋。
**昔在，今在，以後永在。**見 啟 1:4 的註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第402頁；《早期著作》第116，288頁；《善惡之爭》第645頁；《救贖的故事》第412頁。

4.en:
**Seats.** Gr. thronoi, “thrones.” The 24 elders are seen seated upon 24 thrones surrounding the throne of God.
**Four and twenty elders.** This scene is reminiscent of the LXX of Isa. 24:23, “The Lord shall reign … and before the elders He shall be glorified.” The fact that the elders here portrayed are clothed in white garments, which may be symbolic of righteousness (see on Rev. 3:4), and have on their heads “crowns” (stephanoi, emblems of victory; �see on ch. 2:10), has led some to suggest that they represent redeemed men.
One interpretation understands the description of the heavenly throne in chs. 4 and 5 to be fixed at a time before the events symbolized by the seven seals begin to take place. On this basis, if the 24 elders are human beings, it follows that they must be men already in heaven in John’s day. Adventists have often identified them with the saints who arose from their graves at the time of Christ’s resurrection (Matt. 27:52, 53; cf. Eph. 4:8), since that is a group known to have already been resurrected. The main resurrection is still future (1 Thess. 4:16). It is certain, therefore, that the presence of human beings in heaven cannot be taken as evidence that the resurrection of all the redeemed must precede the events portrayed in the seals.
Another interpretation compares the 24 elders with the 24 courses of the Levitical priesthood. As the priests ministered before God in the earthly sanctuary, so John sees 24 elders ministering in the heavenly sanctuary.
Another suggestion is that the 24 elders symbolize Israel in its fullest sense (see on Rev. 7:4)—two elders from each tribe, one symbolizing literal Israel, God’s people before the cross; and the other, spiritual Israel, the Christian church, God’s people since the cross. Thus they may be likened to the 12 patriarchs and the 12 apostles. This view would emphasize the symbolic character of these figures, instead of making them out to be literal saints now in heaven (see on v. 1).
Some interpreters see the 24 elders as angels, not as human beings. They point out that the elders are portrayed as ministering the prayers of the saints (ch. 5:8), a work, they say, that would hardly be committed to humans.
**White raiment.** See on ch. 3:18.
**Crowns.** See the foregoing on “four and twenty elders.”
**Gold.** Here, perhaps, simply a token of preciousness.
4.zh:
寶座的周圍又有二十四個座位；其上坐著二十四位長老，身穿白衣，頭上戴著金冠冕。

**座位。**“寶座。”二十四位長老坐在上帝寶座周圍的二十四個座位上。
**二十四位長老。**與賽 24:23 所描寫的場面相似：“耶和華必…..作王；在敬畏 祂的長老面前，必有榮耀。” 由於長老們身穿象徵公義的白衣（見 啟 3:4 註釋），頭戴“冠冕,”（象徵勝利；又見 啟 2:10 註釋），有人認為他們代表贖民。
有人認為 《啟示錄》第四，五章所描寫天上寶座的場面發生在七印所象徵的事件之前。如果這二十四位長老是人，那麼在約翰的時代，他們已經在天上了。復臨信徒一般認為他們是與耶穌一同復活的聖徒（太 27:52, 53；參 弗 4:8），是一群已經復活的人。而大批的復活還有待將來（帖前 4:16）。 因此在天上有人不一定證明所有的贖民必須在七印的事件之前復活。
還有人認為二十四位長老象徵猶太教祭司的二十四個班次。在地上的聖所中，有祭司為上帝供職，照樣，約翰也看到有二十四位長老在天上的聖所中服務。
又有人認為二十四位長老代表全體以色列人（參 啟 7:4 註釋）。每一個支派有兩位長老，一位代表主釘十架前的上帝子民，即肉身的以色列人，另一位代表主釘十架後的上帝子民，即屬靈的以色列人——基督教會。因此他們被比作十二先祖和十二使徒。這種看法強調數字的象徵性意義，而不是在天上的真實人數（見第 1 節註釋）。
有些解經家認為這二十四位長老是指天使，而不是人。他們在處理聖徒的禱告（啟 5:8）。這項工作是世人所難以承擔的。
**白衣。**見 啟 3:18 註釋。
**金。**可能只是象徵冠冕的貴重。
**冠冕。**見以上“二十四位長老”的註釋。

2.en:
**In the spirit.** Gr. en pneumati (see on ch. 1:10). John goes into vision a second time. How long a period of time elapsed between the first vision and this cannot be known.
**Was set.** Rather, “was sitting.” The throne is already in position.
**One sat.** John’s reverent reticence about the Ruler of the universe, in avoiding terms that might seem anthropomorphic, is apparent from the fact that he describes Him simply by the participle kathēmenos, “sitting,” without stating what or who was sitting. He implies only that a presence was upon the throne. Such a reference to the Father stands in striking contrast with the detailed description of the Son (ch. 1:13–16); but the Son is human as well as divine, and can therefore be described appropriately in human terms. See v. 3; cf. chs. 6:16; 7:10.
2.zh:
我立刻被聖靈感動，見有一個寶座安置在天上，又有一位坐在寶座上。

**我立刻被聖靈感動。**見 啟 1:10 註釋。 約翰第二次進入異象。不清楚兩個異象相隔的時間有多久。
**安置。**寶座已經安置在那裡。
**那坐著的。**約翰在這裡避免採用人格化的術語，只用了一個分詞（katheµmenos ，“那坐著的”）來指上帝，而沒有明言誰坐在寶座上，表明他對宇宙的主宰十分敬畏。他只是說有一位坐在寶座上。他對聖父的隱諱和對聖子的渲染形成了鮮明的對比（啟 1:13–16）。因為聖子既是人又是神，可以用人的語言來描述。見 第 3 節；參 啟 6:16; 7:10。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《先祖與先知》第107頁。

6.en:
**Sea of glass.** This description has much in common with Ezekiel’s vision of the throne of God, which rested upon a “firmament” (Eze. 1:26). In ancient times glass was much more valuable than it is today. Here, it represents the clear, crystalline appearance of the surface on which the throne stood.
**Crystal.** Gr. krustallos, a word meaning either “crystal,” a colorless, transparent mineral, or “ice.” What John sees is a vast shimmering expanse, gloriously reflecting the red and green radiance about the throne. Compare the vision of Ezekiel (ch. 1:22).
**Midst of the throne.** Perhaps, like Ezekiel’s cherubim (Eze. 1:22, 26), these beasts were seen under the throne as well as around it. The symbolism here is in harmony with ancient Semitic thought. Thus a sarcophagus from Byblus, from the end of the 2d millennium .., portrays a Phoenician king seated on a throne supported by an animal cherub (see W. F. Albright, “What Were the Cherubim?” The Biblical Archaeologist 1:1 [Feb., 1938], pp. 1–3). See Ps. 80:1; 99:1; Isa. 37:16.
**Beasts.** Gr. zōa, “living beings.” The word zōa does not indicate to what order of creatures these four belong. However, they closely resemble those of Ezekiel’s vision (see on Eze. 1:5–26), which Ezekiel calls cherubim (ch. 10:20–22).
**Full of eyes.** See Eze. 1:18; 10:12. This may be understood as a symbol of the intelligence and ceaseless vigilance of heavenly beings.
Inasmuch as the symbol of eyes is plainly drawn from Ezekiel, it is possible to understand it here also in terms of Hebrew thought. Nine times in the OT the Hebrew word ‘ayin, “eye,” is used in the sense of “color,” or “brilliance” (Prov. 23:31; Eze. 1:4, 7, 16, 22, 27; 8:2; 10:9; Dan. 10:6). This suggests that in describing the four beasts as “full of eyes,” John may mean that their appearance was one of shining brilliance.
6.zh:
寶座前好像一個玻璃海，如同水晶。寶座中和寶座周圍有四個活物，前後遍體都滿了眼睛。

**玻璃海。**與以西結對上帝寶座的描述相似。以西結稱之為“穹蒼”（結 1:25）。古代的玻璃比現在貴重得多。它象徵寶殿地面的晶瑩透剔。
**水晶。**krustallos。表示無色透明的礦物質“水晶”，或“冰”。約翰所看到的，是浩瀚的穹蒼，有紅色和綠色的榮光在寶座周圍閃耀。見以西結的異象（結1：22）。
**寶座中。**可能像以西結的基路伯一樣（結 1:22, 26）。這些活物不僅在寶座下面，也在寶座周圍。這裡的形象與古代閃族人的觀念是一致的。在巴布魯斯（Byblus）曾經出土了一個公元前一千多年的石棺，上面畫一位腓尼基國王，坐在動物基路伯所支撐著的寶座上（見奧爾布賴特《基路伯是什麼？》，《聖經考古學家》1938年2月，1:1）。參 詩 80:1; 99:1; 賽 37:16。
**活物。**zoµa, “生物。”沒有說明這四個活物屬於那一種動物。但它們很像以西結異象中的活物（見 結 1:5–26 註釋）。以西結稱之為基路伯（啟 10:20–22）。
**滿了眼睛。**見 結 1:18; 10:12。可以理解為象徵天上生靈的智慧和警覺。
眼睛的形象顯然出自以西結，可以按希伯來的思維方式來理解。在《舊約》中，希伯來詞 ayin,（“眼睛”） 有九次表示“色彩”或“光輝”（箴 23:31；結 1:4, 7, 16, 22, 27；8:2; 10:9；但 10:6）。 這表明，約翰說四活物“滿了眼睛”，可能是指他們光明的外形。

10.en:
**Four and twenty elders.** See on v. 4.
**Him that sat.** See on v. 2.
**Liveth for ever.** See on v. 9.
**Cast their crowns.** See on v. 4.
10.zh:
那二十四位長老就俯伏在坐寶座的面前敬拜那活到永永遠遠的，又把他們的冠冕放在寶座前，說：

**二十四位長老。**見 第 4 節註釋。
**坐寶座的。**見 第 2 節註釋。
**活到永永遠遠。**見 第 9 節註釋。
**把他們的冠冕放在。**見 第 4 節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第191，289，295頁；《今日的生活》第352頁；《證言》卷八第254頁。

7.en: **Lion.** Here each of the four beings appears with one of the four faces that were characteristic of each of the cherubim in Ezekiel’s vision (see Eze. 1:10; 10:14). For a discussion of the meaning of these symbols see on Eze. 1:10.
7.zh:
第一個活物像獅子，第二個像牛犢，第三個臉面像人，第四個像飛鷹。

與以西結異象中基路伯的四張臉相同（參 結 1:10; 10:14）。關於這些形象的意義，見 結 1:10註釋。

5.en:
**Lightnings and thunderings and voices.** A favorite expression with John (see chs. 8:5; 11:19; 16:18), probably portraying power and majesty (see Job 37:4, 5; Ps. 29:3, 4; Eze. 1:13).
**Seven lamps of fire.** Or, “seven fiery lamps.” See on ch. 5:6. Although these bear a superficial resemblance to the seven golden “candlesticks” of ch. 1:12, these are called “lamps” (lampades) rather than “candlesticks,” or “lampstands” (luchnia; see on ch. 1:12). Furthermore, they are clearly said to represent the seven Spirits of God, whereas those in ch. 1 represent the seven churches (see v. 20). On the basis of this symbolism some have identified the “door” (ch. 4:1) as one opening into the first apartment of the heavenly sanctuary.
**Seven Spirits.** See on ch. 1:4.
5.zh:
有閃電、聲音、雷轟從寶座中發出；又有七盞火燈在寶座前點著；這七燈就是神的七靈。

**閃電，聲音，雷轟。**這是約翰的習慣用語（見 啟 8:5; 11:19; 16:18），可能象徵能力和威嚴（參 伯 37:4, 5; 詩 29:3, 4; 結 1:13）。
**七盞火燈。**見 啟 5:6註釋。表面上與啟 1:12 的七個金“燈臺”相似，但它們被稱為“燈”（lampades），而不是“燈臺”（ luchnia，參 啟 1:12）。再者，這裡說它們代表上帝的七靈，而《啟示錄》第一章的燈臺則代表七教會（啟1：20）。有人據此認為啟 4:1的“門”是通往天上第一層聖所的。
**七靈。**見 啟 1:4註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第414頁；《先祖與先知》第356頁；《救贖的故事》第377頁。

1.en:
**After this.** That is, after John had seen the vision of chs. 1:10 to 3:22. The words “after this” do not imply any chronological relationship between the closing events of the preceding vision and the one about to be related.
**I looked.** Or, “I saw,” an expression John uses repeatedly to introduce new scenes or important new symbols (see on ch. 1:2).
**A door.** Here the door, apparently, into the throne room of the universe (see v. 2; cf. on v. 5).
**Opened.** Or, “standing open.”
**In heaven.** Not, “into heaven,” as if John were on the outside looking in. Inasmuch, as looking within, he beheld the throne of God, this must have been a door opening upon the throne room of the universe. This throne room has been identified as the most holy place of the heavenly sanctuary.
From a consideration of the state of the church on earth (chs. 1–3) John’s attention is now directed to a symbolic vision of the throne of God in heaven. That the description of God’s throne and the scene about it in chs. 4 and 5 is to be understood symbolically, rather than literally, is clear, for instance, from ch. 5:6, where Christ is described as “a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes,” yet alive and able to come and take the book from the hand of God. Inasmuch as this is obviously a highly symbolic figure, it follows that the whole prophetic incident is to be interpreted in the same way. In symbol the prophet can soar above the mundane and material objects of human life and reach the higher levels of the mind and heart with impressions of heaven that defy expression in literal language (see on Eze. 1:10).
**The first voice.** The meaning of the original is more clearly expressed thus: “Behold, … the first voice which I had heard as a trumpet speaking with me, was saying …” This voice is doubtless that of ch. 1:10, which introduced the first vision and now introduces the second.
**Come up hither.** An invitation to John to enter into vision, directing his senses away from his earthly surroundings and focusing them on heavenly things.
**Hereafter.** That is, not necessarily after the fulfillment of the previous vision, but from the standpoint of John’s own time. Consequently, this statement parallels that of ch. 1:1 (see comment there).
1.zh:
此後，我觀看，見天上有門開了。我初次聽見好像吹號的聲音，對我說：你上到這裡來，我要將以後必成的事指示你。

**此後。**即約翰看見啟 1:10-3:22 的異象之後。用“此後”一詞，並不表示前面異象中有關末日的事件同以下的異象之間存在著時間上的聯繫。
**我觀看。**約翰經常用這句話來引出新的畫面和重要的新表號（見啟 1:2註釋）。
**天上。**約翰似乎從通往宇宙寶殿的門外朝裡面看。他看見了上帝的寶座。這個寶殿被認定為天上聖殿的至聖所。
此刻，約翰的注意力從地上的教會（啟 1–3）轉到了天上上帝的寶座。《啟示錄》第 4 章和第 5 章對上帝寶座及其周圍情形的描寫顯然是象徵性的，而不是真實性的。因為啟 5:6把基督描寫成“羔羊. . . ，像是被殺過的，有七角七眼，” 但祂依然活著，前來從上帝的手中接過書卷。這個場面顯然是象徵性的。所以整個預言的異像也應當從這個角度來理解。先知在象徵性的異象中超越世俗和物質範疇，達到了心靈的更高境界，看到了無法用語言來表達的天國景象（見 結 1:10 註釋）。
**門。**這裡顯然指通往宇宙寶殿的門（見第 2 節；參 第 5 節註釋）。
**開了。**或“開著。”
**我初次聽見好像吹號的聲音。**無疑指 啟 1:10 中第一個異象開始時的號聲，現在又作為第二個異象的開始。
**你上到這裡來。**這裡邀請約翰進入異象，使他的感官從地上的環境轉到了天上的氛圍。
**以後必成的事。**不一定指前面的異象應驗以後的事情，而是指約翰的時代以後所發生的事。這句話與啟 1:1的意思是一樣（見 啟 1: 1 註釋）。

11.en:
**Opened.** Literally, “standing open.” Heaven was open when John’s attention was first directed to it, and remained open. Compare chs. 4:1; 11:19; 15:5. Accompanied by the angel armies of heaven (ch. 19:14), Christ is seen descending from heaven as King of kings (v. 16) in power and majesty to deliver His faithful people from those who are bent upon their destruction (cf. GC 641). The scene described in vs. 11–21 is the climax of “the battle of that great day of God Almighty,” often called the battle of Armageddon (see on ch. 16:12–19; cf. 6T 406).
**Behold.** Compare on ch. 21:5.
**White horse.** In Bible times horses were used almost exclusively in connection with warfare or government business. When used figuratively in the Bible, as here, the horse is usually a symbol of battle (cf. Ex. 15:21; Isa. 43:17; Jer. 8:6; Eze. 38:15; Zech. 10:3; Rev. 14:20; see on ch. 6:2). White typifies holiness of character (see on chs. 3:4; 6:2; 7:14). White horses have ever been the favorite of kings and military leaders. Christ has received the right to rule this earth as King of kings (see on ch. 19:1, 7) and now appears, figuratively, as a warrior, riding forth as a conqueror on a magnificent white charger to occupy His lawful domain and to escort His faithful people back to the “marriage supper” (v. 9; see on ch. 11:15). Compare Isa. 63:1–6.
**Faithful and True.** It should be remembered that Oriental names depict character (see on Acts 3:16), and that therefore the names here ascribed to Christ specifically represent Him in His role as champion of His beleaguered people on earth. Four statements are made concerning Christ’s name in connection with the battle of Rev. 19:11–21: 1. Christ is called “Faithful and True” (v. 11) in that He now appears, according to His promise (John 14:1–3), to deliver His own. To them He has seemed to delay His coming (see on Rev. 16:15), but they “have waited for him,” and He now appears for the purpose of effecting their salvation (Isa. 25:9; cf. Rev. 16:17). 2. The “name written, that no man knew, but he himself” (v. 12) represents the heretofore unknown role in which He now appears, as the avenger of His people (see on ch. 16:1). In the performance of this “strange” work (Isa. 28:21) He acts in a role new to both men and angels. 3. But as the avenger and deliverer of His people He is still “The Word of God” (v. 13). He is “The Word of God” at work carrying out the will of the Father on earth, now in judgment, as formerly in mercy (see on John 1:1–3; Rev. 19:15). 4. The title “King of kings, and Lord of lords” (v. 16) applies in a special sense to Christ at this time (see on ch. 17:14). All power has been given into His hands (1 Cor. 15:25). Satan selfishly aspired to the exalted position that had been reserved for Christ as the Son of God (Isa. 14:12–14; Rev. 12:7–9; PP 36). But the latter, not counting equality with the Father a thing to be grasped, had voluntarily relinquished the full exercise of the attributes and prerogatives of Deity for a time (see on Vol. V, p. 918; see on Phil. 2:6-8), and thereby demonstrated His worthiness to receive the honor and dignity implicit in the title “King of kings, and Lord of lords.”
**In righteousness.** His cause is altogether just (see on chs. 15:3; 16:5). Throughout history earthly rulers have waged war for selfish ends and personal or national aggrandizement. Compare Isa. 11:1–5.
**Doth judge and make war.** He executes judgment by waging war. This war is against the political and military forces of earth, which had assembled to destroy His faithful servants (see on chs. 13:15; 16:13, 14, 16, 17).
11.zh:
我觀看，見天開了。有一匹白馬，騎在馬上的稱為誠信真實，他審判，爭戰，都按著公義。

**觀看。**參 啟 21:5 註釋。
**天開了。**直譯為“天開著。” 當約翰的注意力初次被引到天上的時候，天就已經開了，並且一直開著。參 啟 4:1；11:19；15:5。 基督在天上眾軍的簇擁下 （啟 19:14），以萬王之王的身份從天降臨（第 16 節），將祂忠心的子民從那些定意要消滅他們的人手中拯救出來（參 《善惡之爭》第641頁）。第 11–21 節描寫的是“上帝全能者的大日聚集爭戰”的高潮。這場戰爭通常被稱為哈米吉多頓之戰（見 啟 16:12–19 註釋；參 《證言》 卷 六第 406 頁）。
**白馬。**在聖經時代，馬基本上只用於戰爭或政府公務。在聖經的表號中，馬通常象徵戰爭（參 出 15:21；賽 43:17；耶 8:6；結. 38:15；亞 10:3；啟 14:20；見 啟 6:2 註釋）。白色象徵品格上聖潔（見 啟 3:4；6:2；7:14 註釋）。白馬素來都是君王和將領所最喜愛的。基督已作為萬王之王接受了統治地球的權柄 （見 啟 19:1，7 註釋）。現在祂又象徵性地以戰士的形象出現，作為征服者騎在雄俊的白馬上，要去佔據祂的合法領土，並迎接祂忠心的子民回來參加“婚宴”（第 9 節；見 啟 11:15 註釋）。參 賽 63:1–6。
**誠信真實。**務要記住，東方人的名字往往表達人的品格 （見 徒3:16 註釋）。因此這裡基督的名字特別體現了祂在解救祂被圍困之地上子民時所起的作用。以下四點關於基督名字的論述，都是與 啟 19:11–21 的戰爭有關的：
一.	基督被稱為“誠信真實”（第 11 節），是因為祂按照自己的應許顯現（約 14:1–3），拯救祂的子民。他們覺得祂似乎耽擱了來臨（見 啟 16:15 註釋），但他們“素來等候祂。”現在祂來了，為實現拯救他們的目的（賽 25:9；參 啟 16:17）。
二.	“寫著的名字，除了祂自己沒有人知道” （第 12 節），說明祂如今顯現為祂的子民伸冤，這樣的工作是以前所不為人知的 （見 啟 16:1 註釋）。在完成這個“奇異”的工作時（賽 28:21），祂擔任了對世人和天使來說都是新的角色。
三.	雖然祂是祂子民的伸冤者和拯救者，祂依然是“上帝的道” （第 13 節），執行天父在地上的旨意，以前是憐憫，如今是懲罰（見 約 1:1–3；啟 19:15 註釋）。
四.	“萬王之王，萬主之主” 的稱號（第 16 節）特別適合於此時的基督（見 啟 17:14 註釋）。一切權柄都曾交給了祂 （林前 15:25）。撒但自私地想要篡奪上帝的兒子基督的崇高地位（賽 14:12–14；啟 12:7–9；《先祖與先知》 第 1 章， 36頁）。但是基督卻不以自己與上帝同等為強奪的，甘願暫時放棄一切專屬上帝的特性和特權（見《SDA聖經註釋》 卷 五，第 918 頁；見 腓 2:6-8 註釋），因此祂配受“萬王之王，萬主之主”這個稱號所暗示的一切榮耀和尊貴。
**審判爭戰。**祂藉著爭戰來執行判決。這場戰爭是針對地上政治和軍事勢力的。這些勢力聚集在一起要消滅祂忠心的僕人（見 啟 13:15；16:13，14，16，17 註釋）。
**按著公義。**祂的作為完全公義（見 啟 15:3；16:5 註釋）。在歷史中，地上的統治者們為了自私的目的以及他們個人或民族的野心而發動一次次的戰爭。參 賽 11:1–5。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第641頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–16節）**。見啟16：13-16懷愛倫註釋。

8.en:
**To her was granted.** John has set forth the New Jerusalem symbolically as the bride (see on v. 7). Continuing the figure, he speaks of the garments in which she is arrayed.
**Fine linen.** Here a figure for a righteous character (cf. chs. 3:5; 6:11; see on ch. 3:18; cf. on ch. 22:14).
**Clean.** Literally, “splendid,” brilliant and shining like the light of a lamp. The same word is translated “gorgeous” in Luke 23:11, and “bright” in Rev. 22:16.
**White.** Literally, “pure.”
**Righteousness.** Gr. dikaiōmata, “righteousness deeds,” not dikaiosunē, “righteous character” (see on Matt. 5:6; Rom. 3:20). Righteous deeds are the natural and inevitable result of a righteous character. Dikaiōmata applies particularly to the sanctified deeds of the Christian, his victorious life developed by the grace of the indwelling Christ (see on Gal. 2:20; James 2:17, 18, 20). For comment on the wedding garment in the parable of the Man Without a Wedding Garment see on Matt. 22:11. Compare on Matt. 5:48; see COL 315–317.
8.zh:
就蒙恩得穿光明潔白的細麻衣。（這細麻衣就是聖徒所行的義。）

**蒙恩。**約翰將新耶路撒冷比作新娘（見 第 7 節註釋）。他繼續這一比喻，講述她的衣飾。
**光明。**像明燈發光。該詞在 路 23:11 中被譯為 “華麗，” 在 啟 22:16 中譯為“明亮。”
**潔白。**直譯為“純潔。”
**細麻衣。**在這裡比喻公義的品格 （參 啟 3:5；6:11；見 啟 3:18 註釋；參 啟 22:14 註釋）。
**義。**希臘文為 dikaioµmata（“公義的行為” ），而不是 dikaiosuneµ（“公義的品格”  ，見 太 5:6；羅 3:20 註釋）。公義的行為是公義品格的自然流露。 Dikaioµmata 特別指基督徒成聖的行為，因基督的恩典住在他心中而形成的得勝生活（見 加 2:20；雅 2:17，18，20 註釋）。關於不穿禮服赴婚宴比喻中的禮服， 見 太 22:11 註釋。參 太 5:48 註釋；見 《天路》 第315–317.頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第591頁；《復臨信徒家庭》第536頁；《基督比喻實訓》第310頁；《兒童教育指南》第190頁；《教育論》第249頁；《今日的生活》第272頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《基督教育之研究》第341頁。

12.en:
**His eyes.** See on ch. 1:14. As Christ goes forth, the great champion of eternal justice, nothing escapes His notice.
**Crowns.** Gr. diadēma (see on ch. 12:3). In the Bible diadēma is never applied to the reward of the saints. It is always the crown of royalty. In addition to the many royal crowns that Christ receives as King of kings, He also wears the chaplet of victory, the stephanos, since He too overcame Satan (see on ch. 12:3; 14:14).
**A name.** See on v. 11; cf. on ch. 2:17.
12.zh:
他的眼睛如火焰，他頭上戴著許多冠冕；又有寫著的名字，除了他自己沒有人知道。

**祂的眼睛。**見 啟 1:14 註釋。當基督作為永恆公義的衛士顯現時，祂是明察秋毫的。
**冠冕。**diadeµma （見 啟 12:3 的註釋）。在聖經中， diadeµma 從來不用於對聖徒的賞賜。它是王冠。基督作為萬王之王除了戴許多王冠以外，還戴勝利的花冠，就是 stephanos，因為祂也戰勝了撒但（見 啟 12:3；14:14 註釋）。
**名字。**見 第 11 節註釋；參 啟 2:17 註釋。

7.en:
**Be glad.** The inward experience of the heart.
**Rejoice.** The outward expression that results from the inward emotion of gladness. It comes from a heart overflowing with happiness that Christ is now reigning as king (cf. ch. 18:20).
**Honour.** Literally, “glory.” This is the climatic expression of gratitude and devotion.
**Marriage.** “The bride, the Lamb’s wife” is “that great city, the holy Jerusalem” (ch. 21:2, 9, 10). The New Jerusalem is to be the capital of the new earth, and as such is representative of “the kingdoms of this world,” which are to “become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ” (chs. 11:15; 21:1–5; GC 426). The New Jerusalem will contain the Garden of Eden, in which the tree of life has been preserved (see ch. 22:1, 2; cf. PP 62; GC 299, 646–648). The wedding here referred to consists of the reception by Christ of His kingdom, as represented by the New Jerusalem, and His coronation as King of kings and Lord of lords, in heaven at the close of His priestly ministry before the plagues are poured out (EW 55, 251, 280, 281; GC 427, 428; see on ch. 17:14). As in the parable of the Ten Virgins, the waiting saints are represented as guests invited to the wedding (ch. 19:9; GC 426, 427; cf. Matt. 25:1–10).
**The Lamb.** See on ch. 5:6.
**Is come.** Or, “has [finally] come,” that is, the event has already taken place when this announcement is made (see above on “marriage”; cf. on v. 1).
**Made herself ready.** John continues his figurative account in terms of an ancient Oriental wedding. For comment on customs connected with such an occasion see on Matt. 22:1–13; 25:1–10; John 2:1–10.
7.zh:
我們要歡喜快樂，將榮耀歸給他。因為，羔羊婚娶的時候到了；新婦也自己預備好了，

**歡喜。**這是內心的體驗。
**快樂。**因內心歡悅的外在表現，源於一顆因感戴基督作王而快樂的心（參 啟 18:20）。
**將榮耀歸給祂。**這是感恩與獻身的最高表現。
**羔羊。**見 啟 5:6 註釋。
**婚娶。**“新婦，羔羊的妻” 就是“聖城耶路撒冷”（啟 21:2，9，10）。新耶路撒冷是新地球的首都。她代表將成為“我主和主基督的國” （啟 11:15；21:1–5；《善惡之爭》第426頁）的“世上的國”。新耶路撒冷裡有栽種著生命樹的伊甸園（見 啟 22:1，2；參 《先祖與先知》第62頁；《善惡之爭》第299，646–648頁）。這場婚禮包括基督承受新耶路撒冷所代表的國度，以及在最後七災降下之前，祂在天上的大祭司工作結束時被加冕為萬王之王，萬主之主（《早期著作》第 55，251，280，281 頁；《善惡之爭》第427，428頁；見 啟 17:14 註釋）。就像十個童女的比喻一樣，等候主的聖徒被比作應邀參赴婚宴的客人（啟 19:9；《善惡之爭》第 426，427頁；參 太 25:1–10）。
**到了。**即這樣宣佈的時候，事情已經發生了（見 上面“婚娶”的註釋；參 第 1 節註釋）。
**新婦也自己預備好了。**約翰繼續引用古代東方婚禮的習俗。見 太 22:1–13；25:1–10；約 2:1–10 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《證言》卷八第154頁；【 SDA7.986】。

17.en:
**Standing in the sun.** Perhaps the blinding light of the sun is here descriptive of the glorious light of the divine presence (cf. 2 Thess. 2:8, 9; Rev. 6:15–17). Thus the angel who issues the challenge of ch. 19:17 would be standing next to Christ, as in ancient combat an armor-bearer would be near his lord.
**Fowls.** This invitation to the “fowls” warns the assembled hosts of the wicked as to the fate that impends for them (see on ch. 16:15–17). It is couched in the graphic Oriental phraseology of a challenge to personal combat (cf. 1 Sam. 17:44–46). To be devoured by the scavengers of the skies constituted one of the curses for disobedience pronounced by Moses in his valedictory address to the people of Israel (Deut. 28:26). John’s phraseology in Rev. 19:17, 18 appears to be based on God’s words to the heathen nations of earth as recorded in Eze. 39:17–22 (cf. Jer. 7:32, 33).
**Supper.** The gruesome alternative to eating at the marriage supper of the Lamb (v. 9) is to be eaten by the fowls of heaven at the “supper of the great God.” Those who do not voluntarily accept God’s gracious invitation to be present at the one must respond to His imperative summons to the other.
17.zh:
我又看見一位天使站在日頭中，向天空所飛的鳥大聲喊著說：你們聚集來赴神的大筵席，

**站在日頭上。**這裡太陽眩目的光芒可能代表上帝顯現的榮光（參 帖後 2:8，9；啟 6:15–17）。發出本節呼籲的天使就這樣侍立在基督旁邊，就像古代作戰時為主人拿武器的士兵一樣。
**所飛的鳥。**向“所飛的鳥”發出的這一邀請，是警告邪惡的大軍所要面臨的厄運（見 啟 16:15–17 註釋）。 這裡採用了東方所特有的挑戰語氣（參 撒上 17:44–46）。摩西在對以色列民的告別演說中，曾把被空中的飛鳥吃掉作為他們違約的咒詛之一（申 28:26）。 約翰在 啟 19:17，18 中的用語似乎源於結 39:17–22 （參 耶 7:32，33）上帝對地上的外邦各國所說的話。
**大宴席。**不赴羔羊婚宴之人的可悲命運（第 9 節），就是在“上帝的大宴席”上被天空的飛鳥吃盡。凡不接受上帝恩典邀請的人將被迫接受祂的另一道命令。

13.en:
**Vesture.** Gr. himation (see on Matt. 5:40), here perhaps a rider’s coat, or the cloak of a military commander.
**Dipped in blood.** Figuratively, of course. The question arises as to whose blood stains the cloak of the rider. Some have suggested that it is a symbol of Christ’s own blood shed on the cross, on the assumption that it cannot be that of the wicked, who, at this point in the narrative, have not yet been slain. However, Christ here appears, not in the role of “a Lamb as it had been slain” (ch. 5:6), but of a conquering warrior. The striking similarity between this passage and that of Isaiah (ch. 63:1–6) suggests that this passage is a fulfillment of the words of Isaiah.
**His name.** See on v. 11.
**Word of God.** See on John 1:1. In executing divine justice on those who persist in rebellion against the government of heaven, Christ is as truly the “Word of God” as when, at His first advent, He came to earth with the gracious offer of divine mercy. His coming on both occasions is an expression of the divine will.
13.zh:
他穿著濺了血的衣服；他的名稱為神之道。

**濺了血。**當然是象徵性的。問題是誰的血濺在騎手的衣服上。有人說這象徵基督在十字架上所流的血。他們認為這血不可能是惡人的，因為那時惡人還沒有被殺。但是基督在這裡的形象不是“被殺過”的羔羊（啟 5:6），而是勝利的戰士。本節經文與《以賽亞書》63:1–6極其相似，說明這句話是以賽亞預言的應驗。
**衣服。**himation （見 太 5:40 註釋），可能指騎手的外套或將領的披風。
**祂的名。**見 第 11 節註釋。
**上帝的道。**見 約 1:1 註釋。基督作為“上帝的道”，對那些堅持反叛天上政權的人執行上帝的判決，就像祂第一次降臨時，帶著上帝的恩典和慈愛一樣。祂兩次降臨都表達了上帝的旨意。

14.en: **Armies.** That is, the angelic hosts that accompany Christ at His second advent (see Matt. 24:31; 25:31). See on Rev. 17:14; cf. Matt. 22:7.
14.zh:
在天上的眾軍騎著白馬，穿著細麻衣，又白又潔，跟隨他。

**眾軍。**就是陪伴基督復臨的天軍（見 太 24:31；25:31）。 見 啟 17:14；參 太 22:7 的註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第523頁；《善惡之爭》第641頁。

10.en:
**Fell.** A typical Oriental gesture of reverence and worship. Here it is an expression of profound joy and gratitude, for the marriage supper is a celebration of triumph over the forces of evil, which have sought to prevent this very event. This is the first occasion on which John responded thus to the message of the angel, and represents the depth of feeling it stirred in him.
**Do it not.** Compare Acts 10:26.
**Fellowservant.** Literally, “fellow slave,” “fellow bondsman.” What a privilege it is that devoted workers on earth may share the companionship of, and be co-workers with, heavenly angels!
**Of thy brethren.** That is, a fellow servant of thy brethren. Some have considered this designation as evidence that the speaker must be a member of the human family, such as Enoch, Elijah, Moses, or one of the saints raised with Christ at His resurrection. However, there is no direct evidence in Scripture that a translated human being ever acted in the role of an angel, as here, to reveal truth to his fellow men (cf. EW 231).
**The testimony of Jesus.** See on chs. 1:2; 12:17.
**Spirit of prophecy.** For the word “prophecy,” compare the word “prophet” in Matt. 11:9. The Holy Spirit was sent to bear testimony to Jesus (John 15:26), and His witness is equivalent to that of Jesus in person. The Spirit of prophecy is one of the gifts of the Spirit (see on 1 Cor. 12:10; Eph. 4:11). For the manifestation of this gift among the people of God in the last days see Additional Note at end of chapter; see on ch. 12:17.
10.zh:
我就俯伏在他腳前要拜他。他說：千萬不可！我和你，並你那些為耶穌作見證的弟兄同是作僕人的，你要敬拜神。因為預言中的靈意乃是為耶穌作見證。

**俯伏。**東方人表示尊敬和崇拜的典型姿勢，在這裡表達了約翰深切的喜樂和感恩，因為羔羊的婚宴是慶祝對邪惡勢力作戰的勝利。邪惡的勢力曾企圖阻止這件事的發生。這是約翰第一次以這種方式回應天使的信息，表達該信息給他所帶來的激動。
**千萬不可。**參 徒 10:26。
**你那些 . . . 弟兄。**有人據此認為說話的是人類的一員，如以諾，以利亞，摩西或基督一同復活之聖徒中的一位。但聖經沒有直接的證據證明有昇天的人充當天上的使者，像這裡那樣，向同胞傳達真理（參 《早期著作》第 231 頁）。
**為耶穌作見證。**見 啟 1:2；12:17 註釋。
**同作僕人的。**這是多大的特權啊！地上獻身的工人竟能與天使同工為伴！
**預言中的靈意。**關於 “預言” ，參 太 11:9 的“先知”。聖靈奉差遣為耶穌作見證（約 15:26）。祂的見證就是耶穌的見證。預言之靈是聖靈恩賜的一種 （見 林前 12:10；弗 4:11 註釋）。關於末世時這種恩賜在上帝子民中間的表現， 見 本章補充註釋；見 啟 12:17 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第231頁；《今日的生活》第41頁；《先祖與先知》第367頁。

16.en:
**Vesture.** See on v. 13.
**And on his thigh.** Preferably, “that is, upon his thigh.” The name was seen inscribed on the part of his cloak that covered the thigh.
**A name.** See on v. 11.
**King of kings.** See on ch. 17:14; cf. on ch. 19:6.
16.zh:
在他衣服和大腿上有名寫著說：萬王之王，萬主之主。

**衣服。**見 第 13 節註釋。
**大腿上。**名字寫在遮住大腿上的那一部分衣服上。
**名。**見 第 11 節。
**萬王之王。**見 啟 17:14 註釋；參 啟 19:6 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第739頁；《早期著作》第179，286頁；《善惡之爭》第641頁；《福山寶訓》第108頁；《救贖的故事》第410頁；《證言》卷六第406頁。

15.en:
**Out of his mouth.** The sword is obviously figurative. By the word of the Lord the earth and its inhabitants were brought into being (Ps. 33:6, 9), and now, by the word of His mouth, He terminates their existence (see Rev. 19:20, 21).
**Sword.** Gr. rhomphaia (see on ch. 1:16), the large weapon of assault used by soldiers of ancient times, in contrast with the machaira, the short stabbing sword used in defense (see on Luke 22:36). Compare Jer. 46:10.
**Smite.** Literally, “smite [once for all].”
**Rule.** Gr. poimainō, literally, “to shepherd” (see on Matt. 2:6). The expression “and shall rule them” may better be translated, “that is, shall rule them,” for the smiting and the ruling refer to the same thing.
**Rod of iron.** See on Rev. 2:27; cf. Ps. 2:9; 110:1, 2, 5, 6. The ancient shepherd’s rod had a double function. The crook on one end served to help and guide the sheep, while the heavy ferrule on the other end, a metal cap or ring to strengthen the rod, made it also a weapon of assault. This was used for the protection of the flock, to repel and kill wild animals that would scatter and destroy it. It is now time for the Good Shepherd to use the “rod of iron” against the nations for the deliverance of His beleaguered flock on earth. His ruling, or smiting the nations, with a rod of iron results in their extermination, not their government during the millennium, as some hold (see Additional Notes on Chapter 20, Note 2).
**Winepress.** See on Isa. 63:3; Rev. 14:19, 20, where the same figure is developed further. Compare Lam. 1:15.
**Of the fierceness and wrath.** Rather, “which is the fury of the anger.” See on ch. 16:1.
**Almighty.** See on ch. 1:8.
15.zh:
有利劍從他口中出來，可以擊殺列國。他必用鐵杖轄管（轄管：原文是牧）他們，並要踹全能神烈怒的酒醡。

**利劍。**希臘文為 rhomphaia （見 啟 1:16 註釋），是古代士兵所用的進攻性武器，與防身的短刀 machaira 不同（見 路 22:36 註釋）。 參 耶 46:10。
**從祂口中。**這劍顯然是象徵性的。地和地上的居民都藉上帝的話而有的（詩 33:6，9）。現在祂藉著祂的口所說的話，結束了他們的存在 （見 啟 19:20，21）。
**擊殺。**直譯為“殺滅。”
**鐵杖。**見 啟 2:27 註釋；參 詩 2:9；110:1，2，5，6。古代牧人的杖有兩個功能。有彎柄的一端用來幫助和引導羊群，另一端有金屬環，用於加固牧杖，或用作攻擊的武器。牧杖可以保護羊群，打退或擊殺那些驅趕和吞噬羊群的野獸。現在，好牧人用“鐵杖”攻擊列國，要拯救祂在地上被囚的羊群。祂用鐵杖轄管或擊殺列國，消滅了他們，而不是像一些人認為的，讓他們在一千年期間執政（見 第 20 章補充註釋 2）。
**轄管。**poimainoµ，直譯為 “牧養” （見 太 2:6 註釋）。擊殺和轄管指的是同一件事。
**全能者。**見 啟 1:8 註釋。
**烈怒。**見 啟 16:1 註釋。
酒榨。 詳見 賽 63:3；啟 14:19，20 註釋。參 哀 1:15。

1.zh:
此後，我聽見好像群眾在天上大聲說：哈利路亞（就是要讚美耶和華的意思）！救恩、榮耀、權能都屬乎我們的神！

**此後。**就是在目睹了 啟 17 章和 18章的異象之後 （見 啟 18:1 註釋）。  啟 19 章的異像是緊接著向約翰顯示的。從第 2 節中可以看出，這首歌顯然是在第七災期間執行了對“大淫婦” 的判決之後唱的（見 啟 16:19；17:1 註釋），因此發生在 啟 17:16，17；18:4–23 所描述的場面之後。根據 《給傳道人的證言》第 432 頁，這首讚美上帝的頌歌是緊接在掌管第七災的天使完成了任務之後。既然 啟 18 至 20 章的事件是按照時間的順序，那麼 啟 19:1–7 中的頌歌就是與基督復臨時的事件密切相關的，但不能確定是在基督復臨前，復臨時，還是在復臨之後。上下文似乎暗示發生在基督復臨前夕的某個時刻（參 第 11 節）。
**群眾。**指天上的居民，可能還包括地上的贖民（參 啟 18:20）。啟 19:1–7 的頌歌可能是對啟 18:20 的呼召的回應。
**大聲。**見 啟 11:15 註釋。
**哈利路亞。**希臘文為 Allelouia，譯自是希伯來語 halelu-Yah “你們讚美耶和華”（見 詩 104:35 註釋）。 Halal意，“發光，”“誇耀，”“慶祝，”“讚美” ； Yah是Yahweh （“耶和華”）的縮略形式。“哈利路亞”與另一個希伯來詞 “阿們”原封不動地引進了英語。在《新約》中，“哈利路亞”只在 啟 19 章中出現四次（第 1，3，4，6 節） 。
第 1–7 節形成了輪唱，由兩句頌歌和兩句回應組成：（1） 在第 1–3 節中，天上的大聲音引出了詩歌的主題：因懲罰了巴比倫而將榮耀和公義歸給祂。（2）在 第 4 節中，“四活物”和“眾長老”回應表示贊同。（3） 在 第 5 節中，有聲音從寶座出來，呼籲全宇宙忠心子民一同讚美上帝。（4） 在 第 6，7 節，全宇宙的生靈同心合意歡呼上帝至高無上的威權。這首歡歌與 啟 18:10–19 的哀歌形成了鮮明的對比。
這段輪唱頌歌的主題與 詩 24:7–10 相似。那首詩也是由兩句頌詞和兩句回應組成。這首啟應的合唱最初用於護送約櫃迴歸耶路撒冷的遊行（《先祖與先知》第708頁）。幾百年之後在耶穌復活（《早期著作》第 187 頁）和昇天的時候再次響起（《歷代願望》 第 833頁；《早期著作》第 190，191 頁）。
**救恩。**在希臘文裡，這裡歸給上帝的每一樣美德之前都加有定冠詞，說明各樣美德的完美和豐富。啟 12:10 的“救恩”（見 該節註釋）是指脫離那“控告我們弟兄的”。本節的“救恩”則是指脫離奧秘之巴比倫（見 啟 16:17 註釋）。前者是耶穌第一次降臨時成就的；後者是祂復臨時成就的。
**榮耀。**見 太 6:13；羅 3:23 註釋。
**權能。**見 太 6:13；28:18 註釋。
有文本在“上帝”前面還加上“主”。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–6節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第432頁。
1.en:
**After these things.** That is, after witnessing the scenes of chs. 17 and 18 (see on ch. 18:1). Those of ch. 19 were presented to John immediately, without interruption. From v. 2 it is apparent that this song is sung after judgment has been executed upon the “great whore,” an event that takes place under the seventh plague (see on chs. 16:19; 17:1), and thus after the scene described in chs. 17>17:16, 17; 18:4–23. According to TM 432 the singing of this song of praise to God follows immediately upon the completion of the work of the seventh plague-bearing angel. If the events of chs. 18 to 20 are recorded in chronological order, as appears to be the case, the anthem of ch. 19:1–7 is sung in close connection with events at the second coming of Christ, whether at that very time or just before or after cannot be determined with certainty. The context may be understood as assigning the anthem to a point of time immediately prior to the actual appearance of Christ (cf. v. 11).
**A great voice.** See on ch. 11:15.
**Much people.** The inhabitants of heaven, and possibly also men redeemed from this earth (cf. ch. 18:20). It may be that the anthem of ch. 19:1–7 is sung in response to the call of ch. 18:20.
**Alleluia.** Gr. Allelouia, a transliteration of the Heb. halelu-Yah, “praise ye Yahweh” (see on Ps. 104:35), from halal, “to shine,” “to boast,” “to celebrate,” “to praise,” and Yah, a shortened form of Yahweh. Like another Heb. word “amen,” “hallelujah” has been adopted into the English language practically unchanged. The four occurrences of the word in Rev. 19 (vs. 1, 3, 4, 6) are the only instances of its use in the NT.
Verses 1–7 constitute an antiphonal choral arrangement composed of two anthems and two responses: (1) In vs. 1–3 a great voice in heaven leads out with the theme of the song, ascribing honor and justice to God for having punished Babylon. (2) In v. 4 the “beasts” and the “elders” respond in affirmation. (3) In v. 5 a voice from the throne summons all loyal subjects throughout the universe to a joint recognition of the truth of the theme. (4) In vs. 6, 7 the entire universe unites in acclaiming the right of God to universal sovereignty. This paean of praise stands in striking contrast with the dirge of death in ch. 18:10–19.
The motif of this antiphonal hymn of praise is similar to that Ps. 24:7–10, which is likewise composed of two anthems and two responses. This responsive chorus was first used during the triumphal procession marking the return of the ark to Jerusalem (PP 708), and centuries later at the resurrection (EW 187) and the ascension (DA 833; EW 190, 191).
**Salvation.** Literally, “the salvation.” In the Greek each of the virtues here ascribed to God is preceded by the definite article. This suggests the fullness, the sum total, of each attribute. The “salvation” of ch. 12:10 (see on comment there) is specifically salvation from “the accuser of our brethren”; here, it is salvation from mystical Babylon (see on ch. 16:17). The one refers to what was accomplished at the first advent, the other, to what is to be accomplished at the second.
**Glory.** See on Matt. 6:13; Rom. 3:23.
**Honour.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the omission of this word.
**Power.** See on Matt. 6:13; 28:18.
**The Lord.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the omission of this expression.

2.zh:
他的判斷是真實公義的；因他判斷了那用淫行敗壞世界的大淫婦，並且向淫婦討流僕人血的罪，給他們伸冤。

**判斷。**（見 啟 16:7 的註釋），這裡無疑是泛指最後的七災，特別是對奧秘之巴比倫的懲罰（見 啟 17:1；18:4，10 註釋）。
**真實。**就是“真實可靠的”（見 啟 15:3 註釋）。
**公義的。**（見 啟 15:3；16:1，5 註釋）。上帝的判斷絕無錯誤。祂考慮全部的事實。
**因祂。**第 2 節指出了第 1 節讚美的理由。
**判斷了。**原文表示一個完成了的動作。
**淫行。**見 啟 17:2 註釋。
**敗壞。**她的罪行持續了很長一段時間。見 啟 17:2，6 註釋。
**大淫婦。**見 啟 17:1，5 註釋。
**僕人血。**見 啟 6:9，10；16:6；17:6 註釋。
**給他們伸冤.。**就是懲罰。見 啟 18:6，20 註釋。
2.en:
**For.** Verse 2 accounts for the ascription of praise in v. 1.
**True.** That is, genuine, real, dependable (see on ch. 15:3).
**Righteous.** Or, “just” (see on chs. 15:3; 16:1, 5). God will make no error in His acts of judgment. He will take all the facts into account.
**Judgments.** Literally, “[acts of] judging” (see on ch. 16:7), here, doubtless, the seven last plagues in general and the judgment of mystical Babylon in particular (see on chs. 17:1; 18:4, 10).
**Hath judged.** The Greek specifies a single, completed act.
**Great whore.** See on chs. 17:1, 5.
**Did corrupt.** Or, “was corrupting.” Her criminal conduct covered a long period of time. See on ch. 17:2, 6.
**Her fornication.** See on ch. 17:2.
**And hath avenged.** Or, “in that he hath avenged.” The judging is the avenging. See on ch. 18:6, 20.
**Blood of his servants.** See on chs. 6:9, 10; 16:6; 17:6.

3.zh:
又說：哈利路亞！燒淫婦的煙往上冒，直到永永遠遠。

**煙往上冒。**見 啟 18:8，9 註釋。
**永永遠遠。**見 啟 14:11 註釋。
3.en:
**Her smoke rose up.** See on ch. 18:8, 9.
**For ever and ever.** See on ch. 14:11.

4.zh:
那二十四位長老與四活物就俯伏敬拜坐寶座的神，說：阿們！哈利路亞！

**長老。**見 啟 4:4 註釋。
**活物。**見 啟 4:6–8 註釋。
**俯伏。**參 啟 4:10。
**坐寶座的上帝。**見 啟 4:10 註釋。
**阿們。**見 太 5:18 註釋。
4.en:
**Elders.** See on ch. 4:4.
**Beasts.** See on ch. 4:6–8.
**Fell down.** Compare ch. 4:10.
**Sat on the throne.** See on ch. 4:10.
**Amen.** See on Matt. 5:18.

5.zh:
有聲音從寶座出來說：神的眾僕人哪，凡敬畏他的，無論大小，都要讚美我們的神！

**從寶座出來。**要麼是上帝自己的聲音，要麼是祂代言者的聲音（見 啟 16:17 註釋）。
**眾僕人。**見 啟 1:1 註釋。
**凡敬畏祂的。**就是“眾僕人” 。
**敬畏。**就是尊敬畏懼（見 啟 11:18 註釋）。
**無論大小。**參 啟 11:18。
**讚美。**直譯為 “不斷讚美。” 回應這一呼召的是第 6，7節中的合唱。
5.en:
**Out of the throne.** This was either the voice of God Himself or that of one speaking for Him (see on ch. 16:17).
**Praise.** Literally, “keep on praising.” The response to this call is the chorus of voices of vs. 6, 7.
**His servants.** See on ch. 1:1.
**And ye.** Or, “even ye,” “ye that fear,” is equivalent to “ye his servants.”
**Fear.** That is, in the sense of reverential awe (see on ch. 11:18).
**Small and great.** Compare ch. 11:18.

6.zh:
我聽見好像群眾的聲音，眾水的聲音，大雷的聲音，說：哈利路亞！因為主─我們的神、全能者作王了。

**我聽見。**參 啟 1:2 註釋。
**好像。**或“似乎。”
**聲音。**見 啟 14:2 註釋。
**眾水。**參 啟 14:2。
**哈利路亞。**見 第 1 節註釋。
**全能者。**見 林後 6:18；啟 1:8註釋。
**作王了。**意為“開始作王”。在查案審判結束，基督離開至聖所之前，祂就得了國，擔任“以萬王之王”（《早期著作》第 280 頁；《善惡之爭》 第428頁；參 《早期著作》第 55 頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第48頁；《善惡之爭》第673頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《歷代願望》第151頁；《先知與君王》第721頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–9節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第421頁。
6.en:
**I heard.** Compare on ch. 1:2.
**As it were.** Or, “what seemed to be.”
**Voice.** See on ch. 14:2.
**And as the voice.** Rather, “even as the voice,” in both instances where this expression occurs in v. 6.
**Many waters.** Compare ch. 14:2.
**Alleluia.** See on v. 1.
**Omnipotent.** Or, “Almighty” (see on 2 Cor. 6:18; Rev. 1:8).
**Reigneth.** Literally, “reigned,” in the sense that He “began to reign.” It is at the close of the investigate judgment, but before Christ leaves the most holy place, that He receives His kingdom and begins His reign as “King of kings” (EW 280; GC 428; cf. EW 55).

9.zh:
天使吩咐我說：你要寫上：凡被請赴羔羊之婚筵的有福了！又對我說：這是神真實的話。

**天使。**就是 第 10 節中的那位天使。
**你要寫上。**見 啟 1:2，11 註釋。
**被請。**就是受到邀請參加婚宴（見 太 22:14；羅 8:28 註釋）。
**羔羊。**見 啟 5:6 註釋。
婚宴。 希臘文為 deipnon（“晚餐”）.。“羔羊的婚宴”在地球漫長“一天”的結束時舉行。見 太 22:1–14 註釋。
**有福了。**見 太 5:3 註釋。
**這是。**就是 邀請的話。
**真實的話。**意為“絕對可靠”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第503頁；《歷代願望》第151頁；《早期著作》第19頁；《善惡之爭》第427頁；《今日的生活》第356頁；《給傳道人的證言》第19頁；《證言》卷一第69頁；《證言》卷六第412頁；《證言》卷七第54頁；《證言》卷八第153頁。
9.en:
**He.** That is, the angel of v. 10.
**Write.** See on ch. 1:2, 11.
**Blessed.** Or, “happy” (see on Matt. 5:3).
**Called.** That is, invited to the marriage feast (see on Matt. 22:14; Rom. 8:28).
**Supper.** Gr. deipnon, the evening meal. The “marriage supper of the Lamb” takes place at the end of earth’s long day. See on Matt. 22:1–14.
**The Lamb.** See on ch. 5:6.
**These.** That is, the words of the invitation.
**True sayings.** Literally, “genuine [ones].” The invitation is absolutely trustworthy; it can be depended upon.

18.zh:
可以吃君王與將軍的肉，壯士與馬和騎馬者的肉，並一切自主的為奴的，以及大小人民的肉。

**君王。**地上各國的聯盟，在冒充光明天使的撒但直接領導之下統一行動（參 啟 16:14，16，17；17:12，14 註釋）。
**將軍。**軍隊的指揮官們聚集在一起要執行撒但在善惡之爭最後幾幕中的旨意。
**肉。**參 啟 17:16 註釋。
**壯士。**指組織嚴密，訓練有素，裝備精良的軍隊。
**騎馬者的肉。**第 18 節的後半部分描繪了邪惡勢力在基督復臨時遭到徹底毀滅的生動畫面（參 啟 6:15；14:17–20；16:21）。
**自主的為奴的。**參 啟 13:16。
18.en:
**Flesh.** Literally, “flesh pieces” (cf. on ch. 17:16).
**Kings.** The confederate nations of earth, acting in concert under the direct supervision of Satan in the guise of an angel of light (cf. on chs. 16:14, 16, 17; 17:12, 14).
**Captains.** The leaders in command of the military forces assembled to carry out Satan’s will in the closing scenes of the great controversy.
**Mighty men.** Armed forces organized, trained, and equipped.
**Flesh of horses.** The remainder of v. 18 is a graphic word picture of the total destruction of all the forces of evil at the second coming of Christ (cf. chs. 6:15; 14:17–20; 16:21).
**Free and bond.** Compare ch. 13:16.

19.zh:
我看見那獸和地上的君王，並他們的眾軍都聚集，要與騎白馬的並他的軍兵爭戰。

**那獸。**見 啟 17:3，8，11 註釋。
**地上的君王。**見 啟 16:14，16；17:12–14 註釋。
**他們的眾軍。**現在要聚在一起彼此殘殺（見 啟 16:17，19 註釋）。
**聚集。**見 啟 16:14，16 的註釋。
**騎。**見 第 11 節註釋。
**祂的軍兵。**參 “同著羔羊的”（啟 17:14；參 啟 16:12；19:14 註釋）。
**爭戰。**就是 “全能者的大日聚集爭戰”，通常被稱為哈米吉多頓戰爭（見 啟 16:14 註釋）。
19.en:
**The beast.** See on ch. 17:3, 8, 11.
**Kings of the earth.** See on chs. 16:14, 16; 17:12–14.
**Their armies.** Now assembled for battle and engaged in bitter conflict among themselves (see on ch. 16:17, 19).
**Gathered together.** See on ch. 16:14, 16.
**War.** Literally, “the war,” that is, “the battle of that great day of God Almighty,” often called the battle of Armageddon (see on ch. 16:14).
**Him that sat.** See on v. 11.
**His army.** Compare “they that are with him” (ch. 17:14; cf. on chs. 16:12; 19:14).

20.zh:
那獸被擒拿；那在獸面前曾行奇事、迷惑受獸印記和拜獸像之人的假先知，也與獸同被擒拿。他們兩個就活活的被扔在燒著硫磺的火湖裡；

**那獸。**見 啟 17:3，8 註釋。
**被擒拿。**基督顯現之後的戰爭進行得十分神速，一開始就把“獸”和“假先知”俘獲了（見 啟 16:17，19 註釋）。
**奇事，迷惑。**見 啟 13:13，14；16:14；17:2；18:2，3，23 註釋。
**獸印記.。**見 啟 13:16 註釋；參 啟 14:9；16:1。
**獸像。**見 啟 13:14；14:9 註釋。
**假先知。**就是受撒但迷惑與他合作的背道的基督教 （見 啟 13:11–17；16:14 註釋）。“先知”是代言人（見 太 11:9 註釋），為“死傷”醫好的頭一個獸說話（見 啟 13:12；17:8 註釋），勸說世人效忠獸。
**火湖。**讀者馬上會想到 啟 20:10 中的“火湖”，以為這兩處指的是同一件事，也就是惡人要在一千年結束時才毀滅。但這就引起了一個問題。第 19 章顯然是指基督復臨時的事件。如果把 啟 19:20 所描述的事件放到一千年之後，就與上下文脫節了。所以最好能找到一種可以符合聖經歷史順序的解釋。關於 啟 19:20，有一種合理的解釋是上帝在一千年的前後有兩次焚燒。說一千年的前後各有一個火湖，就不會再有矛盾了。
關於這一點，懷雅各是這樣寫的：“因此可能存在兩個火湖，一個在一千年之前，一個在一千年之後”（《評論與通訊》，1862年 1月21日）。
20.en:
**The beast.** See on ch. 17:3, 8.
**Taken.** Or, “captured.” The phrase of the battle following Christ’s appearance is short and dramatic, for at its very outset the “beast” and the “false prophet” are captured (see on ch. 16:17, 19).
**False prophet.** That is, apostate Protestantism, which is deluded by Satan and cooperates with him (see on chs. 13:11–17; 16:14). A “prophet” is one who speaks on behalf of another (see on Matt. 11:9). This “prophet” speaks on behalf of the first beast, in connection with the healing of its “deadly wound” (see on chs. 13:12; 17:8), to persuade the world to unite in allegiance to it.
**Miracles … deceived.** See on chs. 13:13, 14; 16:14; 17:2; 18:2, 3, 23.
**Mark of the best.** See on ch. 13:16; cf. chs. 14:9; 16:1.
**Image.** See on chs. 13:14; 14:9.
**A lake of fire.** Or, “the lake which is fire.” This phrase immediately turns the reader’s mind to an identical phrase in ch. 20:10, which in turn seems to call for the conclusion that these phrases refer to the same fiery event, namely, the destruction of the wicked at the end of the thousand years. But to do so presents a problem. The 19th chapter is most evidently discussing events in connection with the second coming of Christ. Hence to hold that the lake of fire mentioned in ch. 19:20 describes an event at the close of the millennium is to lift this verse out of its contextual sequence. It is always better, if possible, to find an explanation that allows any given statement to maintain its historical sequence in a passage of Scripture. As regards ch. 19:20, this is possible on the reasonable premise that there is a fiery judgment from God both at the beginning and at the close of the millennium. There is no inconsistency and certainly no contradiction in speaking of a lake of fire at the beginning and a lake of fire at the end of the millennium.
James White wrote thus on this point: “So, if you please, there are two lakes of fire, one at each end of the one thousand years” (RH Jan. 21, 1862).

21.zh:
其餘的被騎白馬者口中出來的劍殺了；飛鳥都吃飽了他們的肉。

**其餘的。**就是 除了贖民以外地上所有的居民（見 第 20 章補充註釋 2）。
**騎。**見 第 11 節註釋。
**劍。**見 第 15 節註釋。
**飛鳥都。**見 第 17 節註釋。
21.en:
