**The remnant.** Or, “the rest,” that is, all of earth’s inhabitants except the redeemed (see Additional Notes on Chapter 20, Note 2).
**Sword.** See on v. 15.
**Him that sat.** See on v. 11.
**All the fowls.** See on v. 17.

900.zh:
在 啟 12:17中，約翰說到“預言之靈”是“為耶穌作見證的”。這是“餘民”的特徵之一（見 該節註釋）。
“預言”指上帝藉著先知所傳達的任何靈感的信息（見 太 11:9 註釋）。 預言可以是對將來事件的預測，但在一般的情況下卻不是。“預言之靈”是指聖靈以特殊的形式“顯在”人身上，默示人，使他“被聖靈感動” （彼後 1:21），以上帝代表的身份，帶著權威說話（林前 12:7–10）。啟 19:10 的上下文就是從這種意義上來界定“為耶穌作見證” 和“預言之靈”的。鑑於 啟 12:17 中的“其餘的兒女” 特指第 6 節和 14 節中1260 日預言日子結束時，也就是 1798 年以後的教會 （見 但 7:25 註釋），啟 12:17 所指的自然就是預言之“靈”或“恩賜” 在我們今日教會中的特別彰顯。安息日復臨信徒認為懷愛倫的工作以其獨特的方式符合 啟 12:17 的特徵。
聖經作者們先後提到了二十多位當時代享有預言恩賜的人，儘管他們的信息沒有被納入聖經正典。他們中有拿單，迦得，易多，亞迦布等 （撒下 7:2；代上 29:9；代下 9:29；徒 11:27，28；21:10）。 預言的恩賜顯然並不限於男性。在舊約和新約時代都出現過女先知，如底波拉 （士 4:4），戶勒大 （代下 34:22），以及腓利的四個女兒（徒21:9）。
《新約》是作者從來就沒有認為預言的恩賜是到使徒時期教會為止的。相反，保羅宣稱，與他在 弗 4:11所列舉的其他聖靈恩賜一樣，預言的恩賜將繼續存在，“直等到我們眾人在真道上同歸於一，認識上帝的兒子，得以長大成人，滿有基督長成的身量” （第 13 節）。今日的教會依然需要第 11 節所提到的其他特別恩賜，而且聖靈依然分派教會中的男男女女擔任這些職分。為什麼先知的職分就被視為例外呢？
預言的恩賜一直都有贗品存在。不僅舊約時代如此（見 代下 18；耶 27–29），我們的主也曾警告說，基督教會將會受到假先知的擾亂，特別是在祂復臨的前夕 （太 24:11，24）。這些假先知的誘惑力很大。若有可能，連“選民”都被迷惑了。基督既警告在祂復臨前夕會出現預言恩賜的虛假表現，就證明一定會有這種恩賜的真實表現，否則祂就會警告人防備所有的先知了。
與基督的警告相一致的是，約翰勸勉教會要試驗那些聲稱具有屬靈恩賜的人 （約壹 4:1），看看這些恩賜是否是真的。聖經提供了衡量自稱上帝代言人的具體標準： 一， 先知的個人生活應當與聖經的教導一致 （太 7:15–20）。 二， 他的信息要與聖經一致。三， 他的工作要高舉基督為上帝的兒子和人類的救主 （約壹 4:2）。 四， 預言的應驗將證實他的工作 （耶 28:9；參 撒上 3:19）。還有一個合理的標準是，他的信息應該對教會有實際的幫助，並且是及時而合適的，不受任何人所左右。當先知在公開場合見異象時，他的狀態要與聖經的先知相似。懷愛倫的生活，工作和著作完全合乎這些要求。
安息日復臨信徒並不認為懷愛倫的著作是聖經正典的補充或替代。對於復臨信徒來說，聖經是基督徒信仰和行為唯一至高的標準（見 《早期著作》第 78 頁）。用懷愛倫自己的話說，她的著作是“小光，要引導人進入更大的光”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》， 1903年1月 20 日）。預言之靈的著作並不提供新的得救之道。它旨在引導人明白和欣賞聖經，並歡然取飲於其中所啟示的救恩泉源。
有人推測靈感有不同的級別。因此他們認為，與聖經正典的作家相比，底波拉，拿單和亞迦布等先知所得的默示級別較低。他們據此認為懷愛倫所得的默示也是較低級別的。但聖經並沒有提到默示的級別問題，也不對這種觀點提供任何的支持。復臨信徒認為這種推測不僅無用而且還有害。人類有限的頭腦怎能明白上帝如何藉著聖靈去啟發祂所揀選之代言人的思維呢？
關於懷愛倫的一些具體問題，見 尼克爾《懷愛倫和她的批評者》。
900.en:
In ch. 12:17 John speaks of “the testimony of Jesus” which is “the spirit of prophecy” as one of the identifying marks of the “remnant” (see comment there).
The word “prophecy” describes any inspired message communicated by God through a prophet (see on Matt. 11:9). Prophecy may be a prediction of future events, though more commonly it is not. The expression “spirit of prophecy” refers specifically to the “manifestation of the Spirit” in the form of a special gift of the Holy Spirit that inspires the recipient and enables him to speak authoritatively as a representative of God (1 Cor. 12:7–10). when “moved by the Holy Ghost” to do so (2 Peter 1:21). The context of the expression in Rev. 19:10 defines “the testimony of Jesus” and “the spirit of prophecy” in this sense. In view of the fact that the “remnant” of ch. 12:17 specifically refers to the church after the close of the 1260 prophetic days of vs. 6 and 14, that is, after 1798 (see on Dan. 7:25), ch. 12:17 stands as a clear prediction of the special manifestation of the “spirit,” or “gift,” of prophecy in the church in our day. Seventh-day Adventists believe the ministry of Ellen G. White meets the specifications of Rev. 12:17 in a unique way.
The Bible writers refer to more than 20 of their contemporaries who exercised the gift of prophecy, though their messages were not incorporated into the canon. Such were Nathan, Gad, Iddo, Agabus, and others (2 Sam. 7:2; 1 Chron. 29:9; 2 Chron. 9:29; Acts 11:27, 28; 21:10). It is evident, furthermore, that the gift of prophecy was not limited to men, either in OT or in NT times, for there were prophetesses such as Deborah (Judges 4:4), Huldah (2 Chron. 34:22), and the four daughters of Philip (Acts 21:9).
New Testament writers nowhere suggest that the gift of prophecy was to end with the apostolic church. On the contrary, Paul declares that, with the other gifts of the Spirit he lists in Eph. 4:11, it was to continue “till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ” (v. 13). All of the other special gifts mentioned in v. 11 are still needed in the church, and men and women are still qualified by the Holy Spirit to fill these offices. Why should the office of prophet be considered an exception?
There have ever been counterfeit manifestations of the prophetic gift. Not only was this so in OT times (see Chron. 18; Jer. 27–29), but our Lord warned that the Christian church would be troubled by false prophets, particularly as the time for His second advent should draw near (Matt. 24:11, 24). The deceptive power of these false prophets was to be so great that if it were possible they would “deceive the very elect.” The fact that Christ warned against a false manifestation of the prophetic gift prior to His second coming argues strongly that there would also be a genuine manifestation of this gift, as otherwise He could simply have warned against any and all prophets who might arise.
In harmony with Christ’s warning John counsels the church to test those who claim to have been entrusted with spiritual gifts (1 John 4:1), to determine whether these gifts are genuine. The Scriptures specify certain standards by which those who profess to speak for God are to be measured: (1) The personal life of the prophet will be in harmony with the teachings of Scripture (Matt. 7:15–20). (2) His messages will likewise accord with Scripture. (3) His ministry will exalt Christ as the Son of God and the Saviour of men (1 John 4:2). (4) His ministry will be confirmed by fulfilled predictions (Jer. 28:9; cf. 1 Sam. 3:19). It is reasonable also to expect that the messages he bears will be of practical benefit to the church, that they will be timely and appropriate, that they will be free from human influence, and that when he is in open vision his experience will be similar to that of the Bible prophets. The life, ministry, and writings of Ellen G. White fully meet these various requirements.
Seventh-day Adventists do not consider the writings of Ellen G. White as either a substitute for or an addition to the Sacred Canon. For Adventists, the Bible stands unique and supreme as the test of Christian faith and practice (see EW 78), while the writings of Ellen G. White serve, in her own words, as “a lesser light to lead men and women to the greater light” (EGW RH Jan. 20, 1903). The writings of the Spirit of prophecy do not present a new way of salvation, but are designed to lead men to understand and appreciate the Bible, and to avail themselves of the fount of salvation therein revealed.
Some have speculated that there are degrees of inspiration. Accordingly, they consider such prophets, for example, as Deborah, Nathan, and Agabus, as possessing a lower, or inferior, kind of inspiration than the canonical writers. On the same premises they would consider Ellen G. White as possessing a lower, or inferior, kind of inspiration. But the Bible says nothing about degrees of inspiration, nor does it lend any support to the idea. Adventists believe that all such speculation is not only idle but dangerous. How can finite minds hope to understand the mystery of how God, through the Spirit, uniquely illumines the minds of His chosen spokesmen?
For a discussion of certain questions raised regarding Mrs. White see F. D. Nichol, Ellen G. White and Her Critics.

17.en:
**Was wroth.** Or, “was enraged.” Failure to destroy the church in the wilderness intensifies the wrath of the dragon, so much so that he sets about with great determination to wage war upon the people of God, particularly the “remnant of her seed.”
**To make war.** In an endeavor to destroy the Christian church. His supreme effort in this direction is still in the future (see on chs. 13:11–17; 16:12–16; cf. GC 592).
**Remnant.** Gr. loipoi, “remaining ones,” from leipō, “to leave,” “to leave behind.” See Additional Note at end of chapter.
**Keep the commandments.** That the remnant is thus identified indicates that the commandments of God will be especially controverted in this struggle between the dragon and church (see on ch. 14:12; see GC 445–450).
**Testimony of Jesus Christ.** Or, “witness of Jesus Christ.” In the Greek this phrase may be understood either as the “testimony” (or “witness”) Christians bear concerning Jesus or as the “testimony” (or “witness”) that originates with Jesus and is revealed to His church through the prophets (see on ch. 1:2). A comparison with ch. 19:10 clearly favors the latter interpretation. There the “testimony of Jesus” is defined as the “spirit of prophecy,” meaning that Jesus is witnessing to the church through the medium of prophecy.
The close relationship between the “testimony of Jesus” and prophecy is further demonstrated by a comparison between chs. 19:10 and 22:9. In ch. 19:10 the angel identifies himself as “thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus,” and in ch. 22:9 as “thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets.” Thus, on the reasonable conclusion that these two expressions of the angel are parallel, those who have the testimony of Jesus are identified with the prophets. Since it is the distinctive work of the prophets to bear messages from Jesus to the people (see on ch. 1:1), the interpretation that the testimony of Jesus refers to the “testimony,” or “witness,” that Jesus bears to the church is strongly supported. Seventh-day Adventists thus interpret the passage and believe that the “remnant” will be distinguished by the manifestation of the gift of prophecy in their midst. The “testimony of Jesus Christ,” they believe, is the witness of Jesus in their midst through the medium of the prophetic gift. See Additional Note on Chapter 19.
17.zh:
龍向婦人發怒，去與他其餘的兒女爭戰，這兒女就是那守神誡命、為耶穌作見證的。那時龍就站在海邊的沙上。

**發怒。**龍因未能消滅在曠野中的教會而越發生氣了。他決心要與上帝的子民，特別是“她其餘的兒女”決戰。
**其餘的的兒女。**loipoi。源於動詞leipoµ，“留下”，“剩下”。見本章補充註釋。
**爭戰。**撒但企圖摧毀基督教會的最大行動尚有待將來（見 啟 13:11–17 ；16:12–16 註釋；參《善惡之爭》592頁）。
**守上帝誡命。**這裡所指出餘民的特徵表明，龍與教會這場鬥爭的焦點是上帝的誡命（見 啟 14:12 註釋；參 《善惡之爭》445-450頁）。
**為耶穌作見證。**或“有耶穌的見證。” 原文既可以理解為基督徒為耶穌所作的“見證”，也可理解為耶穌的藉著眾先知啟示教會的“見證”（見 啟 1:2 解釋）。參照啟 19:10 ，後一種理解顯然更為恰當。在啟 19:10中，“有耶穌的見證”被界定為“預言中的靈意”（預言之靈），就是耶穌藉著預言給教會作見證。
將 啟 19:10 和 啟 22:9 相對照，就更加說明了“耶穌的見證”與預言之間的密切聯繫。在 啟 19:10中，天使說自己與  “那些為耶穌作見證的弟兄是同作僕人的”。在 啟 22:9中，天使說自己和“你的弟兄眾先知”“同是作僕人的。”根據這兩節經文的平行關係，可以把為耶穌作見證的人理解為眾先知。先知的特殊工作就是把耶穌的見證傳達給百姓（見 啟 1:1 註釋），因此，把“耶穌的見證”解釋成耶穌給教會的“見證”或“證言”是有充分理由的。安息日復臨信徒是如此解釋這段經文的，並相信“餘民”的特徵就是在他們中間有預言的恩賜。他們認為“耶穌基督的見證”就是耶穌藉著預言的恩賜傳達給他們的見證。見 第 19 章補充註釋。
**龍就站在。**龍站在沙灘上等待獸的出現，要將自己的權柄授予獸（啟 13:2）。有文本為“我就站在”。
**海邊的沙。**這裡的海無疑指多民，多國和多方（見 啟 17:1, 2, 8註釋；參但 7:2 註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第398頁；《善惡之爭》第592頁；《先知與君王》第605頁；《給傳道人的證言》第39，133頁；《證言》卷一第223，330，337頁；《證言》卷二第105頁；《證言》卷三第110，571頁；《證言》卷五第213，449，472，《證言》卷八第41，117頁。

11.en:
**They overcame.** The mind of the prophet is absorbed in contemplation of those who have been accused by the instigator of evil. He thinks of how they have suffered, and the indignities to which they have been exposed. He remembers how amid hardships they overcame, not in their own strength, but “by the blood of the Lamb.”
**By the blood.** Literally, “because of the blood,” or “on the basis of the blood.” The saints overcame because of the victory of Calvary. For the significance of the “blood” see on Rev. 1:5; cf. on Rom. 5:9.
**Lamb.** See on John 1:29.
**By the word.** Literally, “on account of the word,” or “on the basis of the word.”
**Their testimony.** That is, their personal witness concerning Jesus and the gospel.
**Loved not their lives.** What fidelity! Men would die rather than disobey God. See on John 12:25.
11.zh:
弟兄勝過他，是因羔羊的血和自己所見證的道。他們雖至於死，也不愛惜性命。

**勝過它。**先知的思想集中在那些曾受到罪惡的發動者指控的人身上。他想到他們所受的痛苦和屈辱。他想起他們是怎樣在逆境中得勝的，不是憑自己的力量，而是靠“羔羊的血。”
**羔羊。**見 約 1:29 註釋。
**因羔羊的血。**直譯為“因血的緣故，”或“在血的基礎上。”聖徒得勝是因為十字架的勝利。關“血”的意義 ，見 啟 1:5 註釋；參 羅 5:9 註釋。
**和自己所將見證的道.。**直譯為“因為道的緣故，”或“在道的基礎上。”
**自己所見證。**就是關於耶穌和福音的個人見證。
**也不愛惜性命。**多麼忠誠啊！他們寧死也不願背叛上帝。見 約 12:25 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《論飲食》第162，186頁；《早期著作》第114頁；《善惡之爭》第十一章；《今日的生活》第141頁；《醫療佈道論》第264，296頁；《給青年人的信息》第347頁；《先祖與先知》第77頁；《成聖的人生》第78頁。

10.en:
**A loud voice.** There is great rejoicing in the courts of heaven over the casting down of Satan and his host.
**Now is come.** The focus of time is the cross (see on vs. 7, 9). Well might the inhabitants of heaven rejoice, for Satan’s destruction was now assured. It was certain in the plan of God before, but now heavenly intelligences joined in the song, for they had seen Satan’s malignity against Christ revealed at Calvary.
**Salvation.** Gr. sōtēria, “deliverance,” “preservation,” “salvation,” here, perhaps, “victory.” The Greek has the article, hence we should read “the victory.”
**Strength.** Gr. dunamis, “power,” “might,” “strength.” The reference here is doubtless to the display of power in the overthrow of the dragon.
**Kingdom.** Satan had contended that he was the rightful ruler of this world. His failure to lead Jesus into sin assured the kingdom for Christ.
**Power.** Gr. exousia, “authority.”
**His Christ.** Or, “His Anointed.” Christ means “anointed” (see on Matt. 1:1).
**The accuser.** Satan was the accuser of the brethren in OT days (see Job 1:8–12; Zech. 3:1). This role he has continued since the cross, but in a restricted sense (see on John 12:31; cf. DA 761). Rabbinical writings frequently represent Satan as the great accuser (see Talmud Sanhedrin 89b, Soncino ed., p. 595; Midrash Rabbah, on Ex. 32:2, Soncino ed., p. 494).
**Brethren.** Compare ch. 6:11.
**Day and night.** That is, whenever the opportunity presented itself.
10.zh:
我聽見在天上有大聲音說：我神的救恩、能力、國度、並他基督的權柄，現在都來到了！因為那在我們神面前晝夜控告我們弟兄的，已經被摔下去了。

**大聲音。**天庭因撒但及其使者被摔下來而歡喜快樂。
**救恩。**soteria。“拯救”，“保護”之意。在這裡可能指“勝利”。原文帶有定冠詞。
**能力。**在這裡無疑指在推翻龍時所展示的能力。。
**國度。**撒但曾聲稱自己是這個世界的合法主宰。他引誘耶穌犯罪的失敗，註定了基督國度的建立。
**權柄。**“權威”之意。
**祂基督。**或 “祂的受膏者。”基督”意為“受膏者”（見 太 1:1 註釋）。
**現在都來到。**發生在主釘十字架之時（見 第 7，9 節註釋）。 天庭的居民有充分的理由高興，因為撒但的滅亡已經是註定的了。雖然這在上帝的計劃中是早已確定的，但現在天上的生靈要加入歌唱，因為他們已經看見撒但在髑髏地所暴露出來的對基督的狠毒。
**那在我們上帝面前晝夜控告。**撒但在舊約時代就是控告弟兄的（見 伯 1:8–12；亞 3:1）。主釘十字架以後他繼續控告弟兄，但受到了限制（見 約12:31 註釋；參 《歷代願望》 761頁）。拉比的著作常把撒但稱成大控告者（見 《塔木德》，595頁；出 32:2《米德拉什》，494頁.）。
**晝夜。**意為只要有機會。
**我們弟兄。**參 啟 6:11。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《天路》第166頁；《歷代願望》第626，761頁；《善惡之爭》第395，520頁；《福山寶訓》第57頁；《先知與君王》第585頁；《先祖與先知》第689頁；《給傳道人的證言》第37，504頁；《證言》卷二第106頁；《證言》卷五第34，95，137，286，470，620頁；《證言》卷六第11頁；【 SDA7.974】。

8.en:
**Prevailed not.** Inasmuch as the phrase “war in heaven” (v. 7) may have a dual application, describing both the original controversy in heaven between Lucifer and God and the controversy on earth between Satan and the incarnate Christ, the phrase “prevailed not” would appropriately apply to both stages of the conflict. In neither was Satan successful.
**Their place.** This phrase may be understood either as the place once possessed, or occupied, by them, or the place once assigned them. Lucifer was at one time the covering cherub (see on Eze. 28:14), and the angels who joined him in rebellion held various positions of responsibility. These, Lucifer and his angels lost when they were cast out of heaven.
8.zh:
並沒有得勝，天上再沒有他們的地方。

**並沒有得勝。**與“在天上就有了爭戰”（第 7 節）一樣，這句話也可以有兩層意思，既可指路錫甫與上帝在天上所開始的鬥爭，也可指撒但與道成肉身之基督在地上的鬥爭。“並沒有得勝”對於這兩個階段都合適。撒但都沒有取得成功。
**他們的地方。**既可理解成他們所佔領的地方，也可理解為分配給他們的地方。路錫甫曾是遮掩約櫃的基路伯（見 結 28:14 註釋）。那些與他一起背叛的天使也曾有各自的職位。當路錫甫和他的使者被逐出天庭之後，這一切權利都喪失了。

7.en:
**And there was.** Literally, “and there became.”
**War in heaven.** John now presents briefly the history of the great controversy between Satan and Christ in heaven, from its origin to the time of Christ’s victory at the cross (Rev. 12:7–9; cf. Col. 2:14, 15), the final casting out of Satan at that time to this earth (Rev. 12:10–12), and the course of the controversy on earth down to the time of the end (Rev. 12:13–16; see on Dan. 11:35). This brief survey stands as a background for the extended delineation of developments in the conflict during the time of the end, by means of which it is finally and successfully terminated (Rev. 12:17 to 20:15).
In ch. 12:9–11 John speaks most particularly of the phase of the conflict waged in heaven in connection with Christ’s death on the cross. For contextual evidence that points to this conclusion see on v. 9.
Though the revelator is focusing primarily on the turning point of the controversy reached at the time of the cross, it is proper to understand the words, “there was war in heaven,” as referring also to the time prior to the creation of the earth, when the hostility of the dragon began, and Lucifer aspired to be like God (see on Isa. 14:13, 14; Eze. 28:12–16). At that time he and the angels who symphatized with him were expelled from heaven (see 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6). The loyal angels did not then understand fully all the issues involved. But when Satan basely shed the blood of Christ, he stood exposed completely and forever before the heavenly world. Henceforth his activities were further restricted (see DA 761).
**Michael.** Gr. Michaēl, a transliteration of the Heb. mika’el, meaning “who [is] like God?” Michael is referred to as “one of the chief princes” (Dan. 10:13), as “the great prince” (Dan. 12:1), and also as “the archangel” (Jude 9). Jewish literature described Michael as the highest of the angels, the true representative of God, and identified him with the angel of Jehovah (see Talmud Yoma 37a, Soncino ed., p. 172; Midrash Rabbah, on Gen. 18:3; Ex. 3:2, Soncino ed., pp. 411, 53). According to Midrash Rabbah, on Ex. 12:29, Michael was the angel who vindicated Israel against Satan’s accusations (Soncino ed., p. 222). A careful examination of the Scripture references to Michael points to the conclusion that he is none other than our blessed Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ (see on Dan. 10:13; cf. on Jude 9).
**His angels.** That is, the loyal angels, the “ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation” (Heb. 1:14).
**Dragon.** See on v. 3.
**His angels.** That is, the angels who sided with Satan in his warfare against Christ (see on v. 4).
7.zh:
在天上就有了爭戰。米迦勒同他的使者與龍爭戰，龍也同他的使者去爭戰，

**就有了。**“開始了。”
**在天上 . . . 爭戰。**約翰現在簡單敘述了基督和撒但在天上大斗爭的歷史，從它的開始到基督在十字架上取得得勝（啟 12:7–9；參 西 2:14，15），最終將撒但摔到地上（啟 12:10–12），以及大斗爭在地上的進程，直到世界的末日（啟 12:13–16；見 但 11:35 註釋）。這段簡介構成了末後善惡之爭進程細節描述的背景。這場鬥爭最後將取得勝利（啟 12:17 -  20:15）。
**在。**啟 12:9–11中，約翰特別講述了天上的爭戰與基督在十字架上受死的聯繫。關於這個結論的內證 ，見 第 9 節註釋。
雖然蒙啟示的約翰所強調的是善惡之爭在十字架上的轉折點，我們仍可把“在天上就有了爭戰”理解為創造地球以前的時候。那時龍對基督就有了敵意。路錫甫妄想能像上帝一樣（見 賽 14:13，14 註釋；結 28:12–16）。於是他和同情他的天使就被趕出了天庭（見 彼後 2:4；猶 6）。 那時忠心的天使還沒有完全認識到事情的根由。但當撒但卑鄙地殺害了基督後，他就在全天庭面前完全徹底地暴露了他的真面目。從此，他的行動受到了進一步限制（見 《歷代願望》 761頁）。
**米迦勒。**Michaeµl。譯自希伯來語mika’el，意思是“有誰象上帝？” 米迦勒被稱為“天使長”（ 但 10:13和猶 9）和“大君”（但 12:1）。猶太文獻稱米迦勒是天使中地位最高的，為上帝的真正代表。他就是耶和華的使者（見 《塔木德》 Yoma， 172頁；創 18:3，出 3:2《米德拉什》411，53頁）。 出 12:29《米德拉什》（註釋）說，米迦勒是駁斥撒但控告，為以色列人辯護的天使（222頁）。經過仔細審視聖經各處所提到的米迦勒，可以得出結論說，祂就是我們神聖的主救主耶穌基督（見 但 10:13 註釋；參 猶 9 註釋）。
**祂的使者。**即忠實的天使，就是“服役的靈，奉差遣為那將要承受救恩的人效力的（來 1:14）。
**龍。**參 第 3 節註釋。
**他的使者。**就是在反叛基督的戰爭中站在撒但一邊的天使（參 第 4 節）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第146頁；《證言》卷三第328頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–9節）**。《救贖的故事》第19頁；《證言》卷一第440頁；《證言》卷六第456頁；見結28：15，19；弗6：12；約壹2：6懷愛倫註釋。。

9.en:
**The great dragon.** See on v. 3.
**Was cast out.** Satan and his angels were cast out of heaven in ages past (2 Peter 2:4), prior to the creation of this world (PP 36–42; cf. EW 145, 146; GC 498–500; 3SG 36–39; 1SP 17–33). Nevertheless, it seems that until the cross he had access to heavenly beings, and to a limited extent, possibly as “prince of this world” (John 12:31; Luke 4:6), but not as an inhabitant of heaven, to the precincts of heaven (DA 761; cf. SR 26, 27; see below on “into the earth”). However this may be, a decisive casting out occurred at the cross, as our Lord Himself declared (John 12:31, 32; cf. PP 68–70; DA 490, 679, 758). That John here (Rev. 12:9) refers most particularly to events connected with Christ’s triumph on the cross is evident from the context (vs. 10–13). The following points may be noted: 1. The proclamation in vs. 10–12 by a “loud voice … in heaven” is more or less parenthetical, its purpose being to explain the significance of the casting down of Satan in v. 9, first with respect to the inhabitants of heaven and then to those of this earth. Following this explanatory parenthesis, v. 13 takes up the narrative of Satan’s activities at the point where it was left in v. 9. Accordingly, vs. 10–12 constitute, primarily, a statement concerning the status of the plan of salvation at the point of time when Satan was “cast out into the earth.” 2. The first declaration by the “loud voice” consists of a series of facts relative to Christ’s triumph over Satan on the cross—the plan of “salvation” was made sure, “strength” was provided for resisting the wiles of Satan, Christ’s “kingdom” was made sure, and His “power,” literally, “authority,” to be man’s Saviour, high priest, and king was confirmed (Matt. 28:18; GC 503). 3. The reason assigned in Rev. 12:10 for this fourfold achievement is specifically said to be that “the accuser of our brethren is cast down.” This clearly links these accomplishments with the casting down of v. 9. 4. At the time of the casting down of vs. 9, 10, 13 “the accuser of our brethren” had already been actively accusing “them before our God day and night.” Obviously, the fall here referred to came after a period during which Satan had been accusing “the brethren,” and it would therefore appear that this cannot be the original casting out of Satan prior to the creation of our earth. 5. Verse 11 specifically states that it was “the blood of the Lamb”—the death of Christ upon the cross—that had made victory over the “accuser of our brethren” possible.
**Old.** Gr. archaios, “ancient,” “old,” from archē, “beginning.” Our English word “archaic” comes from archaios. Compare John 8:44.
**Serpent.** A reference to the serpent who deceived Eve (Gen. 3:1).
**Devil.** Gr. diabolos, “a slanderer” (see on Matt. 4:1).
**Satan.** Gr. Satanas, a transliteration of the Heb. śaṭan, meaning “adversary” (see on Zech. 3:1).
**Deceiveth.** Gr. planaō, “to cause to wander,” “to lead astray,” “to deceive” (see on Matt. 18:12).
**World.** Gr. oikoumenē, literally, the “inhabited [world],” from oikeō, “to dwell” (see on Matt. 4:8).
**Into the earth.** The controversy in heaven began over plans for the creation of man (see 3SG 36). When the earth was created and Adam was appointed its vicegerent, Satan directed his efforts at overthrowing the newly created man. When he succeeded in bringing about the downfall of Adam and Eve he claimed the earth as his domain (see on Matt. 4:8, 9). However, he did not confine his efforts to this earth but tempted also the inhabitants of other worlds (see EW 290). Not until the second coming of Christ will Satan be completely confined to this earth (see on Rev. 20:3; cf. EW 290; DA 490).
9.zh:
大龍就是那古蛇，名叫魔鬼，又叫撒但，是迷惑普天下的。他被摔在地上，他的使者也一同被摔下去。

**大龍。**見 第 3 節註釋。
**古。**archaios 。源於 archeµ（起初）。參 約 8:44。
**蛇。**指那條曾迷惑夏娃的蛇（創 3:1）。
**魔鬼。**diabolos。誹謗者。見太 4:1 註釋。
**撒但。**Satanas。譯自希泊來語satan，意為“敵人”（見 亞 3:1註釋）。
**迷惑。**planaoµ。“欺騙”，“誤導”（見 太 18:12 註釋）。
**普天下。**oikoumeneµ，“有人居住的世界。”]源於 oikeoµ ，“居住”（見太 4:8 註釋）。
**被摔。**撒但和他的使者們遠在世界創造之先就被逐出了天庭 （彼後 2:4，《先祖與先知》36–42頁；參 《早期著作》第 145，146 頁；《善惡之爭》498–500頁；《屬靈的恩賜》 卷 三第 36–39 頁；《預言之靈》 卷一第 17–33 頁）。在主釘十字架之前，撒但還能接觸天上的生靈，並在有限的範圍內作這“世界的王”（約12:31；路 4:6）。但他不是天上的居民，不能住在天上（《歷代願望》 761頁；參 《救贖的故事》26，27；見以下“在地上”的註釋）。不管怎樣，撒但在主釘十字架時的“被摔”乃是決定性的，正如主所親宣佈的那樣（約 12:31，32；參 《先祖與先知》68–70頁；《歷代願望》490，679，758頁）。從上下文中可以看出（第 10–13節），約翰在這裡 （啟 12:9）主要是指與基督在十字架上的勝利有關的事件。請注意以下幾點：
1.	第 10–12節“天上 . . . 大聲音”的宣告是一段插敘，其目的是為了解釋第 9 節將撒但摔到地上的意義，先是涉及天上的居民，再是涉及地上的居民。在這段解釋性的插敘之後是第 13 節，繼續第 9 節敘述撒但的行為。因此，第 10–12 節主要是說明撒但被摔到地上時，救贖計劃的執行情況。
2.	“大聲音”第一次宣告了與基督在十字架上的勝利有關的一系列事實：“救恩”的計劃落實了；抵制撒但詭計的“能力”賜予了；基督的“國度”建立了；祂作為人類救主、大祭司及君王的“權柄”也確立了（太 28:18；《善惡之爭》 503頁）。
3. 啟 12:10 指出，這四項成就的原因是“那 . . . 控告我們弟兄的，已經被摔下去了。”說明這些成就是與第 9 節撒但的“被摔”聯繫在一起的。
4.	“那 . .. 控告弟兄的”在第 9，10，13 節的“被摔”之前，就在 “上帝面前晝夜不停地”進行控告。顯然這裡的“被摔”發生在撒但控告了“弟兄”一段時間之後。因此不可能是在創世之前的那一次被摔。
5.	第 11 節特別指出，戰勝“那 . . . 控告弟兄的”，是因為“羔羊的血”，就是基督在十字架上的犧牲。
**在地上。**天上的鬥爭起因於創造人類的計劃（參 《屬靈的恩賜》 卷 三 第 36 頁）。當地球剛被造好，亞當被任命為其中的管理者時，撒但就開始致力於毀滅新造的人類了。當他成功地引誘亞當和夏娃墮落之後，就聲稱地球是屬於他的領土（見 太 4:8，9 註釋）。但他的活動不限於這個地球。他還要去誘惑其他世界的居民（見 《早期著作》第 290 頁）。直到基督再來，撒但才被完全限制在這個地球上（見 啟 20:3 註釋；參 《早期著作》第 290 頁；《歷代願望》490頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第215頁；《善惡之爭》第438，582頁；《先祖與先知》第77，331，431頁。

6.en:
**Wilderness.** Gr. erēmos, “a forsaken, desert, empty place,” “an uninhabited place.” Here erēmos doubtless represents a place of seclusion or obscurity, an area or condition in which the church would be in a place of obscurity, away from the public gaze. See on ch. 17:3.
**A place.** This place is referred to in v. 14 as “her place.” The idea is that the protection and sanctuary in obscurity here found by the woman were divinely appointed and prepared.
**They.** The subject is indefinite and doubtless refers to the various agencies God employed to preserve, strengthen, and build up the church during the time when she was severely persecuted.
**Feed.** Gr. trephō, “to make to grow,” “to bring up,” “to rear,” “to nourish.” Trephō is rendered “nourished” in v. 14. God cares for His own. Even though the church is persecuted and driven into exile the Lord nourishes it.
**Days.** This period of 1260 days is referred to seven times in the books of Daniel and Revelation. As 1260 days it appears in Rev. 11:3; 12:6; as 42 months in Rev. 11:2; 13:5; and as 3 1/2 times in Dan. 7:25; 12:7; Rev. 12:14. For the calculation of this period see on Dan. 7:25. Adventists generally date this period as from .. 538 to .. 1798. During this period God’s hand was over the church, preserving it from extinction.
6.zh:
婦人就逃到曠野，在那裡有神給他預備的地方，使他被養活一千二百六十天。

**曠野。**ereµmos。“荒蕪”，“空曠”，“無人居住之處”。在這裡無疑指與世隔絕，遠離公眾的注意的教會藏身之處。參 啟 17:3 註釋。
**地方。**這就是 第 14 節所提到的“自己的地方。”說明那女子所找到的隱身之處實際上是上帝所安排和預備的。
**使她被養活。**原文沒有提到行為主體。但無疑是指教會在蒙受嚴重逼迫時，上帝藉著多種途徑保護，加強和建設祂的教會。
**養活。**參第 14 節。上帝眷顧祂的教會。即使教會遭受逼迫，被迫流亡，上帝仍然養育它。
**一千二百六十天。**一千二百六十日在《但以理書》和《啟示錄》中共提到過七次。在 啟 11:3；12:6中為一千二百六十日；在啟 11:2；13:5中為42 個月；在 但 7:25；12:7；啟 12:14中為三年半。關於這段時間的計算，見 但 7:25 註釋。復臨信徒一般認為這段時間是從公元 538 年開始，到 1798 年結束的。在這段時期裡，上帝的手護庇著教會，使她不致滅絕。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第55，266頁；《救贖的故事》第331頁。

1.zh:
天上現出大異象來：有一個婦人身披日頭，腳踏月亮，頭戴十二星的冠冕。

**天上。**這裡無疑指的是天空，而不是上帝所住的天庭。關於象徵性異象的性質，見 結 1:10 註釋。
**現出。**本章開始了新一輪的預言，延續到《啟示錄》的結束，表現上帝的教會與邪惡勢力所作的的鬥爭，以及教會最終取得了勝利。
**大異象。**seµmeion，“記號”，“標誌”。源於動詞 seµmaino（“發信號”，“給記號”，“指示”，見 啟 1:1 註釋）。 該詞常譯為“神蹟” （路 23:8；約 4:54）。神蹟是權柄的標誌（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷 五，第 209 頁）。 在 啟 12:1中， seµmeion指即將發生之事件的徵兆。
**婦人。**在《舊約》聖經的表號中，真教會有時用女子來代表（賽 54:5，6；耶 6:2）。 教會背道時，就被比作墮落的女子（耶 3:20；結 23:2–4）。 這樣的表號也出現在《新約》裡（林後 11:2；弗 5:25–32；啟 17:1–3）。
《啟示錄》12章的女子代表真教會。她即將生育基督（見 第 2，4，5 節），並在基督昇天之後受到迫害（第 5，13–17 節）。她代表舊約和新約時代的教會。參 徒 7:38。
**身披日頭。**可以被理解為代表上帝的榮耀，特別是福音所顯示的榮耀。相比之下，那個代表假教會的女人則被描寫成穿著華麗而俗氣的衣裳，手持充滿了邪淫的酒杯（啟 17:4）。
**腳踏月亮。**許多解經家認為這個表號代表舊約時代的整個表號體系。它在基督更大的啟示中黯然失色。月亮代表基督的生與死所應驗的儀文律法。它只是反映了太陽的光輝。
**十二星。**解經家們一般將這個表號解釋為十二位先祖或十二位使徒。因為 啟 12 章的重點在新約教會，所以這裡無疑主要是指十二位使徒。同時十二支派的畫面也穿插在新約教會之中（見 啟 7:4 註釋）。
**冠冕。**stephanos ，勝利的冠冕（見太 27:29 ；啟 2:10 註釋），而不是 diadeµma （“王冠”，見啟 12:3 註釋）。
1.en:
**There appeared.** Chapter 12 begins a new line of prophecy, which continues to the end of the book. This section of prophecy sets forth the church of God in conflict with the powers of evil, and the church’s ultimate triumph over them.
**Wonder.** Gr. sēmeion, “a sign,” “a mark,” “a token,” from sēmaino, “to give a sign,” “to signify,” “to indicate” (see on ch. 1:1). The word is frequently translated “miracle” (Luke 23:8; John 4:54) where a miracle is described from the point of view of a sign of authority (see Vol. V, p. 209). In Rev. 12:1 sēmeion means a sign portending forthcoming events.
**Heaven.** Here doubtless meaning the sky, not the heaven where God dwells. For the nature of symbolic visions see on Eze. 1:10.
**Woman.** In OT figure the true church is at times represented by a woman (Isa. 54:5, 6; Jer. 6:2). When the church apostatized it was compared with a corrupt woman (Jer. 3:20; Eze. 23:2–4). The same figures appear in the NT (2 Cor. 11:2; Eph. 5:25–32; Rev. 17:1–3).
In Rev. 12 the woman represents the true church. Since she is presented as about to give birth to Christ (see vs. 2, 4, 5) and later as being persecuted, following the ascension of Christ (vs. 5, 13–17), she represents the church of both the OT and the NT. Compare Acts 7:38.
**Clothed with the sun.** This may be thought of as representing the glory of God, especially as revealed in the gospel. By contrast the woman representing the false church is portrayed as arrayed in gaudy garments and as carrying a cup filled with abominations (ch. 17:4).
**Moon.** This symbol is understood by many commentators as representing the system of types and shadows of OT times, which were eclipsed by the greater revelation that came through Christ. The ceremonial law, being fulfilled in the life and death of Christ, could well be represented by the moon, which shines with light borrowed from the sun.
**Crown.** Gr. stephanos, a victor’s crown (see on Matt. 27:29; Rev. 2:10), not diadēma, a kingly crown (see on ch. 12:3).
**Twelve stars.** In general commentators have applied this symbol to either the 12 patriarchs or the 12 apostles or to both. Since the principal emphasis in ch. 12 is on the NT church, the emphasis is doubtless on the 12 apostles. At the same time, the picture of 12 tribes is also carried over into the NT church (see on Rev. 7:4).

2.zh:
他懷了孕，在生產的艱難中疼痛呼叫。

這裡的教會處在彌賽亞即將誕生的時期。有人認為這裡是引用 賽 7:14。關於產難女人的象徵意義，見 賽 26:17；66:7，8。
2.en: **With child.** The church is presented at the time the Messiah is about to be born. Some see a reference to Isa. 7:14. For the figure of a travailing woman see Isa. 26:17; 66:7, 8.

3.zh:
天上又現出異象來：有一條大紅龍，七頭十角；七頭上戴著七個冠冕。

**異象。**見 第 1 節註釋。
**紅龍。**第 9 節說，大龍就是“那古蛇，名叫魔鬼，又叫撒但。” 這裡象徵撒但藉著異教的羅馬活動。異教的羅馬在耶穌降生時統治著世界（見 第 4 節註釋；參 《善惡之爭》438頁， 第 25 章）。說龍是 “紅”色的，可能是因為在涉及上帝教會一切事上，它都扮演著逼迫者和破壞者的角色。它處心積慮地要消滅至高者的兒女。
**七頭。**約翰所見從海中上來的獸（啟 13:1）和硃紅色的獸（啟 17:3）也有七個頭。在 啟 17:9，10 中， 七頭代表“七座山”和“七位王。” 因此可以推定龍的七頭代表維護龍之事業的政治勢力。龍藉著這些政治勢力實施逼迫。有人認為這裡的“七”是一個大概的數字，象徵著完全，而不一定代表為撒但工作的七個國家。參 啟 17:9，10 註釋。
關於古代神話中七頭之蛇，見 賽 27:1 註釋。《塔木德》也提到過一個七頭之龍（141頁）。
**十角。**13 章的獸和 17 章的獸都有十個角。有人認為龍的十角就是那兩個獸的十角。而獸的十角又與 但 7 章裡第四獸的十角相同。關於《但以理書》第四獸的身份，見 但 7:7 註釋。還有人認為龍的十角只是泛指為撒但工作的小國，而七頭則代表大的政治勢力（見以上 “七頭”的註釋）。他們認為“十”只是一個大概的數字，就像聖經其他地方一樣（見 路 15:8 註釋）。參 啟 17:9，10 註釋。
**頭上。**七頭戴著王室的標記，進一步證明它們代表國家政權（見 以上“七頭”的註釋）。
**冠冕。**希臘文為 diadeµmata。單數為 diadeµma。意為“系在周圍之物”。源於動詞diadeoµ。意為“系在周圍”。該詞曾用來指波斯國王的標誌，即頭巾上鑲著白邊的蘭色絲帶。所以該詞代表王室的標誌。Diadeµmata 只出現在本節和啟 13:1 ，以及 啟 19:12 中。Diadeµma 與 stephanos 相對。stephanos在《新約》中也譯為“冠冕”（太 27:29；林前 9:25；提後 4:8等）。 stephanos 是花環，往往是花冠或項圈，作為勝利者的獎賞（見 林前 9:25 註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第92頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《善惡之爭》第438頁。
3.en:
**Wonder.** Gr. sēmeion (see on v. 1).
**Red dragon.** In v. 9 the power thus represented is identified as “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan.” Here the symbol represents Satan as working through pagan Rome, the power ruling the world when Jesus was born (see on v. 4; cf. GC 438). The dragon is described as “red,” probably because of the fact that in all his connection with the church of God he has appeared in the role of persecutor and destroyer. It has been his studied purpose to destroy the children of the Most High.
**Seven Heads.** Seven heads appear also on the beast John saw rising from the sea (Rev. 13:1), and on the scarlet-colored beast (ch. 17:3). The heads in ch. 17:9, 10 are identified as “seven mountains” and “seven kings.” It seems reasonable to conclude that the seven heads of the dragon represents political powers that have championed the cause of the dragon, and through which the dragon has exercised his persecuting power. Some hold that the number “seven” is here used as a round number denoting completeness, and that it is not necessary to find precisely seven nations through whom Satan has operated. Compare on ch. 17:9, 10.
For a description of the seven-headed serpent in ancient mythology see on Isa. 27:1. The Talmud also mentions a dragon with seven heads (Ḳiddushin 29b, Soncino ed., p. 141).
**Ten horns.** The beast of ch. 13 and that of ch. 17 also had ten horns each. Some hold the ten horns of the dragon to be identical with those of these two beasts, and the latter to be identical with the ten horns of the fourth beast of Dan. 7. For an identification of the ten horns of Daniel’s fourth beast see on Dan. 7:7. Others see in the ten horns of the dragon a more general designation for the minor political powers through which Satan has operated, in contrast with the seven heads, which may be regarded as representing the major political powers (see above on “seven heads”). They suggest that the number “ten” may be a round number, as so often elsewhere in Scripture (see on Luke 15:8). Compare on Rev. 17:9, 10.
**Crowns.** Gr. diadēmata, singular diadēma, literally, “something bound around,” from diadeō, “to bind around.” The word was used to describe the badge of kingship worn by Persian kings, a blue ribbon trimmed with white, worn on the turban. Hence the word came to be used as a badge of royalty. Diadēmata occurs only here and in chs. 13:1 and 19:12. Diadēma is contrasted with stephanos, also translated “crown” in the NT (Matt. 27:29; 1 Cor. 9:25; 2 Tim. 4:8; etc.). Stephanos is a wreath, often signifying the garland, or chaplet, given as a prize for victory (see on 1 Cor. 9:25).
**Upon his heads.** The fact that the heads are wearing badges of royalty may be taken as further evidence that they represent political kingdoms (see above on “seven heads”).

4.zh:
他的尾巴拖拉著天上星辰的三分之一，摔在地上。龍就站在那將要生產的婦人面前，等他生產之後，要吞吃他的孩子。

**他的尾巴拖拉。**約翰在預言的異象中看到這一行為正在發生。
**三分之一。**有人認為這裡所象徵的事件，在 第 7-9 節裡得到進一步描述。“天上星辰的三分之一”代表三分之一的天使參加路錫甫的叛亂，後被趕出天庭（見 《證言》 卷三第 115 頁；《證言》 卷 五第 291 頁）。 還有人把“星辰”解釋為猶太的領袖。他們分成三類：國王，祭司和猶太公會。三分之一摔在了地上，解釋為取消猶大的王位。
**要吞吃。**象徵撒但要殺害嬰孩耶穌。從希律王聽到博士們報告後的反應來看（太 2:16），本節的象徵性描述是非常貼切的。在以後的歲月中，異教的羅馬起來反對“萬王之王” 見 但 8:25 註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷三第115頁；《證言》卷五第291頁。
4.en:
**His tail drew.** Literally, “his tail is drawing.” In prophetic vision John saw the action in progress.
**The third part.** Some believe that the event here symbolized is further described in vs. 7–9, and that “the third part of the stars of heaven” represents a third part of the heavenly angels, who joined Lucifer in his rebellion and were expelled from heaven (see 3T 115; 5T 291). Others interpret the “stars” as Jewish rulers, of which there were three classes—kings, priests, and the Sanhedrin. A third part being cast to the ground they interpret as Rome’s taking away of the kingship from Judah.
**To devour.** This represents the efforts of Satan to destroy the infant Jesus. One needs only to recall the attitude of Herod as he listened to the message from the wise men (Matt. 2:16, to perceive the appropriateness of this figurative description of the event. In later years pagan Rome stood up against the “Prince of princes” �see on Dan. 8:25).

5.zh:
婦人生了一個男孩子，是將來要用鐵杖轄管（轄管：原文是牧）萬國的；他的孩子被提到神寶座那裡去了。

**男孩子。**“兒子。”
**轄管萬國。**引自 詩 2:8，9。顯然指彌賽亞。猶太人自己也同意這樣的解釋（《塔木德》.，247頁）。 在 啟 19:13–16裡，這位“用鐵杖轄管萬國的”被稱為“上帝的道”和“萬王之王。”見 啟 2:27 ；19:15 註釋。
**被提到上帝寶座那裡去了。**指耶穌基督的昇天（來 1:3；10:12）。為了達到預言的目的，異象省略了耶穌的生活、工作、受難、受死和復活，而只提到了昇天。
5.en:
**A man child.** Literally, “a son, a male.”
**Rule all nations.** An allusion to Ps. 2:8, 9, and clearly applicable to the Messiah. This application the Jews themselves recognized (Talmud Sukkah 52a, Soncino ed., p. 247). In Rev. 19:13–16 the being here described is identified as the “Word of God” and as “King of kings.” See on chs. 2:27; 19:15.
**Caught up.** A reference to the ascension of Jesus Christ (Heb. 1:3; 10:12). For the purpose of this prophecy the symbolism passes over completely the story of the life, work, suffering, death, and resurrection of Jesus. It mentions only the ascension.

12.zh:
所以，諸天和住在其中的，你們都快樂吧！只是地與海有禍了！因為魔鬼知道自己的時候不多，就氣忿忿的下到你們那裡去了。

**諸天和住在其中的，你們都快樂吧。**在天上有了歡樂，因為天使和其他世界的居民得知因基督在髑髏地的勝利，撒但註定要滅亡。
**有禍了。**因為教會將遭遇進一步的逼迫。因此信徒們還快樂不起來。
**不多。**oligos。指數量的“少”或時間的“短”。Oligos 的意義按上下文來確定。在耶穌讓四千人吃飽的故事裡，oligos 指“幾條小魚” ，與需要吃飽的龐大人數形成對比（太 15:34）。 找到永生之道的人是 “少” 的（oligos），與選擇滅亡之道的人形成對比（太7:14）。耶穌按手在“幾個”（oligos）病人身上，與本來也可以因信而得蒙醫治的人數形成對比（太ֹ 6:5）。
在《新約》中，Oligos 八次用來指時間。其中有五次是由該詞本身來表示的（可 6:31；雅 4:14；彼前 1:6；5:10；啟 17:10）。有三處是用oligos 所修飾的詞來表示的（徒 14:28；來 12:10；啟 12:12）。oligos 所表示的時間長度，取決於具體的情況。如可 6:31 裡的“歇一歇”可能只有幾天，或最多幾個星期。但 雅 4:14 oligos 卻是指人的一生。 啟 12:12 的 oligos 是指從撒但在耶穌釘十字架時被摔下到撒但對地上居民專權的結束。Oligos  所指的這段時間是與耶穌被釘十字架之前的四千年相對而言的。
表面上看，耶穌釘十字架以後撒但猖狂攻擊教會的這二千年時間很難稱為“不多”。即使同從亞當到十字架相比，它也算不上“不多。” 因此本節的“不多”應按《啟示錄》的整個進程，視基督復臨已近的背景來理解（見 啟 1:1 的註釋；參 啟 22:20）。耶穌既然快來了，撒但活動的時日就“不多”的了。見 啟 17:10 註釋。
**氣忿忿地.。**他生氣是因為自己的失敗。他沒有因罪而悲傷，反而在罪中越陷越深，他帶著更猛烈的惡毒去逼迫永生上帝的教會。參 彼前 5:8。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第46頁；《善惡之爭》第九章，623頁；《先祖與先知》第689頁；《證言》卷一第178，210頁；《證言》卷二第161頁；《證言》卷三第327，374，407頁；《證言》卷四第210頁；《證言》卷五第297，429，644頁；《證言》卷六第31頁；《證言》卷八第100頁；《證言》卷九第16頁；見啟16：13-16；詩17篇懷愛倫註釋。。
12.en:
**Rejoice, ye heavens.** There was rejoicing in heaven, for the angels and the inhabitants of other worlds knew Satan was doomed by Christ’s victory at Calvary.
**Woe.** For the church there was further persecution, hence its members could not yet rejoice.
**Great wrath.** He is angry because of his defeat. Rather than experience remorse and sorrow for evil, he plunges more and more deeply into iniquity. He goes forward with intensified and renewed malignity in his efforts to persecute the church of the living God. Compare 1 Peter 5:8.
**Short.** Gr. oligos, “few,” “small,” “little,” when used of number, quantity, or size; “short,” when used of time. Oligos is a relative term and describes that with which it is associated in terms of the context. Thus oligos describes the “few little fishes” in the narrative of the feeding of the 4,000 in comparison with the number that would be required to feed that multitude (Matt. 15:34). The number that find the way of life are “few” (oligos) compared with the number that choose the way of destruction (Matt. 7:14). Jesus laid His hands on a “few” (oligos) sick folks compared with the number who might have been healed had there not been such unbelief (Mark 6:5).
Oligos is used with reference to time in eight instances in the NT. In five of these instances the time element is implied in the word itself (Mark 6:31; James 4:14; 1 Peter 1:6; 5:10; Rev. 17:10) and the word is translated respectively “a while,” “little time,” “season,” “a while,” “short space.” In three instances the time element is expressed by a word modified by oligos (Acts 14:28, which reads literally, “not a little time”; Heb. 12:10; Rev. 12:12). The length of time expressed by oligos is dependent upon that with which it is compared. For example, the rest described in Mark 6:31 as lasting oligos probably continued only a few days, or at the most a few weeks. On the other hand, in James 4:14 oligos describes the life span of a man. In Rev. 12:12 oligos defines the period of time from the casting out of Satan at the time of the crucifixion of Christ to the end of Satan’s tyranny over the inhabitants of earth. This period of time is described as oligos in comparison with the more than 4,000 years preceding the crucifixion.
It may appear that the 2,000 years since the crucifixion, during which Satan has been actively at work against the church, is hardly a “short time” either absolutely or when compared with all the time from Adam to the cross. However, this expression should be understood against the background of the whole tenor of the book of Revelation, which presents the second coming of Christ as near (see on ch. 1:1; cf. ch. 22:20). If Jesus is coming “quickly,” then the time for Satan to work is “short.” See on ch. 17:10.

13.zh:
龍見自己被摔在地上，就逼迫那生男孩子的婦人。

**婦人。**見第1節註釋。龍既不能直接攻擊上帝的兒子，就企圖通過迫害男孩子的母親，就是教會來傷害祂（見第6節註釋）。
**男孩子。**見第5節註釋。
13.en:
**Woman.** See on v. 1. Being now unable to attack the Son of God directly, the dragon attempts to hurt the Son through the mother, by persecuting the mother of the man-child, the church (see on v. 6).
**Man child.** See on v. 5.

14.zh:
於是有大鷹的兩個翅膀賜給婦人，叫他能飛到曠野，到自己的地方，躲避那蛇；他在那裡被養活一載二載半載。

**兩個翅膀。**古代上帝子民十分熟悉鷹翅的表號。上帝拯救以色列人脫離法老和他的眾軍就是這個表號（出 19:4；申 32:11）。有人認為翅膀象徵教會被迫匆忙地尋找安全之所。
**被養活。**見 第 6 節註釋。
**一載二載半載。見。**第 6 節註釋。
14.en:
**Two wings.** The figure of eagle wings was familiar to God’s ancient people. The deliverance from Pharaoh and his hosts is referred to by this figure (Ex. 19:4; Deut. 32:11). Some see in these wings a symbol of the haste with which the church was obliged to find safety.
**Nourished.** See on v. 6.
**A time, and times.** See on v. 6.

15.zh:
蛇就在婦人身後，從口中吐出水來，像河一樣，要將婦人沖去。

**在。**詩 74:13 和 結 29:3中，龍是水生動物，因此水可能象徵毀滅。撒但不僅藉著迫害，也藉著假道來摧毀教會（見 啟 17:15 註釋）。
15.en: **Water as a flood.** In Ps. 74:13 and Eze. 29:3 a dragon is identified as a water animal, hence, probably the figure of water as a symbol of destruction. Satan sought to destroy the Christian church by the inundation of false doctrines as well as by persecution (cf. on Rev. 17:15).

16.zh:
地卻幫助婦人，開口吞了從龍口吐出來的水（原文作河）。

**地卻幫助婦人。**有人認為本節的“地”是指人煙稀少之處，與“水”相對。“水”有時象徵“多人，”“多民，”“多方”（啟 17:15）。他們指出，在宗教改革時期，歐洲和近東的人口眾多，而北美大陸卻人煙稀少。因此他們認為北美就是幫助歐洲受逼迫之教會的“地。” 西歐的新教國家曾是逼迫的避難所，也可以包括在“地”之內。還有人指出宗教改革本身就是破除背道教會誘惑的的主要因素。
**吞了。**就是讓毀滅的手段失效。
16.en:
**Earth helped the woman.** Some hold that “earth” here represents areas where there was a scarcity of peoples, in contrast with “waters,” which sometimes represent “peoples,” “nations,” and “tongues” (ch. 17:15). They point out that at the time of the Reformation there were multitudes of people in Europe and the Far East, but that the North American continent was very sparsely populated. Thus they point to this land as the “earth” which here brings relief to the persecuted church of the Old World. The Protestant lands of Western Europe, which became a haven from persecution, may also be included. Others point to the Protestant Reformation itself as the major factor in breaking the spell of the apostate church.
**Swallowed up.** That is, made ineffectual the devices of destruction.

900.zh:
《啟示錄》的語言和表號大多出自《舊約》（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷七， 725頁；參 賽 47:1 ；耶 25:12 ；賽 50:1 ；結 26:13 註釋；見啟 18 章補充註釋）。所以要正確地理解啟 12:17 “其餘的兒女”，就得查考該詞的對應詞在《舊約》中的用法。在希伯來文中通常有三個詞表示“其餘的”：（1）peletah（或palet，palatּ），“逃脫的”，源於動詞palat，“逃脫”，“拯救”。（2） sheÕerith （或 sheÕar），“其餘的”，“剩下的”。源於動詞 shaÕar  “剩下”，“留下”。（3）yether，“剩下的”，源於動詞yethar，“剩下”。下面是這些詞用來指上帝選民的例子：
1.	約瑟所照顧的雅各家成員被稱為“餘種，” （sheÕerith ，創45:7）。 這裡所強調的是蒙保守的事實。我們知道雅各的全家都得到了保守。
2.	在普遍背道的情況下，以利亞提出：“作耶和華先知的只剩下我一個人”（王上 18:22）。但是上帝宣告說：“我在以色列人中為自己留下（sha’ar）七千人，是未曾向巴力屈膝的 （王上 19:14，18；參 羅 11:4，5）。
3.	十個支派中有少數“脫離亞述王手的餘民”（peletah，代下30：6）留在了巴勒斯坦。而大多數人都被擄走了。到公元前 722 年，只“剩下（shaÕar） 猶大一個支派”（王下 17:18）代表整個民族。因此猶大就成為十二支派中的“餘民” （sheÕar），繼承了原先屬於所有十二支派的聖約的應許，特權和責任（賽 10:22；見《SDA聖經註釋》 卷 四，26–32頁）。
4.	幾年以後，亞述王西拿基立攻佔了耶路撒冷之外的猶大全地。因此耶路撒冷的居民被稱為“餘剩的民”（peletah）。他們是“猶大家所逃脫的人（sha’ar）”，要“往下紮根，向上結果，”並“從錫安山出來”作為上帝選民中“餘剩的民”（sheÕerith），為祂所指定拯救世界的工具（王下 19:4，30，31；賽 37:4，31，32；參 賽 4:2；10:20）。 上帝也定意“招回”那些被擄到亞述的以色列和猶大的人中“所餘剩的”（sheÕar），為他們預備一條“大道”，就像祂當初領他們的祖先從埃及地出來時一樣（賽 11:11，12，16）。
5.	一個世紀以後，當“巴比倫王”入侵巴勒斯坦時，也留下了（yether，在王下 25:22 中為shaÕar，參 啟 24:14）“剩下的民” （peletah，  在王下25：22中為sheÕar，結 14:22；參 耶 40:11；耶 42:2）。這些人要在圍困耶路撒冷時的刀劍，瘟疫和饑荒下“逃脫”（palat）和倖存下來 。但耶利米警告說，即使這些上帝希望“剩在” （shaÕar ）這地的“剩下的百姓” （yether ，參耶39:9），即“剩在耶路撒冷的餘民（shaÕar ），” 後來也會“在天下萬國中拋來拋去”（耶 24:8，9）。這些“剩下的百姓”，大多數人都逃到了埃及。然而耶利米警告說，凡“進入埃及地寄居的，就是所剩下的（sheÕerith ）猶大人，都不得逃脫，也不得存留歸回猶大地”（耶 44:14）。
6. 上帝應許在尼布甲尼撒所擄去的人中有“剩下”（yathar） “脫離刀劍的人，”在“所擄到的各國中記念” 祂的名（結 6:8，9）。 那些被擄的人中必有“餘剩的”（sheÕerith ，耶23:3；參 耶 31:7），最終將“從巴比倫之地逃避（palat）出來”（耶 50:28）。尼希米稱被擄迴歸之人為“剩下逃脫（peletah）的猶大人”和“被擄歸回剩下的人（peletah）（尼 1:2，3）。上帝將聖約的一切責任和應許都託付給了這些“餘剩的民” （sheÕerith ，亞8:12；參《SDA聖經註釋》 卷四，30–32頁）。但祂警告他們說，如果他們再違背上帝的誡命，祂就將滅絕他們，“以致沒有一個剩下（sheÕerith ）逃脫的人（peletah）”（拉 9:14）。
7. “其餘的”一詞，在許多情況下都出現在期盼彌賽亞國度的上下文之中（見 賽 4:2，3；11:11，16；參賽 11:1–9；耶 23:3；參 耶 23:4–6；彌 4:7；參 彌 4:1–8；5:7，8；參 彌 5:2–15；番 3:13）。
從上述經文和《舊約》其他經文的描述來看，“其餘的”是指一班以色列人。他們躲過了戰爭、被擄、瘟疫和饑荒等災難，蒙上帝憐憫，將上帝選民的血脈延續下來（創 45:7；斯 9:13；結 7:16）。聖經一再說這些“剩下的” 人數“極少”（耶 42:2；參 賽 10:22）。 當他們回想起真神並歸向祂時（代下 30:6；賽 10:20；結 6:8，9），就宣佈放棄虛假的宗教（王上 19:18），不再犯罪（番 3:13）。他們效忠上帝的誡命（拉 9:14），被稱為“聖，”並“在生命冊上記名”（賽 4:3）。他們重新接受了上帝永存之約的責任和特權，“向下紮根，… 向上結果”並“出去”到外邦宣揚上帝的榮耀（王下 19:30，31；賽 37:31，32；66:19）。
因此舊約聖經時代的餘民是指以色列各世代中上帝的選民。多數的人一再地背道，但總有一班忠心的餘民成為聖約應許，特權和責任的唯一繼承人。這約是當初是與亞伯拉罕訂立，後來又在西奈山確認的。這班餘民原是上帝所揀選的，要讓彌賽亞從他們中間出來，並藉著他們將福音傳到異教之地。他們不是由分散在各地的人組成的，不管他們有多忠心。他們乃是一個團體，是上帝在地上所設立的組織。還要注意“其餘的”在希伯來文中不表示最後的人或事物，除非這些“餘民”在他們各自的世代中是最後的一脈選民。照著上帝的恩典，從亞伯拉罕的時代起，世上一直有一班餘民存在著（參 羅 11:5）。
上帝警告那些從巴比倫迴歸之人，如果他們將來再悖逆祂，就沒有“剩下逃脫”的了（拉 9:14；參 申 19:20）。因此當猶太人拒絕彌賽亞，不再效忠聖約的時候（《歷代願望》737，738頁， 第 77 章），“上帝的國” 就從他們這個民族奪走，“賜給那能結果子的百姓” （太 21:43；參 彼前 2:9，10）。這就意味著永遠而不可逆轉地終止了他們這個民族在上帝面前的特殊地位，而將聖約的應許、特權和責任轉給了基督教會（見《SDA聖經註釋》 卷四32–36頁）。
保羅在 羅 9:27中說：“以色列雖多如海沙，得救的不過是剩下的餘數” （見 羅 9:27 註釋）。他在這裡把 賽 10:22 的“剩下的”用在他那個時代接受基督為彌賽亞的猶太人身上。但他們被稱為“餘民”是因為他們已成為基督教會的成員，而不是因他們是猶太人的緣故。保羅在 羅 11:5說這些猶太籍基督徒是“照著揀選的恩典 . . . 所留的餘數” 。在 羅 9-11 章中，保羅稱基督教會為永約應許、特權和責任的後嗣。因此基督教會是上帝所指定猶太民族的繼承人，受託保管上帝所啟示，是上帝旨意在地上有組織的代表，是祂為拯救人類而揀選傳福音的工具（見《SDA聖經註釋》 卷四35，36頁）。
除了 羅 9:27；11:5；啟 12:17 之外，《新約》其他地方的“其餘的” （太 22:6；啟 11:13；19:21）不是指上帝的子民。但在 啟 3:2 裡，“剩下的”源自 loipos ，與啟 12:17 中“其餘的兒女”相同。
基督昇天幾個世紀後，教會經歷了羅馬教的大背道。羅馬教的勢力壓制和驅趕上帝在地上的忠心代表達1260 年之久（見《但以理》第 7 章補充註釋；見 但 7:25 註釋；參 啟 12:6）。 通過 16 世紀的宗教改革（見 啟 12:15，16 註釋），上帝定意再領一班“其餘的兒女”離開奧秘的巴比倫。各新教團體成為上天所指定真理的傳報者，一點一點地恢復了救恩的榮耀福音。但這些團體相繼滿足於自己的那一點真理，未能在聖經的亮光中繼續進步。每當一班人拒絕前進時，上帝就興起另一班人來作為傳揚真理的工具。
最後，隨著羅馬教統治1260年的結束（見 啟 12:6，14 註釋）和“末時”的到來，天國最後的信息 （啟 14:6–12） 必須傳給萬民（見 但 7:25；11:35 註釋）。上帝就再次興起“其餘的兒女，” 就是 啟 12:17 （參 第 14–17 節） 所指的那批人。他們是那些曾遭受歷代以來龍的猛烈攻擊，特別是經歷過1260年，即“一載，二載，半載”黑暗、逼迫和謬道的上帝選民所傳承下來的“其餘的兒女”，是上帝最後的“其餘的兒女”，因為他們是祂所指定向世人發出最後呼籲，要他們接受救恩寶貴禮物的使者（啟 14:6–12）。
安息日復臨信徒從一開始就大膽宣揚 啟 14:6–12 三天使的信息為上帝要罪人接受基督的最後呼籲，並謙卑地相信他們的運動就代表這裡所說的“其餘的兒女。”目前還沒有其它宗教團體在宣告這個三重的信息，並符合啟 12:17 所列的特別條件。因此沒有其他團體能具備有效的聖經基礎來宣稱自己是啟 12:17 “其餘的兒女。”
但復臨信徒從來不認為只有他們才算是上帝的兒女，有進入天國的資格。他們相信所有誠心敬拜上帝，遵循已有的亮光而行的人，都可能成為 啟 12:17 所說“其餘的兒女”的最後團體。復臨信徒認為自己莊嚴的任務和快樂的特權是將上帝最後考驗人的真理清楚而雄辯地宣講出來，好叫所有上帝的兒女都被吸引加入預言中所說、預備迎接上帝大日的那一班人。
900.en:
Inasmuch as the language and imagery of the Revelation are drawn largely from the OT (see p. 725; cf. on Isa. 47:1; Jer. 25:12; Isa. 50:1; Eze. 26:13; see Additional Note on Rev. 18), a correct understanding of the word “remnant” as used in Rev. 12:17 calls for consideration of its Hebrew equivalents in the setting of OT usage. The three Hebrew words most commonly used for “remnant” are: (1) peleṭah (or paleṭ, paliṭ), “what escapes,” “those who escape,” from palaṭ, “to escape,” “to deliver”; (2) she’erith (or she’ar), “the rest,” “what remains,” “remainder,” “remnant,” and its verb form sha’ar, “to leave over,” “to be left over,” “to remain”; (3) yether, “what remains,” “remainder,” “remnant,” from yathar, “to leave over,” “to be left over.” Instances of the use of these words with respect to God’s chosen people may be classified as follows: 1. Members of Jacob’s family preserved under Joseph’s care in Egypt are spoken of as “as posterity,” literally, “a remnant” (she’erith; Gen. 45:7). Here, emphasis is upon the fact of preservation. So far as is known the entire family was preserved. 2. In the midst of general apostasy Elijah protested, “I, even I only, remain [yathar] a prophet of the Lord” (1 Kings 18:22), “I, even I only, am left,” but God declared, “I have left [sha’ar] me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal” (1 Kings 19:14, 18; cf. Rom. 11:4, 5). 3. A small “remnant” (peleṭah) of the ten tribes “escaped [sha’ar] out of the hand of the kings of Assyria,” who had led the vast majority of the nation into captivity, and remained in Palestine (2 Chron. 30:6). By 722 .. Judah alone was “left” (sha’ar) to function as a nation (2 Kings 17:18). Accordingly, it became the “remnant” (she’ar) of the twelve tribes and sole heir to the covenant promises, privileges, and responsibilities that originally belonged to all twelve (Isa. 10:22; see Vol. IV, pp. 26–32). 4. A few years later Sennacherib conquered all of Judah except Jerusalem, which, in turn, is spoken of as a “remnant.” This “remnant [peleṭah] that is escaped [sha’ar] of the house of Judah” was to “take root downward,” to “bear fruit upward,” and to “go forth” as the “remnant” (she’erith) of God’s chosen people, His appointed instrument for the salvation of the world (2 Kings 19:4, 30, 31; Isa. 37:4, 31, 32; cf. Isa. 4:2; 10:20). God also purposed to “recover” a “remnant” (she’ar) of the Israelites and Judahites that had gone captive into Assyria, and to prepare a “highway” for this “remnant [she’ar] of his people,” as He formerly had when their ancestors left the land of Egypt (Isa. 11:11, 12, 16). 5. When the “king of Babylon” invaded Palestine a century later, he too “left [yether; sha’ar in 2 Kings 25:22; cf. ch. 24:14] a remnant [peleṭah; she’ar in 2 Kings 25:22]” (Eze. 14:22; cf. Jer. 40:11; Jer. 42:2), which was to “escape” (palaṭ), that is, survive, the sword, pestilence, and famine that accompanied the siege of Jerusalem (Eze. 7:16). But Jeremiah warned that even some of this “remnant” (yether; ch. 39:9), or “residue [sha’ar] of Jerusalem,” that God desired should “remain [sha’ar] in this land,” would later be “removed into all the kingdoms of the earth” (ch. 24:8, 9). Most of this “remnant” fled to Egypt, but Jeremiah warned that “none of the remnant [she’erith] of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there,” should “escape [paliṭ] or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah” (ch. 44:14). 6. The Lord promised to “leave a remnant” (yathar) of those taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar, which would “escape the sword” and “remember” God in the lands of their captivity (Eze. 6:8, 9). A “remnant” (she’erith) of those in captivity (Jer. 23:3; cf. ch. 31:7) would eventually “escape [palat] out of the land of Babylon” (ch. 50:28). Nehemiah speaks of the returned captives as “the Jews that had escaped [peleṭah],” “the remnant [peleṭah] that are left [sha’ar] of the captivity” (ch. 1:2, 3). To this “remnant” (she’erith) God entrusted all the covenant responsibilities and promises (Zech. 8:12; cf. Vol. IV, pp. 30–32), but warned that if they should again break God’s commandments He would consume them, “so that there should be no remnant [she’erith] nor escaping [peleṭah]” (Ezra. 9:14). 7. Many references to the “remnant” occur in a context that clearly anticipates the Messianic kingdom (see Isa. 4:2, 3; 11:11, 16; cf. ch. 11:1–9; Jer. 23:3; cf. ch. 23:4–6; Micah 4:7; cf. ch. 4:1–8; 5:7, 8; cf. ch. 5:2–15; Zeph. 3:13).
A composite description of the “remnant” in these and other OT passages identifies the group thus designated as composed of Israelites who survived calamities such as war, captivity, pestilence, and famine, and who were spared in mercy to continue as God’s chosen people (Gen. 45:7; Ezra. 9:13; Eze. 7:16). Repeatedly, this “remnant” was “left [she’ar] but a few of [from] many” (Jer. 42:2; cf. Isa. 10:22). Remembering the true God and turning to Him (2 Chron. 30:6; Isa. 10:20; Eze. 6:8, 9), they renounced the authority of false religious systems (1 Kings 19:18) and refused to do iniquity (Zeph. 3:13). Loyal to God’s commandments (Ezra. 9:14), they were “called holy” and were “written among the living in Jerusalem” (Isa. 4:3). Accepting anew the responsibilities and privileges of God’s everlasting covenant, they “take root downward, … bear fruit upward,” and “go forth” to declare His glory among the Gentiles (2 Kings 19:30, 31; Isa. 37:31, 32; 66:19).
The “remnant” of OT times is thus composed of successive generations of Israelites—God’s chosen people. Again and again the majority apostatized, but each time there was a faithful “remnant” that became exclusive heirs to the sacred promises, privileges, and responsibilities of the covenant originally made with Abraham and confirmed at Sinai. This “remnant” was the formally appointed group to which God purposed to send the Messiah and through which He proposed to evangelize the heathen; it did not consist of scattered individuals as such, however faithful they might be, but was a corporate entity, God’s visible, divinely commissioned organization on earth. It should also be noted that the various Hebrew terms translated “remnant” do not connote the last of any thing or group of people, except in the sense that, in each instance, those who “remain” are temporarily, in their generation, the last existing link in the chosen line. Ever since the days of Abraham there has been “a remnant” according to God’s “grace” (cf. Rom. 11:5).
God warned those who returned from Babylonian captivity that there would be “no remnant nor escaping” should they again prove disloyal to Him (Ezra. 9:14; cf. Deut. 19:20). Accordingly, when the Jews rejected the Messiah and renounced their allegiance to the covenant (DA 737, 738), the “kingdom of God” was to be taken from them as a people and “given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof” (Matt. 21:43; cf. 1 Peter 2:9, 10). This meant the permanent, irrevocable cancellation of their special standing before God as a nation and the transfer of the promises, privileges, and responsibilities of the covenant relationship to the Christian church (see Vol. IV, pp. 32–36).
In Rom. 9:27 Paul declares that “though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, [only] a remnant [kataleimma] shall be saved” (see on Rom. 9:27). He is here applying the term “remnant” of Isa. 10:22 to Jews of his day who, as individuals, had accepted Christ as the Messiah. But it was as members of the Christian church, and no longer as Jews, that they had a right to this title. In Rom. 11:5 he speaks of these Christian Jews as “a remnant [leimma] according to … grace.” In chs. 9 to 11 Paul presents the Christian church as heir to the promises, privileges, and responsibilities of the everlasting covenant. Thus it is the divinely commissioned successor to Judaism as trustee of the revealed will of God, as the corporate representative of His purposes on earth, and as His chosen instrument for the proclamation of the gospel for the salvation of men (see Vol. IV, pp. 35, 36).
Aside from Rom. 9:27; 11:5; Rev. 12:17, the term “remnant” in the NT (Matt. 22:6; Rev. 11:13; 19:21) is not significant with respect to God’s people. In Rev. 3:2, however, the expression “which remain” is from loipos, the same word translated “remnant” in ch. 12:17.
A few centuries after Christ the church experienced the great papal apostasy. For some 1260 years papal power more or less effectively suppressed and scattered God’s true representatives on earth (see Additional Note on Dan. 7; see on Dan. 7:25; cf. Rev. 12:6). Through the Reformation of the 16th century (see on ch. 12:15, 16) God purposed once more to lead forth a “remnant,” this time from mystical Babylon. Various Protestant groups served as Heaven’s appointed harbingers of truth, point by point restoring the glorious gospel of salvation. But group after group became satisfied with its partial concept of truth and failed to advance as light from God’s Word increased. With each refusal to advance, God raised up another group as His chosen instrument for the proclamation of truth.
Finally, with the passing of the 1260 years of papal supremacy (see on ch. 12:6, 14) and the arrival of the “time of the end,” the time when Heaven’s last message (ch. 14:6–12) was to be proclaimed to the world (see on Dan. 7:25; 11:35), God raised up another “remnant,” the one designated in Rev. 12:17 (cf. vs. 14–17). This is the “remnant” of the long and worthy line of God’s chosen people that has survived the fierce onslaughts of the dragon down through history, most particularly the darkness, persecution, and error of the “time, and times, and half a time,” or 1260 “days” of vs. 6, 14. It is God’s last “remnant” by virtue of the fact that it is the appointed herald of His final appeal to the world to accept the gracious gift of salvation (ch. 14:6–12).
From the very first, Seventh-day Adventists have boldly proclaimed the three messages of ch. 14:6–12 as God’s last appeal to sinners to accept Christ, and have humbly believed their movement to be the one here designated as the “remnant.” No other religious body is proclaiming this composite message, and none other meets the specifications laid down in ch. 12:17. Hence none other has a valid, scriptural basis for claiming to be “the remnant” of v. 17.
However, Adventists repudiate emphatically and unequivocally any thought that they alone are children of God and have a claim upon heaven. They believe that all who worship God in full sincerity, that is, in terms of all the revealed will of God that they understand, are presently potential members of that final “remnant” company mentioned in ch. 12:17. Adventists believe that it is their solemn task and joyous privilege to make God’s last testing truths so clear and so persuasive as to draw all of God’s children into that prophetically foretold company that is making ready for the day of God.

5.en:
**Should not kill.** The punishment inflicted by the locusts is pain, not death.
**Five months.** For a discussion of this period see Additional Note at end of chapter.
**Scorpion.** See on v. 3. The sting of a scorpion may be exceedingly painful, but it is seldom fatal to man.

但不許蝗蟲害死他們，只叫他們受痛苦五個月。這痛苦就像蠍子螫人的痛苦一樣。

**不許蝗蟲害死他們。**蝗蟲所帶來的懲罰是痛苦，而不是死亡。
**五個月。**關於這段時期，見本章補充註釋。
**蠍子。**見 第 3 註釋。蠍子螫人是很痛的，但不致命。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–15節）**。《善惡之爭》第334頁。

14.en:
**Four angels.** Previously the prophet had seen four angels that had power to restrain the winds from blowing (ch. 7:1). They had worldwide power; the present four appear to be localized.
Most commentators who interpret the fifth trumpet as applying to the Saracens have seen the Turks in the sixth. Some of these identify the four angels as four sultanies of the Turkish (Ottoman) Empire, which they identify as Aleppo, Iconium, Damascus, and Baghdad. Others see in these angels the destructive forces that moved against the Western world.
**Are bound.** Literally, “have been bound.” These angels have been restrained from their work of judgment until the sixth angel sounds his trumpet.
**Euphrates.** Commentators who apply the sixth trumpet to the Turks generally give a literal interpretation to the Euphrates, in the sense that it was from the region of the Euphrates that the Turks entered the Byzantine Empire. But inasmuch as the names Sodom, Egypt (ch. 11:8), and Babylon (chs. 14:8; 17:5; 18:2, 10, 21) are used symbolically in the Revelation, other commentators hold that the Euphrates should also be understood symbolically (see on ch. 16:12). Some of these note that, to the Israelites, the Euphrates constituted the northern boundary of the land which ideally they were to occupy (Deut. 1:7, 8) and which, at the height of their power, they dominated, at least to some extent (see on 1 Kings 4:21). Beyond the Euphrates were the heathen nations of the north who repeatedly swept down and engulfed Israel (cf. on Jer. 1:14). According to this point of view the Euphrates here indicates a boundary beyond which God holds the forces that accomplish His judgment under the sixth trumpet.
Still others connect the Euphrates with mystical Babylon. They point out that inasmuch as later in the Revelation the final apostasy is portrayed as mystic Babylon (ch. 17:5) and that particular attention is called to its sitting “upon many waters” (v. 1), and inasmuch as historical Babylon was literally situated upon the waters of the Euphrates (see Vol. IV, p. 796), the Euphrates is here symbolic of the domain of the power represented as mystic Babylon (cf. on ch. 16:12).
14.zh:
吩咐那吹號的第六位天使，說：把那捆綁在伯拉大河的四個使者釋放了。

**四個使者。**先知曾看到四位天使執掌著四風（啟 7:1）。他們的能力是普世範圍的。而眼下的四個使者似乎只是地區性的。
將第五印解釋為指薩拉森人的解經家，多數認為第六印是指土耳其。他們中有人認為這四個使者是指土耳其奧斯曼帝國的四位蘇丹，即阿勒頗，以哥念，大馬士革和巴格達。也有人認為這些使者是指攻擊西方世界的毀滅性勢力。
**捆綁在。**這些使者懲罰的工作上受到了約束，直到第六位天使吹響了號筒。
**幼法拉底河。**那些認為第六號是指土耳其的解經家普遍認同這真是指幼發拉底河。因為土耳其人就是從幼發拉底河流域進入拜占庭帝國的。但是《啟示錄》中的所多瑪，埃及（啟 11:8）和巴比倫（啟 14:8；17:5；18:2，10，21）都是象徵性的地名，因此還有一些解經家認為應該按象徵意義來理解幼法拉底河（見 啟 16:12 註釋）。這些解經家認為，對於以色列人來說，幼法拉第河是他們應佔領地區的北界（申 1:7，8）。在以色列的鼎盛時期，他們的確也佔領了這裡的部分區域（見 王上 4:21 註釋）。幼發拉底河以外就是北方的異族。他們不斷南下吞噬以色列（參 耶 1:14 註釋）。根據這種觀點，幼發拉底河代表一條界限，是第六號筒下的懲罰勢力所不可以越過的。
還有人將幼發拉底河與奧秘的巴比倫連繫在一起。他們指出，《啟示錄》後面的章節把最後的大背道描寫為奧秘的巴比倫（啟 17:5），並強調她坐在“眾水上” （啟 17:1）。既然歷史上的巴比倫是建造在幼法拉底河畔的 （見《SDA聖經註釋》 卷 四，796頁），這裡的幼發拉底河也就象徵奧秘之巴比倫的勢力範圍（見 啟 16:12註釋）。

7.en:
**Shapes.** Gr. homoiōmata, “likeness.”
**Like unto horses.** See on Joel 2:4, of which this passage is reminiscent. Some see in the horses a reference to cavalry, a prominent feature of Arabian military forces.
**Crowns.** Gr. stephanoi, symbols of victory (see on ch. 2:10). Some see a reference here to the turban, which was long the national headdress of the Arabians.
**Faces of men.** Perhaps an implication that the agents of this visitation are human beings.
7.zh:
蝗蟲的形狀，好像預備出戰的馬一樣，頭上戴的好像金冠冕，臉面好像男人的臉面，

**形狀。**樣子。
**好像預備出戰的馬一樣。**見 珥 2:4 註釋。兩處的描寫相似。有人認為這是騎兵。騎兵是阿拉伯人的主要兵種。
**冠冕。**象徵勝利（見 啟 2:10 註釋）。 有人認為這是指阿拉伯人所常戴的頭巾。
**男人的臉面.。**可能暗示這次懲罰是藉著人來實施的。

1.en:
**Fifth angel.** The fifth trumpet is discussed in vs. 1–12. This trumpet is the first “woe” (see on ch. 8:13; cf. ch. 9:12, 13).
**A star fall.** Or, “a star fallen.” The star depicted here is not seen falling, as under the third trumpet (ch. 8:10), but is shown already fallen upon the earth.
It is interesting to note in passing that the figure of a fallen star occurs also in Jewish apocalyptic literature to describe Satan as a star fallen from heaven (Enoch 88:1; R. H. Charles, The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, vol. 2, p. 251).
**To him was given.** This implies that the power represented by the key was not intrinsically his, but was allowed to him by a higher power.
**The key.** Possession of the key implies the power to open and close (see Rev. 3:7; cf. Matt. 16:19).
A number of commentators have identified the fifth and sixth trumpets with the ravages of the Saracens and the Turks. They point to the wars between the Persians under Khosrau II (.. 590–628) and the Romans under Heraclius I (610–641) as weakening the two empires, thus preparing the way for the Moslem conquest. The key, they suggest, is the fall of Khosrau, whose overthrow and murder in .. 628 marked the end of the Persian Empire as an effective power and opened the way for the advance of the Arabian forces.
**Bottomless pit.** Gr. phrear tēs abussou, “pit of the bottomless [place],” or “well of the abyss.” The word abussos is used repeatedly in the LXX to translate the Hebrew tehom (see on Gen. 1:2, where abussos represents the primeval ocean). In Job 41:31 it represents the sea in general, and in Ps. 71:20, the depths of the earth. The abussos is also the abode of leviathan. Thus the LXX of Job 41:22, 23, 25 (vs. 31, 32, 34 of the Masoretic text) reads, “He [the dragon] makes the deep [abussos] boil like a brazen caldron; and he regards the sea as a pot of ointment, and the lowest part of the deep as a captive: he reckons the deep as his range. … He beholds every high thing: and he is king of all that are in the waters” (English trans. in Bagster’s ed. of the LXX). With respect to the Arabs, the bottomless pit may be thought of as representing the vast wastes of the Arabian deserts, whence these followers of Mohammed issued forth, to spread their conquests over vast areas.
1.zh:
第五位天使吹號，我就看見一個星從天落到地上，有無底坑的鑰匙賜給他。

**第五位天使。**第 1–12 節討論第五個號筒。這枝號筒是第一“禍” （見 啟 8:13 註釋；參 啟 9:12，13）。
**一個星從天落到地上。**希臘文直譯為“一個已經掉下來了的星。”這顆星不象第三號筒吹響之後的星那樣正在掉下來（啟 8:10），而是已經掉到地上了。
值得注意的是，猶太啟示文學也把撒但比作是從天上掉到地上的星 （《以諾書》 88:1，查爾斯《舊約次經和偽經》卷二，251頁）。
**有無底坑的鑰匙賜給他。**暗示鑰匙所代表的權力本不歸他所有，而是出於一個更高的權威。
**無底坑。**phrear teµs abussou。深井。七十士譯本經常把希伯來文的譯成tehom abussos（見 創 1:2 註釋。這裡 abussos 指創造前的海）。在 伯 41:31，它泛指海洋。在 詩 71:20 中，它指地的深處。abussos 還指大魚（Leviathan，中文譯為“鱷魚”）的住處。因此七十士譯本的伯41:22，23，25 （中文第 31，32，34 節）寫道：“它使深淵開滾如鍋，使洋海如鍋中的膏油。它行的路隨後發光，令人想深淵如同白髮。. . . 凡高大的，它無不藐視。它在驕傲的水族上作王。”無底坑用於阿拉伯人，可能指阿拉伯沙漠的大片的荒地。這是默罕默德的追隨者進行軍事擴張的發祥地。
**鑰匙。**鑰匙象徵開啟和關閉的的權力（見 啟 3:7；參 太 16:19）。
許多解經家認為第五和第六枝號筒所描寫的是薩拉森人和土耳其人的蹂躪。他們指出，霍斯羅夫二世（公元 590–628 年）所率波斯人與希拉剋略一世（公元 610–641 年）所率的羅馬人之間的戰爭，削弱了兩個帝國的力量，為穆斯林的征服鋪平了道路。他們認為，鑰匙代表霍斯羅夫克的失敗。他在公元 628年的被推翻和殺害，標誌著波斯帝國作為世界強國地位的結束，為阿拉伯勢力的擴張打開了門戶。

15.en:
**Four angels.** See on v. 14.
**For an hour.** Concerning the expression “for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year” see Additional Note at end of chapter; cf. on ch. 17:12.
**Third part.** See on ch. 8:7.
15.zh:
那四個使者就被釋放；他們原是預備好了，到某年某月某日某時，要殺人的三分之一。

**四個使者。**見 第 14 節註釋。
**某年某月某日某時。**見本章補充註釋；參 啟 17:12註釋。
**三分之一。**見 啟 8:7 註釋。

13.en:
**Sixth angel.** That is, the second woe (see on chs. 8:13; 11:14; cf. ch. 9:12).
**Four horns.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 10) between this and the reading “horns.” For the horns on the altar of incense in the ancient wilderness tabernacle see Ex. 37:26.
**The golden altar.** Doubtless the same altar as the one where the angel had ministered the prayers of the saints (ch. 8:3–5).
13.zh:
第六位天使吹號，我就聽見有聲音從神面前金壇的四角出來，

**第六位天使。**指第二樣災禍 （見 啟 8:13；11:14註釋；參 啟 9:12）。
**四角。**關於古代曠野會幕中香壇的角，見 出 37:26。
**金壇。**無疑指啟8:3-5中天使處理聖徒祈禱的那座壇。

21.en:
**Murders.** The sin of idolatry against God often leads to crimes such as those here listed (see Rev. 21:8; 22:15; cf. Gal. 5:20).
**Sorceries.** See on ch. 18:23.
**Fornication.** Gr. porneia, “prostitution,” “unchastity,” a general term denoting every imaginable kind of unlawful sexual intercourse.
**Thefts.** See 1 Cor. 6:10.
21.zh:
又不悔改他們那些兇殺、邪術、姦淫、偷竊的事。

**兇殺。**得罪上帝的拜偶像之罪往往導致下列的罪行（見 啟21:8；22:15；參 加 5:20）。
**邪術。**見 啟 18:23 註釋。
**姦淫。**泛指所有不正當的性行為。
**偷竊。**見 林前 6:10。

3.en:
**Locusts.** This visitation is reminiscent of the plague of locusts that infested Egypt (Ex. 10:13–15). As early as the 8th century .., Beatus, a Spanish monk, is said to have identified the symbol of the locusts with the Moslem Arabs, who in his day had just overrun North Africa, the Near East, and Spain. Since his time many expositors are on record as having made a similar identification.
**As the scorpions.** Normally locusts do not attack human beings, but these locusts are portrayed as having the venom of scorpions. Scorpions are described as hostile toward man (see Eze. 2:6; Luke 10:19; 11:12).
3.zh:
有蝗蟲從煙中出來，飛到地上；有能力賜給他們，好像地上蠍子的能力一樣，

**蝗蟲。**與從前埃及的蝗災相似（出 10:13–15）。 早在公元八世紀，西班牙修士比亞圖斯就認為蝗蟲是指阿拉伯穆斯林。當時他們剛剛蹂躪了北非，中東和西班牙。以後許多解經家都持相同的看法。
**好像地上的蠍子。**蝗蟲通常不攻擊人類，但這裡的蝗蟲卻有蠍子的毒液。聖經所描寫的蠍子是與人類為敵的（見 結 2:6；路 10:19；11:12）。

10.en:
**Like unto scorpions.** That is, like the tails of scorpions, which contain poisonous stings.
**Hurt men.** See on v. 5.
**Five months.** See Additional Note at end of chapter.
10.zh:
有尾巴像蠍子，尾巴上的毒鉤能傷人五個月。

**像蠍子。**象蠍子的尾巴。蠍子的尾巴上有毒刺。
**傷人。**見 第 5 節註釋。
**五個月。**見本章補充註釋。

16.en:
**Army of the horsemen.** The four angels are portrayed as wreaking their judgments by means of a great army of cavalry. In ancient times the cavalry was the swiftest, most mobile branch of an army. Therefore, here, it may be thought of as symbolizing the rapidity and scope with which this visitation comes.
**Two hundred thousand thousand.** That is, two hundred million. The number is doubtless symbolic of a vast, innumerable host.
**I heard.** The syntax of this statement in Greek may imply that John heard this number and understood its significance. Oral information confirmed his impression of a numberless throng.
16.zh:
馬軍有二萬萬；他們的數目我聽見了。

**馬軍。**這四位使者用強大的騎兵來實施懲罰。在古代，騎兵是行動最為迅速和機動的部隊。在這裡可能象徵這場懲罰的迅速和範圍之廣。
**二萬萬。**這個數字無疑象徵多得不可勝數。
**我聽見。**暗示約翰聽見了這個數字，也明白了它的含義。口信確認了數目之多。

2.en:
**Bottomless pit.** See on v. 1.
**Darkened.** Compare on ch. 6:12. Darkness is also a characteristic of the fifth plague (ch. 16:10). With respect to the Moslems, the darkening of the sun may be thought of as the obscuration of the sun of Christianity. Such was the effect of the spread of the religion of Islam.
2.zh:
他開了無底坑，便有煙從坑裡往上冒，好像大火爐的煙；日頭和天空都因這煙昏暗了。

**無底坑。**見 第 1 節註釋。
**昏暗了。**參 啟 6:12 註釋。黑暗也是第五災的特徵（啟 16:10）。如用於穆斯林，日頭昏暗可以理解為基督教日頭的昏暗。這是伊斯蘭教擴張的結果。

11.en:
**King over them.** The wise man Agur declared that “the locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands” (Prov. 30:27). The locusts in the present passage, however, are more highly organized in their destructive work, for they have a ruler whose commands they follow. Some who apply the fifth and sixth trumpets to the Moslem Arabs and Turks see in this king a reference to Osman (Othman) I (1299–1326), the traditional founder of the Ottoman Empire. His first attack upon the Greek Empire, which, according to Gibbon, took place on July 27, 1299, they take as marking the beginning of the five-month period of torment (Rev. 9:7, 10). For a discussion of this period see Additional Note at end of chapter.
**Angel.** Or, “messenger,” the one in charge of the forces issuing from the bottomless pit.
**Bottomless pit.** See on v. 1.
**Abaddon.** Gr. Abaddōn, a transliteration of the Heb. ’Abbadon, “destruction,” “ruin.” This word is used with a general meaning in Job 31:12, and is paralleled with “hell” (Heb. she’ol, the figurative realm of the dead; see on Prov. 15:11) in Job 26:6. The use of a Hebrew name here is significant with respect to the fact that much of John’s symbolism is of Hebrew and Jewish origin. In Jewish tradition ’Abbadon is personified (see Talmud Shabbath 89a).
**Greek tongue.** John supplies a Greek name that translates ’Abbadon for his Greek-speaking readers.
**Apollyon.** Gr. Apolluōn, “one who destroys,” “a destroyer.”
11.zh:
有無底坑的使者作他們的王，按著希伯來話，名叫亞巴頓，希利尼話，名叫亞玻倫。

**無底坑。**見 第 1 節註釋。
**使者。**負責管理從無底坑上來的勢力。
**做它們的王。**智者亞古珥說：“蝗蟲沒有君王，卻分隊而出” （箴 30:27）。但本節的蝗蟲，卻是組織嚴密地進行毀滅的工作，因為有王在指揮他們。一些相信第五和第六號筒是指阿拉伯穆斯林和土耳其人的人認為這個王就是奧斯曼一世（1299–1326）。他是奧斯曼帝國的締造者。根據吉本記載，他第一次襲擊希臘帝國是在 1229 年 7 月 27日。持上述觀點的人認為這是五個月痛苦的開始（啟 9:7，10）。關於這段時期，見本章補充註釋。
**亞巴頓。希臘文為Abaddoµn。**，譯自希伯來語Abbadon，意為“破壞，”“毀滅。” 該詞在伯 31:12中譯為“毀滅”；在 伯 26:6中指“陰間” （“陰間”的希伯來語是 sheÕol 。喻指死人的領域。見箴 15:11 註釋）。鑑於約翰的許多表號均來自希伯來和猶大，這裡使用希伯來的名字是有重要意義的。根據猶太的傳統， Abbadon 是擬人化的（見 《塔木德》Shabbath 89a）。
**希臘話。**約翰為他的希臘語讀者把亞巴頓譯為亞玻倫。
**亞玻倫。**希臘語為 Apolluoµn。意為“毀滅”和“毀滅者”。

8.en:
**Hair of women.** Some have applied this feature of the vision to the allegedly long hair worn by the Arabian troops.
**Teeth of lions.** This figure suggests strength and rapacity.
8.zh:
頭髮像女人的頭髮，牙齒像獅子的牙齒。

**頭髮像女人的頭髮。**有人認為這是指阿拉伯軍人的長髮。
**獅子的牙齒。**象徵力量和貪婪。

6.en: **Seek death.** Compare the attitude of men here with that portrayed in ch. 6:16. See Job 3:21; cf. Jer. 8:3.
6.zh:
在那些日子，人要求死，決不得死；願意死，死卻遠避他們。

**求死.。**把他們的意願與 啟 6:16 相對照。見 伯 3:21；參 耶 8:3。

4.en:
**They should not hurt.** Locusts destroy vegetation, not men. But these locusts are commanded not to harm any growing plant. Their attacks are to be directed only against unrighteous men.
Those who identify the locust symbol with the Saracens have suggested that this prohibition reflects the policy of the Arab conquerors not to destroy property wantonly or to kill Christians and Jews so long as they submitted to the payment of tribute. Concerning a certain class, Abu-bakr, Mohammed’s successor, is recorded to have said to his soldiers: “‘You will find another sort of people that belong to the synagogue of Satan, who have shaven crowns; be sure you cleave their skulls, and give them no quarter, till they either turn Mahometans or pay tribute’” (quoted in Edward Gibbon, The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, J. B. Bury, ed., vol. 5, p. 416). This class has not been definitely identified.
When applied to the Moslem Arabs this restriction may be thought of as representing their policy of permitting the conquered to live. This course was adopted so that the conquered might support the warriors out on conquest.
**Have not the seal.** Some have suggested that inasmuch as the keeping of the Sabbath is ultimately to be the outward sign of the inner work of sealing by the Holy Spirit (see on Eze. 9:4), the ones attacked by the “locusts” here are those who do not observe the true Sabbath.
**In their foreheads.** See Eze. 9:4; Rev. 7:3.
4.zh:
並且吩咐他們說，不可傷害地上的草和各樣青物，並一切樹木，惟獨要傷害額上沒有神印記的人。

**不可傷害。**蝗蟲所傷害的是植物，而不是人。但這裡的蝗蟲卻奉命不得傷害任何植物，只傷害不義之人。
那些認為蝗蟲是指薩拉森人的人說，這道禁令反映了阿拉伯征服者的政策。只要基督徒和猶太人願意納貢，他們就不任意傷人害物。史載穆罕默德的繼承人艾布伯克爾命令給他的士兵：“你們會發現另一等屬於撒但一會的人，剃著光頭；一定要把他們的頭顱劈開，不要饒恕他們，除非他們改信穆斯林都或納供”（引自 吉本《羅馬帝國的興衰》卷五，416頁）。但至今尚未確認這等人是誰。
用於阿拉伯穆斯林，這條禁令可以理解為代表他們保留被征服者性命的政策。這樣做是為了讓被征服者供養出徵的戰士。
**額上。**見 結 9:4；啟7:3。
**沒有上帝印記的。**有人認為遵守安息日既是證明聖靈在人內心工作的外在印記 （參 結 9:4），這裡的“蝗蟲”所攻擊的是那些沒有遵守真安息日的人。

9.en:
**Breastplates of iron.** The scales of the locusts may have suggested this description. The figure indicates the impregnability of the agents of this judgment.
**Sound of chariots.** Compare Joel 2:5.
9.zh:
胸前有甲，好像鐵甲。他們翅膀的聲音，好像許多車馬奔跑上陣的聲音。

**鐵甲。**蝗蟲身上的甲符合這一特徵。它可能指實施懲罰之人的勢不可當。
**車馬奔跑上陣的聲音。**參 珥 2:5。

20.en:
**Rest of the men.** The majority of men were not destroyed by this horrible visitation, but in spite of what their fellow men had suffered they did not take the lesson to heart as they should have done, and repent.
**Works of their hands.** Particularly the idols they had made (see Deut. 4:28; Ps. 135:15; Jer. 1:16). In modern days men who give to the structures of their own inventive genius greater importance in their lives than they do to God and His kingdom, stand equally condemned. While good in themselves, modern creature comforts—the works of men’s hands—may often fill men’s lives so fully that they become idols as much as the ancient gods of wood, stone, and metal ever were. Compare on 1 John 5:21.
**Devils.** Gr. daimonia, “demons” (see on 1 Cor. 10:20). This refers to the worship of spirits, common in ancient times and still widely practiced among many heathen groups.
**Idols.** As contrasted with the worship of spirits, this condemns the worship of concrete, but inanimate, objects.
**Gold.** Gold, silver, brass, stone, wood, are listed in the descending order of their value as materials.
**Neither can see.** The folly of idolatry is dramatized by the fact that these objects, worshiped as gods, have not even the common powers of an animal, much less a man (see Ps. 115:4–7; Jer. 10:5; Dan. 5:23).
20.zh:
其餘未曾被這些災所殺的人仍舊不悔改自己手所做的，還是去拜鬼魔和那些不能看、不能聽、不能走，金、銀、銅、木、石的偶像，

**其餘。**儘管有同胞被殺，大多數人還是沒有喪生於這場可怕的懲罰。他們沒有從中吸取應有的教訓，不思悔改。
**自己手所作的。**主要指他們所製作的偶像 （參 申 4:28；詩 135:15；耶 1:16）。 現代的人看重自己所發明的產品，勝過上帝和祂的國度。他們同樣要受到譴責。這些產品本身是好的，給人的生活帶來便利，但若過分注重，就成了他們的偶像，與古時用木頭、石頭或金屬製作的假神一樣。參 約壹 5:21 註釋。
**鬼魔。**見林前 10:20 註釋。神靈崇拜在古代十分普遍。在現代的許多異教群體中也很盛行。
**金、銀、銅、木、石的。**按材料的優劣排列。
**不能看、不能聽、不能走。**偶像崇拜的荒唐在於這些崇拜對象連動物的最基本能力都沒有，更不用說同人相比了（見 詩 115:4–7；耶 10:5；但 5:23）。
**偶像。**這裡所譴責的，除了崇拜鬼魔之外，還有崇拜有形而無生命的偶像。

12.zh:
第一樣災禍過去了，還有兩樣災禍要來。

**災禍。**見 啟 8:13 註釋。

17.zh:
我在異象中看見那些馬和騎馬的，騎馬的胸前有甲如火，與紫瑪瑙並硫磺。馬的頭好像獅子頭，有火、有煙、有硫磺從馬的口中出來。

**我。**. . . 看見。 這裡對馬和騎手的描寫似乎遵循了希伯來語逆向平行體的格式：先是馬，然後是騎馬的；再是騎馬的，最後是馬。
**如火。**不僅騎兵的盔甲看上去透亮，整個部隊在先知看來，也像是罩了一層火焰一般。參下面“紫瑪瑙”的註釋。
**紫瑪瑙。**紫色或深蘭色。有人認為這是指伴隨著火焰的煙雲（見下面“有火，有煙，有硫磺.”的註釋）。也有人認為這種顏色是指土耳其的軍服。土耳其軍服的顏色通常以紅（或猩紅色），藍色和黃色為主。他們認為火代表紅色，硫磺代表黃色。
**硫磺。**《啟示錄》經常將火和硫磺並列（啟9:18；14:10；19:20；20:10；21:8）。關這種顏色可能的意義，見前面“紫瑪瑙”的註釋。
**獅子頭。**把騎兵同森林之王相比，說明他們既神氣又殘暴。。
**有火，有煙，有硫磺。**騎兵身上所穿的，似乎也從馬口裡出來。本節的“紫瑪瑙”換成了“煙，”說明這兩個詞的意思是一樣的（參前面“紫瑪瑙”註釋）。參 伯 41:19–21 對大魚的描述。那些把第六號筒解釋為奧斯曼土耳其帝國橫行霸道的人認為，“有火，有煙，有硫磺”是指那時開始使用的火藥和火器。他們指出，騎在馬上的騎兵開火，從遠處看就像有火從馬口裡出來一樣。
17.en:
**I saw.** The description of the horses and their riders seems to follow the familiar Hebrew inverted parallelism: first the horses, then the riders are mentioned; then the riders are described, and finally the horses.
**Breastplates.** That is, of the riders.
**Of fire.** That is, fiery. Perhaps not only the armor of the cavalrymen appeared bright, but the troops themselves may have appeared to the prophet as clothed with fire. See below on “jacinth.”
**Jacinth.** Gr. huakinthinos, a violet or dark-blue color. Some suggest that this may represent the smoke accompanying the fire (see below on “fire and smoke and brimstone”). Others see the color as descriptive of the Turkish uniform, in which the colors red (or scarlet), blue, and yellow are said to have predominated. The fire, they believe, represents the red color, and the brimstone the yellow.
**Brimstone.** Gr. theiōdeis, “sulphurous,” “of brimstone.” Fire and brimstone are frequently mentioned together in the book of Revelation (chs. 9:18; 14:10; 19:20; 20:10; 21:8). For a possible significance of the color see the foregoing on “jacinth.”
**Heads of lions.** This comparison of the “horsemen” to the king of beasts suggests ferocity and majesty.
**Fire and smoke and brimstone.** The same things that appeared to clothe the cavalrymen also come forth from the mouths of their horses. The mention of “smoke” here in place of the “jacinth” of the horsemen strengthens the suggestion that the two are the same (see the foregoing on “jacinth”). Compare the description of leviathan in Job 41:19–21. Expositors who identify the sixth trumpet with the ravages of the Ottoman Turks see in the “fire and smoke and brimstone” a reference to the use of gunpowder and firearms, introduced about this time. They point out that the discharge of a musket by a mounted cavalryman could make it appear from a distance as if fire were coming out of the horse’s mouth.

18.zh:
口中所出來的火與煙並硫磺，這三樣災殺了人的三分之一。

**火，與煙並硫磺。**見 第 17 節註釋。
**這三樣災。**有人以稱懲罰為災作為根據，認為七號筒與最後的七災有密切的聯繫（見 啟 8:6註釋）。
**三分之一。**見 啟 8:7註釋。
18.en:
**These three.** Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the reading “these three plagues.” The fact that these judgments are called plagues is taken by some as suggesting that a close parallel exists between the trumpets and the seven last plagues (see on ch. 8:6).
**Third part.** See on ch. 8:7.
**Fire … smoke … brimstone.** See on v. 17.

19.zh:
這馬的能力是在口裡和尾巴上；因這尾巴像蛇，並且有頭用以害人。

**口裡。**約翰前面說到這些馬用口中出來的火，煙和硫磺殺人（見 第 17 節註釋）。
**尾巴。**這些馬的頭和尾巴都能實施破壞。參照第五個號筒的蝗蟲，也是用尾巴蟄人的（第 10 節）。 有些註釋家認為“尾巴”是指土耳其的軍旗。
19.en:
**Mouth.** John has already depicted these horses as killing men by the fire, smoke, and brimstone that issue from their mouths (see on v. 17).
**Tails.** These horses wreak havoc both with their heads and with their tails. Compare the locusts of the fifth trumpet, whose stings were in their tails (v. 10). With respect to the Turks, certain expositors see in these “tails” a reference to a horse’s tail as a Turkish standard.

900.zh:
據好史料記載，瑞士改革家布林格（逝於 1575）最早把第六號筒所描寫的勢力解釋成土耳其的註釋家之一。然而馬丁路德早就認定第五號筒代表穆斯林。關於第六號筒和第五號筒的時間，解經家們存在很大的分歧。但絕大多數註釋家認同第五號筒是在薩拉森人的鼎盛時期，第六號筒是在土耳其的塞爾柱時期或奧斯曼時期。
1832 年，威廉米勒耳用一種新的方法來確定這些號筒的年代，將它們按照時間順序聯繫起來。他的觀點發表在刊於《佛蒙特電訊報》系列文章的第五篇中。米勒耳根據一日頂一年的原則（見 但 7:25 註釋），推算出第五號筒裡的五個月（啟9:5）為150年，而第六號筒中的“某年某月某日某時”（即“一年，一月，一日，一時”為 391 年零 15 天。許多米勒耳以前的解經家也採用了這種計算的方法，但沒有把兩個時期連起來。米勒耳提出，第六號筒的時期緊接著第五號筒的時期，加起來共 541 年零 15 天。他推定這段時期是從公元 1298 年開始的。他認為那一年奧斯曼土耳其帝國首次對拜占庭帝國發動攻擊。這段時期的終點是 1839 年。因此，根據他的觀點，第五第六號筒都是指奧斯曼土耳其帝國。第五號筒講的是它的興起，第六號筒講的是它的稱霸。
1838 年，米勒耳在美國復臨運動的一個助手約西亞.利奇，對米勒耳的日期進行了修訂，認定到從 1299 年到 1449 年是第五號筒時期；從 1449 年到 1840 年是第六號筒時期。利奇認為 1299年7月27日在尼科美狄亞附近的巴復萌戰役是奧斯曼土耳其帝國首次攻打拜占庭帝國。。他認為公元 1449 年對於拜占庭帝國的崩潰是一個很重要的年份。因為在 1448年底，拜占庭的皇帝帕里奧洛加斯在請示了土耳其蘇丹穆拉德二世之後，才膽敢登上王位。事實是他在得到蘇丹的批准之後，才於公元 1449 年1月6日加冕的。利奇認為這150年就是奧斯曼土耳其人讓拜占庭帝國“受痛苦”的時期（參 第 5 節）。
如上所述，利奇把公元 1299 年作為第五號筒的開始。更準確地說，是1229年7月27日，即他為巴復萌戰役定所定的日期。他認為第五號筒的時間是150年，到公元1449年的7月27日結束。這一天就是第六號筒的開始。再加上 391 年，就到了1840年的7月27日。再加15天就是那年的8月。於是他預言土耳其帝國的勢力將在1840年8月被推翻。開始時他並沒有確定是8月幾號。但在這段時期將近結束時，他宣佈土耳其帝國將在8月11日崩潰，剛好是1840年7月27日加上15天。
那時，世界的注意力都集中在土耳其帝國所發生的事上。1839年6月，埃及的帕夏、蘇丹名義上的附庸穆罕默德.阿里背叛了他的宗主。他擊敗了土耳其人，俘虜了他們的海軍。這時蘇丹馬哈茂德二世去世了。他的繼位者阿卜杜拉的大臣們建議與穆罕穆德阿里簽訂協議，讓阿里獲得世襲埃及的權利，讓他的兒子易卜拉欣統治敘利亞。但這時對中東虎視眈眈的英國，法國，奧地利，普魯士和俄國出來干涉了。他們說，未經他們同意，土耳其與默罕默德阿里之間不得簽署任何協議。談判一直拖到1840年夏天。7月15日，英國，奧地利，普魯士和俄國同時簽署了倫敦條約，建議用武力來保障前一年土耳其所提出之條款的實施。大約在這時，利奇宣佈土耳其的勢力將在8月11日結束。就在那一天，土耳其的使節裡法特.貝帶著倫敦條約來到亞歷山大。也是在這一天，四個大國的大使收到了蘇丹的書信，徵詢他們的意見，希望知道當他的帝國處於危急情形時應該採取什麼措施。得到的回答是：“已經有所準備。”但他卻不知道是什麼樣的準備。利奇將這些事件解釋為土耳其政府已經喪失了獨立。
這些事件正好發生在利奇所預言的時間裡，對美國關心復臨運動之人的思想造成深遠的影響。利奇的這個預言增強了人們對復臨運動所宣講其他尚未應驗之預言的信任，特別是2300日的預言。1840年所發生的這件事對人們期盼基督在三年之後復臨產生重大的影響（見 《善惡之爭》334，335頁，第 18 章）。
但必須指出，解經家和神學家對於第五號筒和第六號筒的意義存在很大的分歧。主要原因有三個方面。一，表號的本身含義；二，希臘原文的意思；三，所涉及的歷史事件和日期。但本書篇幅有限，無法深入探討這些問題。
安息日復臨信徒一般贊同利奇對第五和第六號筒的解釋，特別是所涉及的時間問題。
900.en:
One of the first Biblical expositors on record to identify the Turks as the power portrayed under the sixth trumpet was the Swiss reformer, Heinrich Bullinger (d. .. 1575), although Martin Luther had already set forth this trumpet as symbolic of Moslems.
